title.zh: '''卷二百一十六上''' 列傳第一百四十一上 吐蕃上

meta.sourceNote: Body created from Wikisource raw text because the ChineseNotes scrape produced a zero-byte file.

sentences.zh: ◎吐蕃上

translations.literal: ◎ Tibet (Part One)
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Tibet (Part One)

sentences.zh: 吐蕃本西羌屬，蓋百有五十種，散處河、湟、江、岷間，有發羌、唐旄等，然未始與中國通。

translations.literal: The Tibetans were originally of the Western Qiang affiliation; there were about one hundred and fifty clans, scattered between the Yellow River, Huangshui, Yangtze, and Min rivers, including the Fa Qiang and Tangmao, yet they had never had contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans sprang from the western Qiang peoples. Some hundred and fifty clans lived scattered along the Yellow River, the Huangshui, the Yangtze, and the Min—among them the Fa Qiang and the Tangmao—but they had never yet dealt with the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 居析支水西。

translations.literal: They dwelt west of the Qizhi River.
translations.idiomatic: They settled west of the Qizhi River.

sentences.zh: 祖曰鶻提勃悉野，健武多智，稍並諸羌，據其地。

translations.literal: Their ancestor was called Nutiboxiye; strong and martial, full of wisdom, he gradually annexed the various Qiang and seized their territory.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor named Nutiboxiye, vigorous in arms and shrewd in counsel, gradually brought the Qiang clans under his sway and took possession of their lands.

sentences.zh: 蕃、發聲近，故其子孫曰吐蕃，而姓勃窣野。

translations.literal: The sounds of Fan and Fa were close, so their descendants were called Tubo, and their surname was Boxiye.
translations.idiomatic: Because the words for "Fan" and "Fa" sounded alike, their descendants came to be called the Tibetans (Tubo), and they took the clan name Boxiye.

sentences.zh: 或曰南涼禿發利鹿孤之後。

translations.literal: Some say they were descendants of Tufa Lilugu of Southern Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that they were descended from Tufa Lilugu of Southern Liang.

sentences.zh: 二子，曰樊尼，曰傉檀。

translations.literal: He had two sons, named Fanni and Nutan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Fanni and Nutan.

sentences.zh: 傉檀嗣，為乞佛熾盤所滅。

translations.literal: Nutan succeeded him and was destroyed by Qifo Chiban.
translations.idiomatic: Nutan succeeded to the rule but was overthrown and destroyed by Qifo Chiban.

sentences.zh: 樊尼挈殘部臣沮渠蒙遜，以為臨松太守。

translations.literal: Fanni took the remnant tribes and submitted to Juqu Mengxun, who made him Administrator of Linsong.
translations.idiomatic: Fanni led the surviving tribes to submit to Juqu Mengxun, who appointed him Administrator of Linsong.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜滅，樊尼率兵西濟河，逾積石，遂撫有群羌云。

translations.literal: When Mengxun perished, Fanni led his troops west across the river, passed beyond Jishi, and thus brought the various Qiang under his rule.
translations.idiomatic: After Mengxun's fall, Fanni marched west across the river, crossed beyond Jishi Mountain, and in time brought the Qiang peoples under his control.

sentences.zh: 其俗謂強雄曰贊，丈夫曰普，故號君長曰贊普，贊普妻曰末蒙。

translations.literal: In their custom the powerful and valiant were called zan, and a man was called pu; therefore the ruler was styled Zanpu, and the Zanpu's wife was called Momo.
translations.idiomatic: By their custom the mighty were called zan and a man pu; hence their chieftain was titled Zanpu, and the Zanpu's consort Momo.

sentences.zh: 其官有大相曰論茝，副相曰論茝扈莽，各一人，亦號大論、小論；

translations.literal: Among their offices there was a great minister called Lunzhi and a deputy minister called Lunzhi Humang, one of each, also styled Great Lun and Lesser Lun;
translations.idiomatic: Their chief minister was called Lunzhi and his deputy Lunzhi Humang, one of each—also known as the Great Lun and the Lesser Lun;

sentences.zh: 都護一人，曰悉編掣逋；

translations.literal: there was one protector-general called Xibian Chibo;
translations.idiomatic: a single protector-general titled Xibian Chibo;

sentences.zh: 又有內大相曰曩論掣逋，亦曰論莽熱，副相曰曩論覓零逋，小相曰曩論充，各一人；

translations.literal: there were also an inner great minister called Nanglun Chibo, also called Lun Mangre, a deputy called Nanglun Milengbo, and a lesser minister called Nanglun Chong, one of each;
translations.idiomatic: an inner great minister, Nanglun Chibo (also Lun Mangre), with a deputy Nanglun Milengbo and a junior minister Nanglun Chong, again one apiece;

sentences.zh: 又有整事大相曰喻寒波掣逋，副整事曰喻寒覓零逋，小整事曰喻寒波充：皆任國事，總號曰尚論掣逋突瞿。

translations.literal: there were also a great minister for administration of affairs called Yuhanbo Chibo, a deputy called Yuhan Milengbo, and a junior called Yuhanbo Chong: all held state affairs, and collectively they were called Shanglun Chibo Tuqu.
translations.idiomatic: and ministers of state business titled Yuhanbo Chibo, Yuhan Milengbo, and Yuhanbo Chong—all charged with government, together styled the Shanglun Chibo Tuqu.

sentences.zh: 地直京師西八千里，距鄯善五百里，勝兵數十萬。

translations.literal: Their land lay eight thousand li due west of the capital, five hundred li from Shanshan, with several hundred thousand effectives.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory lay eight thousand li west of the capital, five hundred li from Shanshan, and they could field several hundred thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 國多霆、電、風、雹，積雪，盛夏如中國春時，山谷常冰。

translations.literal: The country had much thunder, lightning, wind, and hail, with accumulated snow; in high summer it was like spring in China, yet the valleys were perpetually frozen.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder, lightning, gales, and hail were common; snow lay deep, and even at midsummer the air felt like spring in China—yet ice lingered in the valleys.

sentences.zh: 地有寒癘，中人輒痞促而不害。

translations.literal: The land had cold miasma; those stricken would gasp and feel tightness in the chest but were not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Cold miasmas haunted the region; those who fell ill would grow short of breath and feel constricted in the chest, yet the sickness was not fatal.

sentences.zh: 其贊普居跋布川，或邏娑川，有城郭廬舍不肯處，聯毳帳以居，號大拂廬，容數百人。

translations.literal: The Zanpu dwelt on the Babu River, or the Luosa River; though there were walled towns and houses he would not stay in them, but joined felt tents to live in, called the Great Fulü, holding several hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: The Zanpu lived along the Babu or Luosa River. Though walled towns and houses stood ready, he refused them, linking felt tents into a great encampment called the Great Fulü, large enough for several hundred people.

sentences.zh: 其衛候嚴，而牙甚隘。

translations.literal: His guard and watch were strict, yet the encampment was very narrow.
translations.idiomatic: His guard was strict, but the royal camp itself was cramped.

sentences.zh: 部人處小拂廬，多老壽至百餘歲者。

translations.literal: The tribesmen dwelt in lesser fulü; many lived to great age, even over a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in smaller tent compounds; many reached great age, some living more than a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 衣率氈韋，以赭塗面為好。

translations.literal: They generally wore felt and leather garments, and considered it fine to paint the face with ochre.
translations.idiomatic: They commonly dressed in felt and hides, and prized painting the face with red ochre.

sentences.zh: 婦人辮發而縈之。

translations.literal: Women braided their hair and wound it about the head.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore their hair in braids wound about the head.

sentences.zh: 其器屈木而韋底，或氈為般，凝面為碗，實羹酪並食之，手捧酒漿以飲。

translations.literal: Their vessels were bent wood with leather bases, or felt for plates; curdled milk for bowls; they filled them with broth and curds and ate together, cupping wine in their hands to drink.
translations.idiomatic: They bent wood for bowls with leather bases, or used felt for plates and clotted curd for bowls; broth and dairy were served together, and they drank wine from cupped hands.

sentences.zh: 其官之章飾，最上瑟瑟，金次之，金塗銀又次之，銀次之，最下至銅止，差大小，綴臂前以辨貴賤。

translations.literal: For insignia of office the highest was turquoise, next gold, then gilt silver, then silver, and lowest only copper; they differed in size and were fastened before the arm to distinguish noble from base.
translations.idiomatic: Official insignia ranked from turquoise at the top, then gold, gilt silver, plain silver, and finally copper; size varied, and badges were worn on the forearm to mark rank.

sentences.zh: 屋皆平上，高至數丈。

translations.literal: Houses all had flat roofs, rising to several zhang in height.
translations.idiomatic: Their houses had flat roofs and stood several zhang high.

sentences.zh: 其稼有小麥、青稞麥、蕎麥、荳豆。

translations.literal: Their crops included wheat, highland barley, buckwheat, and beans.
translations.idiomatic: They grew wheat, highland barley, buckwheat, and legumes.

sentences.zh: 其獸，牦牛、名馬、犬、羊、彘，天鼠之皮可為裘，獨峰駝日馳千里。

translations.literal: Their animals included yak, fine horses, dogs, sheep, and swine; the skin of the "heaven rat" could be made into fur coats, and the single-humped camel could run a thousand li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Among their beasts were yaks, fine horses, dogs, sheep, and swine; the pika's pelt served for furs, and the dromedary could cover a thousand li in a day.

sentences.zh: 其寶，金、銀、錫、銅。

translations.literal: Their treasures were gold, silver, tin, and copper.
translations.idiomatic: Their mineral wealth included gold, silver, tin, and copper.

sentences.zh: 其死，葬為冢，塈塗之。

translations.literal: At death they were buried in mounds and plastered over.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were buried in earthen mounds and sealed with plaster.

sentences.zh: 其吏治，無文字，結繩齒木為約。

translations.literal: In administration they had no writing, but made agreements by knotted cords and notched wood.
translations.idiomatic: They kept no written records in government; contracts were made with knotted cords and notched tally sticks.

sentences.zh: 其刑，雖小罪必抉目，或刖、劓，以皮為鞭抶之，從喜怒，無常算。

translations.literal: In punishment, even for minor crimes they gouged out eyes, or amputated or cut off the nose; they beat with leather whips according to pleasure or anger, with no fixed measure.
translations.idiomatic: Even petty offenses might cost an eye, a limb, or the nose; leather whips were applied at the ruler's whim, with no fixed penalty.

sentences.zh: 其獄，窟地深數丈，內囚於中，二三歲乃出。

translations.literal: Their prisons were pits dug several zhang deep; prisoners were shut within and released only after two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons were pits dug many zhang deep; inmates were cast inside and might not emerge for two or three years.

sentences.zh: 其宴大賓客，必驅耗牛，使客自射，乃敢饋。

translations.literal: When entertaining great guests they always drove out a yak and made the guest shoot it himself before they dared serve food.
translations.idiomatic: When feasting honored guests they drove out a yak and required the guest to kill it with his own shot before food was served.

sentences.zh: 其俗，重鬼右巫，事原羝為大神。

translations.literal: In custom they valued spirits and favored shamans, worshipping Yuandi as the great god.
translations.idiomatic: They revered spirits and trusted shamans, holding Yuandi as their chief deity.

sentences.zh: 喜浮屠法，習咒詛，國之政事，必以桑門參決。

translations.literal: They delighted in Buddhist law, practiced incantations and curses, and state affairs had to be decided with monks participating.
translations.idiomatic: They favored Buddhism, practiced charms and curses, and no state business was settled without monks taking part.

sentences.zh: 多佩弓刀。

translations.literal: Many wore bow and knife at the belt.
translations.idiomatic: Most men went armed with bow and blade.

sentences.zh: 飲酒不得及亂。

translations.literal: In drinking wine one must not reach disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Drunken disorder was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 婦人無及政。

translations.literal: Women did not participate in government.
translations.idiomatic: Women took no part in public affairs.

sentences.zh: 貴壯賤弱，母拜子，子倨父，出入前少而後老。

translations.literal: They honored the strong and despised the weak; mothers bowed to sons, sons were haughty toward fathers; in going out and in, the young went first and the old behind.
translations.idiomatic: Strength was prized and weakness scorned; mothers bowed to sons and sons showed little deference to fathers; the young went ahead and the aged followed when people passed in or out.

sentences.zh: 重兵死，以累世戰沒為甲門，敗懦者垂狐尾於首示辱，不得列於人。

translations.literal: They valued death in battle; families with generations fallen in war were first-class houses; cowards hung fox tails from the head in disgrace and could not rank among others.
translations.idiomatic: Death in war was honored; clans with generations of fallen soldiers ranked as elite houses. Cowards wore fox tails on the head in shame and were shut out of respectable company.

sentences.zh: 拜必手據地為犬號，再揖身止。

translations.literal: In bowing they must press hands to the ground and bark like dogs, bow twice, then straighten the body and stop.
translations.idiomatic: To bow they pressed their hands to the earth and gave a doglike cry, bowed twice, then rose and stopped.

sentences.zh: 居父母喪，斷髮、黛面、墨衣，既葬而吉。

translations.literal: In mourning for parents they cut the hair, blackened the face, wore dark garments, and after burial considered it auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: For parents' mourning they cut their hair, blackened their faces, and wore dark clothes; once the burial was done they regarded the rites as complete.

sentences.zh: 其舉兵，以七寸金箭為契。

translations.literal: When raising troops they used a seven-inch golden arrow as the token of covenant.
translations.idiomatic: To mobilize for war they passed a seven-inch golden arrow as the pledge of alliance.

sentences.zh: 百里一驛，有急兵，驛人臆前加銀鶻，甚急，鶻益多。

translations.literal: Every hundred li there was a post station; when there was urgent military business the courier added silver hawks on the breast—the more urgent, the more hawks.
translations.idiomatic: Post stations stood every hundred li; urgent dispatches were marked with silver hawk badges on the courier's chest—the greater the urgency, the more hawks.

sentences.zh: 告寇舉烽。

translations.literal: To report raiders they raised beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy raids were signaled with beacon fires.

sentences.zh: 其畜牧，逐水草無常所。

translations.literal: In herding they followed grass and water with no fixed abode.
translations.idiomatic: Herdsmen followed pasture and water and had no fixed dwelling.

sentences.zh: 其鎧胃精良，衣之周身，竅兩目，勁弓利刃不能甚傷。

translations.literal: Their armor was finely made; worn over the whole body with only the two eyes pierced, strong bows and sharp blades could not greatly harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Their armor was excellent—worn over the entire body with only slits for the eyes—so that even powerful bows and keen blades inflicted little harm.

sentences.zh: 其兵法嚴，而師無饋糧，以鹵獲為資。

translations.literal: Their military law was strict, yet armies carried no provision grain and relied on plunder for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Military discipline was harsh, but armies carried no grain trains and lived on booty.

sentences.zh: 每戰，前隊盡死，後隊乃進。

translations.literal: In every battle the front rank had to die completely before the rear rank advanced.
translations.idiomatic: In battle the front rank had to be cut down to the last man before the rear rank moved forward.

sentences.zh: 其四時，以麥熟為歲首。

translations.literal: Their seasons took the ripening of wheat as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Their year began when the wheat ripened.

sentences.zh: 其戲，棋、六博。

translations.literal: Their games were chess and liubo.
translations.idiomatic: They played chess and liubo for pastime.

sentences.zh: 其樂，吹螺、擊鼓。

translations.literal: Their music was blowing conches and striking drums.
translations.idiomatic: Music was made with conch horns and drums.

sentences.zh: 其君臣自為友，五六人曰共命。

translations.literal: Lord and ministers made friends of one another; five or six men were called "shared life."
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers bound themselves as sworn companions; groups of five or six were called "shared fate."

sentences.zh: 君死，皆自殺以殉，所服玩乘馬皆瘞，起大屋冢顛，樹眾木為祠所。

translations.literal: When the lord died, all killed themselves to follow in death; garments, ornaments, and riding horses were all buried; a great house was raised atop the tomb mound and many trees planted as a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When the lord died his companions took their own lives to follow him; clothes, treasures, and horses were buried with him; a great hall was built atop the tomb and many trees planted for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 贊普與其臣歲一小盟，用羊、犬、猴為牲；

translations.literal: The Zanpu and his ministers made a small covenant each year, using sheep, dogs, and monkeys as victims;
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Zanpu and his ministers swore a lesser oath with sheep, dogs, and monkeys as offerings;

sentences.zh: 三歲一大盟，夜肴諸壇，用人、馬、牛、閭為牲。

translations.literal: every three years a great covenant, at night feasting at the altars, using men, horses, cattle, and lü as victims.
translations.idiomatic: every three years a great oath by night at the altars, with human beings, horses, cattle, and lü beasts as sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 凡牲必折足裂腸陳於前，使巫告神曰：「渝盟者有如牲。」

translations.literal: All victims had to have legs broken and entrails split and displayed before them; shamans were made to tell the spirits: "Whoever breaks the covenant shall be like this victim."
translations.idiomatic: Victims were always displayed with broken legs and torn bellies; shamans proclaimed to the gods, "Whoever breaks this oath shall fare as this victim."

sentences.zh: 其後有君長曰瘕悉董摩，董摩生佗土度，佗土生揭利失若，揭利生勃弄若，勃弄生詎素若，詎素生論贊索，論贊生棄宗弄贊，亦名棄蘇農，亦號弗夜氏。

translations.literal: Later there was a lord called Jiaxi Dongmo; Dongmo begot Tuotudu, Tuotudu begot Jielishiruo, Jieli begot Bonongruo, Bonong begot Jusuruo, Jusu begot Lunzansuo, Lunzan begot Qizong Nongzan, also named Qisunong, also styled the Fuye clan.
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers included Jiaxi Dongmo; from him came Tuotudu, then Jielishiruo, Bonongruo, Jusuruo, Lunzansuo, and finally Qizong Nongzan—also called Qisunong and known as the Fuye clan.

sentences.zh: 其為人慷慨才雄，常驅野馬、犛牛，馳刺之以為樂，西域諸國共臣之。

translations.literal: He was by nature generous and talented and heroic; he often drove wild horses and yaks and galloped to spear them for amusement; the states of the Western Regions all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed, gifted, and bold, and took his pleasure in driving wild horses and yaks to gallop and spear them; the kingdoms of the Western Regions all acknowledged his rule.

sentences.zh: 太宗，始遣使者來朝，帝遣行人馮德遐下書臨撫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Taizong they first sent envoys to court; the Emperor dispatched the messenger Feng Dexia to deliver a letter and extend imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong they first sent envoys to court, and the emperor dispatched the envoy Feng Dexia with an imperial letter of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 弄贊聞突厥、吐谷渾並得尚公主，乃遣使賫幣求昏，帝不許。

translations.literal: Nongzan heard that both the Turks and the Tuyuhun had been given imperial princesses in marriage, so he sent envoys bearing gifts to request a marriage alliance; the Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that both the Turks and the Tuyuhun had received Tang princesses, Nongzan sent envoys with gifts to seek a marriage alliance, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 使者還，妄語曰：「天子遇我厚，幾得公主，會吐谷渾王入朝，遂不許，殆有以間我乎？」

translations.literal: When the envoys returned they spoke falsely, saying: "The Son of Heaven treated us generously and we nearly obtained a princess, but just as the king of Tuyuhun came to court it was not granted—could someone have set us at odds?"
translations.idiomatic: On their return the envoys lied, saying, "The Son of Heaven received us warmly and we nearly won a princess, but when the Tuyuhun king came to court the match was refused—has someone come between us?"

sentences.zh: 弄贊怒，率羊同共擊吐谷渾，吐谷渾不能亢，走青海之陰，盡取其貲畜。

translations.literal: Nongzan was enraged and led the Yangtong together to attack Tuyuhun; Tuyuhun could not resist, fled to the north of Qinghai Lake, and lost all its goods and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan flew into a rage, led the Yangtong in an attack on Tuyuhun, and when Tuyuhun could not hold its ground it fled beyond Qinghai Lake while the Tibetans seized all its wealth and herds.

sentences.zh: 又攻党項、白蘭羌，破之。

translations.literal: He also attacked the Dangxiang and Bailan Qiang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He next struck the Dangxiang and Bailan Qiang and broke them.

sentences.zh: 勒兵二十萬入寇松州，命使者貢金甲，且言迎公主，謂左右曰：「公主不至，我且深入。」

translations.literal: He marshaled two hundred thousand troops to invade Songzhou, ordered envoys to present golden armor, and also said he came to welcome the princess, telling his attendants: "If the princess does not come, I shall press deeper."
translations.idiomatic: He massed two hundred thousand men and raided Songzhou, sent envoys offering golden armor and claiming he had come to receive the princess, and told his followers, "If the princess is not sent, I will drive farther in."

sentences.zh: 都督韓威輕出覘賊，反為所敗，屬羌大擾，皆叛以應賊。

translations.literal: The Protectorate General Han Wei rashly went out to reconnoiter the enemy and was in turn defeated; the dependent Qiang were greatly disturbed and all rebelled to join the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Protectorate General Han Wei rashly rode out to scout the enemy and was beaten in turn; the dependent Qiang rose in turmoil and went over to the invaders.

sentences.zh: 乃詔吏部尚書侯君集為行軍大總管，出當彌道，右領軍大將軍執失思力出白蘭道，右武衛大將軍牛進達出闊水道，右領軍將軍劉蘭出洮河道，並為行軍總管，率步騎五萬進討。

translations.literal: Then an edict appointed Minister of Civil Appointments Hou Junji as Grand Commander of the campaign army, advancing by the Dangmi route; Right Leader of the Right Army General Zhishi Sili by the Bailan route; Right Martial Guard General Niu Jinda by the Kuanshui route; Right Army General Liu Lan by the Taohe route—all as campaign commanders, leading fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then named Minister Hou Junji grand campaign commander on the Dangmi route, with Zhishi Sili on the Bailan route, Niu Jinda on the Kuanshui route, and Liu Lan on the Taohe route—each at the head of fifty thousand foot and horse—to advance against the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 進達自松州夜鏖其營，斬首千級。

translations.literal: Jinda from Songzhou by night fiercely assaulted their camp and beheaded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: From Songzhou, Niu Jinda stormed the Tibetan camp by night and took a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 初東寇也，連歲不解，其大臣請返國，不聽，自殺者八人。

translations.literal: When they first raided eastward the campaign dragged on for years without resolution; ministers begged to return home and were not heeded—eight men killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern campaign had dragged on for years; ministers pleaded to withdraw but were refused, and eight took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 至是弄贊始懼，引而去，以使者來謝罪，固請昏，許之。

translations.literal: At this Nongzan at last grew afraid, withdrew his army, and sent envoys to apologize; he firmly requested a marriage alliance and was granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Nongzan take fright, pull back his forces, and send envoys to apologize and press anew for a marriage alliance; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 遣大論薛祿東贊獻黃金五千兩，它寶稱是，以為聘。

translations.literal: He sent the Great Lun Xue Ludongzan to present five thousand taels of gold and other treasures in proportion, as betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the great minister Gar Tongtsen (Xue Ludongzan) with five thousand taels of gold and comparable treasures as bride-price.

sentences.zh: 十五年，妻以宗女文成公主，詔江夏王道宗持節護送，築館河源王之國。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year a clanswoman was given in marriage as Princess Wencheng; the Prince of Jiangxia Li Daozong was ordered to escort her with credentials and a lodge was built in the domain of the King of Heyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor gave his clanswoman as Princess Wencheng in marriage, ordered Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong to escort her with imperial credentials, and built a lodge in the King of Heyuan's territory.

sentences.zh: 弄贊率兵次柏海親迎，見道宗，執婿禮恭甚，見中國服飾之美，縮縮愧沮。

translations.literal: Nongzan led troops to camp at Bohai to welcome her in person; seeing Daozong he performed the son-in-law's rites with great respect; seeing the beauty of Chinese dress and ornaments he shrank back ashamed and abashed.
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan marched to Bohai to meet the bride in person; when he saw Daozong he observed the rites of a son-in-law with deep respect, but the splendor of Chinese dress left him abashed and ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 歸國，自以其先未有昏帝女者，乃為公主築一城以誇後世，遂立宮室以居。

translations.literal: Returning to his country, reflecting that his ancestors had never married an emperor's daughter, he built a city for the princess to boast to posterity, and then erected palaces to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Tibet he reflected that no ancestor had ever married an emperor's daughter, built a city for the princess to show posterity, and raised palaces for their residence.

sentences.zh: 公主惡國人赭面，弄贊下令國中禁之。

translations.literal: The princess disliked the people's painting their faces with ochre; Nongzan ordered the practice forbidden throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The princess detested the Tibetan custom of painting the face with ochre, and Nongzan forbade it throughout the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 自褫氈罽，襲紈綃，為華風。

translations.literal: He himself cast off felt and woolens, put on silk gauze, and adopted Chinese style.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside felt and woolens for silk gauze and took up Chinese ways.

sentences.zh: 遣諸豪子弟入國學，習《詩》、《書》。

translations.literal: He sent the sons of the great clans into the National University to study the Odes and the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He sent noble youths to the National University to study the Odes and the Documents.

sentences.zh: 又請儒者典書疏。

translations.literal: He also requested Confucian scholars to manage correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for Confucian scholars to handle official correspondence.

sentences.zh: 帝伐遼還，使祿東贊上書曰：「陛下平定四方，日月所照，並臣治之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned from campaigning against Liao, he had Ludongzan submit a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has pacified the four quarters; wherever sun and moon shine, all are your subjects.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's return from the Liaodong campaign, Gar Tongtsen sent a memorial: "Your Majesty has pacified the four quarters; wherever sun and moon shine, all bow to your rule.

sentences.zh: 高麗恃遠，弗率於禮，天子自將度遼，隳城陷陣，指日凱旋，雖雁飛於天，無是之速。

translations.literal: Goguryeo relied on distance and would not follow the rites; the Son of Heaven personally led the crossing of the Liao, destroyed cities and broke formations, and would return in triumph within days—though geese fly in the sky, none is so swift.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo, trusting in its distance, defied the rites; the Son of Heaven led the crossing of the Liao in person, stormed cities and shattered their lines, and would return victorious within days—no wild goose in flight could match such speed.

sentences.zh: 夫鵝猶雁也，臣謹冶黃金為鵝以獻。」

translations.literal: A goose is like a wild goose; your servant respectfully casts gold into a goose to present."
translations.idiomatic: A goose is kin to the wild goose; your servant has therefore cast a golden goose as tribute."

sentences.zh: 其高七尺，中實酒三斛。

translations.literal: It was seven chi high and held three hu of wine within.
translations.idiomatic: It stood seven chi tall and held three hu of wine within.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，右衛率府長史王玄策使西域，為中天竺所鈔，弄贊發精兵從玄策討破之，來獻俘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Chief Secretary of the Right Guard Wang Xuance was envoy to the Western Regions and was robbed by Central India; Nongzan sent elite troops to follow Xuance and defeat them, then came to present captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Wang Xuance of the Right Guard was robbed in Central India on a mission to the west; Nongzan sent picked troops to join him, crushed the Indians, and presented captives at court.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，擢駙馬都尉、西海郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong acceded, he was promoted to Commandant of the Horse and made Prince of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne, Nongzan was made Commandant of the Horse and Prince of Xihai.

sentences.zh: 弄贊以書詒長孫無忌曰：「天子初即位，下有不忠者，願勒兵赴國共討之。」

translations.literal: Nongzan sent a letter to Zhangsun Wuji saying: "The Son of Heaven has just taken the throne; if there are disloyal subjects below, I wish to lead troops to the realm to join in punishing them."
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan wrote to Zhangsun Wuji: "Now that the Son of Heaven has newly ascended, if any below are disloyal, I am ready to march to your aid and help punish them."

sentences.zh: 並獻金琲十五種以薦昭陵。

translations.literal: He also presented fifteen kinds of golden ornaments as offerings for Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent fifteen kinds of golden ornaments as offerings for Taizong's Zhaoling tomb.

sentences.zh: 進封賨王，賜餉蕃渥。

translations.literal: He was further enfeoffed as Prince of Bin and granted rich provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Prince of Bin and given lavish gifts and supplies.

sentences.zh: 又請蠶種、酒人與碾硙等諸工，詔許。

translations.literal: He also requested silkworm eggs, wine-makers, and millstone craftsmen and other artisans; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for silkworm eggs, vintners, millwrights, and other craftsmen, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，死，遣使者吊祠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yonghui era he died; the court sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui he died, and the court sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 無子，立其孫，幼不事，故祿東贊相其國，

translations.literal: He had no son; his grandson was installed, but being young did not govern, so Ludongzan administered the state.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; a grandson was enthroned but was too young to rule, and Gar Tongtsen governed in his stead.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，獻金盎、金頗羅等，復請昏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, he presented golden bowls, golden patra vessels, and the like, and again requested a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianqing (658), he presented golden bowls, golden patra vessels, and other treasures, and again sought a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吐谷渾內附，祿東贊怨忿，率銳兵擊之，而吐谷渾大臣素和貴奔吐蕃，槊以虛實，故吐蕃能破其國。

translations.literal: Before long Tuyuhun submitted to the interior; Ludongzan was resentful and led crack troops to attack; the Tuyuhun minister Suhe Gui fled to Tibet and informed them of strengths and weaknesses, so Tibet was able to destroy their state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, when Tuyuhun submitted to the Tang, Gar Tongtsen in anger led elite troops against them; the Tuyuhun minister Suhe Gui defected to Tibet and revealed their situation, enabling the Tibetans to overrun the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 慕容諾曷缽與弘化公主引殘落走涼州，詔涼州都督鄭仁泰為青海道行軍大總管，率將軍獨孤卿雲等屯涼、鄯，左武候大將軍蘇定方為安集大使，為諸將節度，以定其亂。

translations.literal: Murong Nuohubo and Princess Honghua led the remnant people in flight to Liangzhou; an edict made Protectorate General of Liangzhou Zheng Rentai Grand Commander of the Qinghai Route campaign army, leading Generals Dugu Qingyun and others to encamp at Liang and Shan, and Left Martial Guard General Su Dingfang Pacification Commissioner to direct the generals and settle the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nuohubo and Princess Honghua fled with the survivors to Liangzhou; Zheng Rentai was named grand commander of the Qinghai route, Dugu Qingyun and others encamped at Liang and Shan, and Su Dingfang was made pacification commissioner to direct the generals and restore order.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃使論仲琮入朝，表吐谷渾罪，帝遣使者譙讓，乃使來請與吐谷渾平憾，求赤水地牧馬，不許。

translations.literal: The Tibetan envoy Lun Zhongqiong came to court and listed Tuyuhun's offenses; the Emperor sent envoys to reprove them, whereupon they sent word asking to settle grievances with Tuyuhun and requesting pasture land at Chishui to herd horses—it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan envoy Lun Zhongqiong came to court accusing Tuyuhun; the emperor sent envoys to rebuke Tibet, after which they asked to make peace with Tuyuhun and sought grazing rights at Chishui—both were refused.

sentences.zh: 會祿東贊死。

translations.literal: Just then Ludongzan died.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Gar Tongtsen died.

sentences.zh: 東贊不知書而性明毅，用兵有節制，吐蕃倚之，遂為強國。

translations.literal: Tongtsen did not know writing but was by nature clear and resolute; in using troops he had discipline; Tibet relied on him and thus became a powerful state.
translations.idiomatic: Gar Tongtsen was illiterate but shrewd and resolute, disciplined in war; Tibet leaned on him and grew into a great power.

sentences.zh: 始入朝，占對合旨，太宗擢拜右衛大將軍，以瑯邪公主外孫妻之。

translations.literal: When he first came to court his answers suited the Emperor's intent; Taizong promoted him to General of the Right Guard and gave him in marriage a granddaughter of the Princess of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: On his first audience his replies pleased Taizong, who made him General of the Right Guard and married him to a granddaughter of the Princess of Langye.

sentences.zh: 祿東贊自言：「先臣為聘婦，不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Ludongzan said himself: "Your servant's late father was betrothal envoy; I dare not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Gar Tongtsen said, "My late father served as betrothal envoy; I dare not accept this command.

sentences.zh: 且贊普未謁公主，陪臣敢辭！」

translations.literal: Moreover the tsenpo has not yet paid court to the princess—how dare a companion minister decline!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the tsenpo has not yet presented himself to the princess—how dare a mere companion minister refuse!"

sentences.zh: 帝異其言，然欲懷以恩，不聽也。

translations.literal: The Emperor was struck by his words, yet wishing to win him with kindness, did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed by his reply but, wishing to win him over with kindness, did not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 有子曰欽陵、曰贊婆、曰悉多於、曰勃論。

translations.literal: He had sons named Qinling, Zanpo, Siduoyu, and Bolun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Qinling, Zanpo, Siduoyu, and Bolun.

sentences.zh: 祿東贊死，而兄弟並當國。

translations.literal: When Ludongzan died, the brothers together held the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After Gar Tongtsen died, the brothers ruled Tibet jointly.

sentences.zh: 自是歲入邊，盡破有諸羌羈縻十二州。

translations.literal: From this time they raided the border yearly, utterly destroying the twelve jimi prefectures of the various Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they raided the frontier every year, overrunning the twelve jimi prefectures of the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 總章中，議徙吐谷渾部於涼州旁南山。

translations.literal: In the Zongzhang era it was proposed to relocate the Tuyuhun tribes to the southern mountains beside Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Zongzhang, the court debated moving the Tuyuhun to the southern hills near Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝刈吐蕃之入，召宰相姜恪閻立本、將軍契何力等議先擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: The Emperor, checking Tibet's incursions, summoned Chancellors Jiang Ke and Yan Liben, General Qi Heli, and others to discuss striking Tibet first.
translations.idiomatic: Wary of Tibetan raids, the emperor summoned Jiang Ke, Yan Liben, Qi Heli, and others to discuss a preemptive strike against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 立本曰：「民饑未可以師。」

translations.literal: Liben said: "The people are starving—it is not yet time for troops."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Liben said, "The people are starving; this is no time to mobilize."

sentences.zh: 何力曰：「吐蕃介在西極，臣恐師到，獸竄山伏，捕討無所得，至春復侵吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Heli said: "Tibet lies at the western extremity; your servant fears that when the army arrives, beasts will bolt into the mountains and lie hidden, and pursuit will gain nothing—by spring they will raid Tuyuhun again.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Heli replied, "Tibet sits at the far west; I fear our armies will find only beasts fled into the hills—nothing to pursue—and by spring they will again harry Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 臣請勿救，使疑吾力困而驕之，一舉可滅也。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks that we not rescue them, so that they suspect our strength is spent and grow arrogant—then in one stroke they can be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Let us withhold aid so they think us exhausted and grow overbold; then one blow can wipe them out."

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「不然，吐谷渾方衰，吐蕃負勝，以衰氣拒勝兵，戰必不亢，不救則滅。

translations.literal: Ke said: "Not so—Tuyuhun is declining, Tibet is buoyed by victory; with declining morale they cannot resist victorious troops and are sure to lose; if we do not save them, they will perish.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ke said, "No—Tuyuhun is failing while Tibet rides a victory; they cannot fight winning troops with failing spirit. Without rescue they are finished.

sentences.zh: 臣謂王師亟助之，使國幸存，後且徐圖可也。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the imperial army should hurry to aid them, so the state may barely survive; later we may plan at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: I urge the imperial forces to rescue them at once so the state may survive; we can plan the rest later."

sentences.zh: 議不決，亦不克徙，

translations.literal: The deliberation was unresolved, and the relocation was not accomplished either.
translations.idiomatic: No decision was reached, and the relocation never took place.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，入殘羈縻十八州，率於闐取龜茲撥換城，於是安西四鎮並廢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng, they entered and ravaged eighteen jimi prefectures, led Khotan to take the Boluan fortress of Kucha, and then the Four Garrisons of Anxi were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1, they invaded and devastated eighteen jimi prefectures, used Khotan to seize Kucha's Boluan fortress, and the Four Garrisons of Anxi were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 詔右威衛大將軍薛仁貴為邏娑道行軍大總管，左衛員外大將軍阿史那道真、左衛將軍郭待封自副，出討吐蕃，並護吐谷渾還國。

translations.literal: An edict made Right Majestic Guard General Xue Rengui Grand Commander of the Luosha Route campaign army, with Left Guard Assistant Grand General Ashina Daozhen and Left Guard General Guo Daifeng as deputies, to campaign against Tibet and also escort Tuyuhun back to its state.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui was appointed grand commander of the Luosha route, with Ashina Daozhen and Guo Daifeng as deputies, to attack Tibet and restore Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 師凡十餘萬，至大非川，為欽陵所拒，王師敗績，遂滅吐谷渾而盡有其地。

translations.literal: The army numbered over a hundred thousand; reaching the Da Fei River, it was blocked by Qinling; the imperial army was routed; Tuyuhun was destroyed and Tibet wholly possessed its lands.
translations.idiomatic: An army of more than one hundred thousand reached the Da Fei River, was blocked by Qinling, and suffered a crushing defeat; Tuyuhun was destroyed and Tibet took all its territory.

sentences.zh: 詔司戎太常伯、同東西臺三品姜恪為涼州道行軍大總管出討，會恪卒，班師。

translations.literal: An edict made Director of Military Affairs and Grand Master of Ceremonies, Peer of Both Eastern and Western Platforms Jiang Ke Grand Commander of the Liangzhou Route campaign army to campaign; but Ke died on the way and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ke was sent as grand commander of the Liangzhou route but died en route and the force was recalled.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣大臣仲琮入朝。

translations.literal: Tibet sent the great minister Zhongqiong to court.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent Minister Zhongqiong to the capital.

sentences.zh: 仲琮少遊太學，頗知書。

translations.literal: Zhongqiong had studied in the Imperial Academy in youth and knew books fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqiong had studied at the Imperial Academy as a youth and was well read.

sentences.zh: 帝召見問曰：「贊普孰與其祖賢？」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned and asked: "Is the tsenpo as worthy as his grandfather?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him and asked, "Is the present tsenpo the equal of his grandfather in worth?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「勇果善斷不逮也，然勤以治國，下無敢欺，令主也。

translations.literal: He replied: "In courage, decisiveness, and keen judgment he does not match him, yet he is diligent in governing the state and none below dare deceive him—a good ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "He lacks his grandfather's courage and decisiveness, yet he governs diligently and none below dare deceive him—a capable ruler.

sentences.zh: 且吐蕃居寒露之野，物產寡薄，烏海之陰，盛夏積雪，暑毼冬裘。

translations.literal: Moreover Tibet dwells in the cold-dew wilderness; its products are scant; west of Wuhai, even in midsummer snow piles up; in summer they wear felt, in winter fur.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet lives on barren highlands with meager produce; west of Wuhai snow lies thick even in midsummer—they wear felt in summer and fur in winter.

sentences.zh: 隨水草以牧，寒則城處，施廬帳。

translations.literal: They follow water and grass to herd; when cold they dwell in walled places and set up felt tents.
translations.idiomatic: They herd by water and grass; in cold weather they settle in walled camps and pitch felt tents.

sentences.zh: 器用不當中國萬分一。

translations.literal: Their utensils and implements are not one ten-thousandth of China's.
translations.idiomatic: Their tools and goods are not one ten-thousandth of China's.

sentences.zh: 但上下一力，議事自下，因人所利而行，是能久而強也。」

translations.literal: Yet above and below are of one mind; deliberation rises from below; they act according to what benefits the people—thus they can endure long and grow strong."
translations.idiomatic: Yet court and people pull together, policy rises from below, and they act on what benefits their people—that is how they endure and grow strong."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吐谷渾與吐蕃本甥舅國，素和貴叛其主，吐蕃任之，奪其土地。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Tuyuhun and Tibet were originally nephew-and-uncle states; Suhegui rebelled against his lord, Tibet employed him, and seized their lands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Tuyuhun and Tibet were kin by marriage; Suhegui betrayed his lord, Tibet used him, and seized Tuyuhun's lands.

sentences.zh: 薛仁貴等往定慕容氏，又伏擊之，而寇我涼州，何邪？」

translations.literal: Xue Rengui and others went to settle the Murong clan, yet you ambushed them and then raided our Liangzhou—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui went to restore the Murong, yet you ambushed him and now raid Liangzhou—why?"

sentences.zh: 仲琮頓首曰：「臣奉命來獻，它非所聞。」

translations.literal: Zhongqiong bowed his head and said: "Your servant came on orders to present tribute; of other matters I have not heard."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqiong kowtowed and said, "I came only to present tribute on orders; I have heard nothing of the rest."

sentences.zh: 帝韙其答。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his reply.

sentences.zh: 然以仲琮非用事臣，故殺其禮，

translations.literal: Yet because Zhongqiong was not a minister in power, his ceremonial reception was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: But because Zhongqiong held no real power at court, his ceremonial honors were cut back.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，遣大臣論吐渾彌來請和，且求與吐谷渾脩好，帝不聽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan (675), they sent the great minister Lun Tuhunmi to sue for peace and also asked to renew friendship with Tuyuhun; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 2 (675), they sent Minister Lun Tuhunmi to sue for peace and to reconcile with Tuyuhun; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，攻鄯、廓、河、芳四州，殺略吏及馬牛萬計。

translations.literal: The next year they attacked the four prefectures of Shan, Kuo, He, and Fang, killing and plundering officials and tens of thousands of horses and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they struck Shan, Kuo, He, and Fang, killing officials and plundering tens of thousands of horses and cattle.

sentences.zh: 乃詔周王顯為洮州道行軍元帥，率工部尚書劉審禮等十二總管，以相王輪為涼州道行軍元帥，率左衛大將軍契何力、鴻臚卿蕭嗣業等軍討之。

translations.literal: Then an edict made Prince of Zhou Xian campaign marshal of the Tao Route army, leading Minister of Works Liu Shenli and twelve other grand commanders, and made Prince of Xiang Lun campaign marshal of the Liang Route army, leading Left Guard General Qi Heli, Minister of Ceremonies Xiao Siye, and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian was made marshal of the Tao route with Liu Shenli and twelve commanders; Prince Lun was made marshal of the Liang route with Qi Heli, Xiao Siye, and others to attack Tibet.

sentences.zh: 二王不克行。

translations.literal: The two princes could not set out.
translations.idiomatic: Neither prince could take the field.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃進攻疊州，破密恭、丹嶺二縣，又攻扶州，敗守將。

translations.literal: Tibet advanced to attack Die Prefecture, broke Migong and Danling counties, then attacked Fu Prefecture and defeated the defending general.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet attacked Die Prefecture, overran Migong and Danling counties, then struck Fu Prefecture and defeated its garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 乃高選尚書左僕射劉仁軌為洮河鎮守使，久之，無功。

translations.literal: Then they highly selected Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Liu Ren'gui as Defender of Tao and He; after a long time, there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ren'gui was then chosen as defender of the Tao and He region, but after a long campaign achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃與西突厥連兵攻安西，復命中書令李敬玄為洮河道行軍大總管、西河鎮撫大使、鄯州都督，代仁軌。

translations.literal: Tibet joined with the Western Turks in arms to attack Anxi; again an edict made Chief Councillor Li Jingxuan Grand Commander of the Tao-He Route campaign army, Pacification Commissioner of the Western Rivers, and Protectorate General of Shan Prefecture, replacing Ren'gui.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet allied with the Western Turks to attack Anxi; Li Jingxuan was made grand commander of the Tao-He route, pacification commissioner of the western rivers, and protector of Shan, replacing Liu Ren'gui.

sentences.zh: 下詔募猛士，毋限籍役痕負，帝自臨遣。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to recruit fierce warriors without limit by household register, corvée service, or tattooed convicts; the Emperor personally saw them off.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recruited fierce fighters without regard to household register, corvée status, or criminal marks; the emperor saw them off in person.

sentences.zh: 又敕益州長史李孝逸、巂州都督拓王奉益發劍南、山南士。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Yizhou Chief Administrator Li Xiaoyi and Qizhou Protectorate General Tuowang Fengyi to raise troops from Jiannan and Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoyi of Yizhou and Tuowang Fengyi of Qizhou were also ordered to raise troops from Jiannan and Shannan.

sentences.zh: 先戰龍支，吐蕃敗。

translations.literal: They first fought at Longzhi and Tibet was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They first fought at Longzhi and defeated the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 敬玄率劉審禮擊吐蕃青海上，審禮戰沒。

translations.literal: Jingxuan led Liu Shenli to strike Tibet on the Qinghai Sea; Shenli fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingxuan led Liu Shenli against Tibet on the Qinghai Sea; Liu Shenli was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 敬玄頓承風嶺，礙險不得縱，吐蕃壓王師屯，左領軍將軍黑齒常之率死士五百，夜斧其營，虜驚，自相藺藉而死者甚眾，乃引去。

translations.literal: Jingxuan halted at Chengfeng Ridge, blocked by rugged terrain and unable to deploy; Tibet pressed the imperial army's encampment; Left Army General Heichi Changzhi led five hundred death-defying soldiers and by night hacked their camp; the barbarians were startled, trampled one another in great numbers and died, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingxuan was pinned at Chengfeng Ridge by the terrain while Tibet pressed the imperial camp; Heichi Changzhi led five hundred picked men in a night raid on the enemy camp; the Tibetans panicked, trampled one another to death in great numbers, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敬玄僅脫。

translations.literal: Jingxuan barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingxuan barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 帝既儒仁無遠略，見諸將數敗，乃博咨近臣，求所以御之之術。

translations.literal: The Emperor, being Confucian and humane and without far-reaching strategy, seeing the generals repeatedly defeated, then broadly consulted close ministers, seeking the means to control them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, scholarly and mild and lacking long-range strategy, saw his generals fail again and again and broadly consulted his close advisers on how to cope with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕未始擐甲履軍，往者滅高麗、百濟，比歲用師，中國騷然，朕至今悔之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I have never yet donned armor and trod the army; in the past we destroyed Goguryeo and Baekje, and in recent years we have used troops—the Central Realm has been unsettled, and I regret it to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have never myself taken the field; we destroyed Goguryeo and Baekje, and in recent years constant campaigning has unsettled the realm—I regret it still.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃內侵，盍為我謀？」

translations.literal: Now Tibet invades within—will you not plan for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Tibet raids within our borders—what will you advise?"

sentences.zh: 中書舍人劉祎之等具對，須家給人足可擊也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Liu Yizhi and others answered in full: only when every household is provided for and the people are sufficient can they be struck.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi and others answered at length that Tibet could be attacked only once every household was secure and the people were provided for.

sentences.zh: 或言賊險黠不可與和，或言營田嚴守便。

translations.literal: Some said the enemy was treacherous and cunning and could not be treated with; some said garrison farming and strict defense were expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the enemy was too treacherous to treat with; others favored garrison farming and strict defense.

sentences.zh: 惟中書侍郎薛元超謂：「縱敵生患，不如料兵擊之。」

translations.literal: Only Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao said: "To indulge the enemy breeds trouble—better to measure troops and strike them."
translations.idiomatic: Only Xue Yuanchao said, "Indulging the enemy breeds trouble; better to muster troops and strike."

sentences.zh: 帝顧黃門侍郎來恒曰：「自李勣亡，遂無善將。」

translations.literal: The Emperor turned to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Lai Heng and said: "Since Li Ji's death, there have been no good generals."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Lai Heng and said, "Since Li Ji's death there has been no capable general."

sentences.zh: 恒即言：「向洮河兵足以制敵，但諸將不用命，故無功。」

translations.literal: Heng immediately said: "The troops at Tao and He were sufficient to control the enemy, but the generals did not obey orders, hence no success."
translations.idiomatic: Lai Heng said at once, "The Tao-He forces were strong enough to hold the enemy, but the generals would not obey—that is why we failed."

sentences.zh: 帝殊不悟，因罷議。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not understand at all and therefore ended the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not grasp this at all and dismissed the council.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年，贊普死，子器弩悉弄立，欽陵復擅政，使大臣來告喪，帝遣使者往會葬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yifeng the tsenpo died; his son Qinu Sennong succeeded; Qinling again usurped government; he sent a great minister to announce the mourning; the Emperor sent envoys to join the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In 679 (Yifeng 4) the tsenpo died; his son Qinu Sennong succeeded while Qinling again seized power; Tibet sent ministers to announce the death, and the emperor sent envoys to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 明年，贊婆、素和貴率兵三萬攻河源，屯良非川，敬玄與戰湟川，敗績。

translations.literal: The next year Zanpo and Suhegui led thirty thousand troops to attack Heyuan, encamped at Liangfei River; Jingxuan fought them at Huang River and was routed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zanpo and Suhegui led thirty thousand men against Heyuan and encamped at the Liangfei River; Li Jingxuan fought them on the Huang River and was routed.

sentences.zh: 左武衛將軍黑齒常之以精騎三千夜搗其營，贊婆懼，引去。

translations.literal: Left Martial Guard General Heichi Changzhi with three thousand picked cavalry raided their camp by night; Zanpo was afraid and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Heichi Changzhi with three thousand elite horsemen raided their camp by night; Zanpo fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 遂擢常之為河源軍經略大使。

translations.literal: Changzhi was then promoted to Commissioner for Planning of the Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi was then made commissioner for the Heyuan army.

sentences.zh: 乃嚴烽邏，開屯田，虜謀稍折。

translations.literal: He then tightened beacon and patrol lines, opened garrison farms, and the barbarians' designs were somewhat checked.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened the beacon lines, opened garrison farms, and Tibetan designs were gradually checked.

sentences.zh: 初，劍南度茂州之西築安戎城，以迮其鄙。

translations.literal: At first Jiannan crossed west of Maozhou to build Anrong Fortress, to constrict their borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiannan had built Anrong Fortress west of Maozhou to pinch the Tibetan frontier.

sentences.zh: 俄為生羌導虜取之以守，因並西洱河諸蠻，盡臣羊同、党項諸羌。

translations.literal: Soon the living Qiang guided the barbarians to take it and hold it; thereby they also annexed the various barbarians west of the Er River, and wholly made subjects of Yangtong and the various Qiang of the Dangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon living Qiang guided the Tibetans to seize and hold it; they then absorbed the tribes west of the Er River and brought Yangtong and the Dangxiang Qiang under subjection.

sentences.zh: 其地東與松、茂、巂接，南極婆羅門，西取四鎮，北抵突厥，幅圓餘萬里，漢、魏諸戎所無也。

translations.literal: Their territory east joined Song, Mao, and Qi; south reached to Brahmana; west took the Four Garrisons; north reached the Turks; its compass exceeded ten thousand li—what the various Rong of Han and Wei never had.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands stretched east to Song, Mao, and Qi, south to India, west to the Four Garrisons, and north to the Turks—a domain of more than ten thousand li, such as no barbarian power of Han or Wei had held.

sentences.zh: 永隆元年，文成公主薨，遣使者吊祠，又歸我陳行焉之喪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonglong, Princess Wencheng died; they sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice, and also returned the remains of our Chen Xingyan.
translations.idiomatic: In 680 (Yonglong 1) Princess Wencheng died; Tibet sent envoys to mourn and returned the body of our envoy Chen Xingyan.

sentences.zh: 初，行焉使虜，論欽陵欲拜己，臨以兵，不為屈，留之十年。

translations.literal: At first Xingyan was envoy to the barbarians; Lun Qinling wished him to bow to himself and menaced him with troops, but he would not yield and was detained ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xingyan was envoy to Tibet, Qinling demanded he bow to him and threatened him with troops; he would not yield and was held ten years.

sentences.zh: 及是喪還，贈睦州刺史。

translations.literal: When at this time his remains were returned, he was posthumously made Prefect of Mu.
translations.idiomatic: When his body was returned, he was posthumously made prefect of Mu.

sentences.zh: 贊婆復入良非川，常之擊走之。

translations.literal: Zanpo again entered Liangfei River; Changzhi struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zanpo again entered the Liangfei River valley; Changzhi drove him off.

sentences.zh: 武後時，與蠻夷同朝賀，

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu, they came to court with the various barbarians to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu they came to court with other barbarians to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，詔文昌右相韋待價為安息道大總管，安西大都護閻溫古副之，以討吐蕃，兵逗留，坐死、徙。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang (689), an edict made Right Chancellor of Literary Brilliance Wei Daojia Grand Commander of the Anxi Route campaign army, with Grand Protector General of Anxi Yan Wengu as deputy, to campaign against Tibet; the troops lingered and on that account some were sentenced to death and others banished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang 1 (689), Wei Daojia was made grand commander of the Anxi route with Yan Wengu as deputy to attack Tibet; the army stalled and commanders were executed or banished.

sentences.zh: 明年，復詔文昌右相岑長倩為武威道行軍大總管討之，兵半道罷。

translations.literal: The next year again an edict made Right Chancellor of Literary Brilliance Cen Changqian Grand Commander of the Wuwei Route campaign army to campaign against them; the troops were halted halfway.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Cen Changqian was sent as grand commander of the Wuwei route, but the campaign was called off en route.

sentences.zh: 又明年，大首領曷蘇率貴川部與党項種三十萬降，後以右玉鈐衛將軍張玄遇為安撫使，率兵二萬迎之，次大度水，吐蕃禽曷蘇去。

translations.literal: The year after that, the great chieftain Hesu led the Guichuan tribe and three hundred thousand of the Dangxiang clans to surrender; later Right Jade Bell Guard General Zhang Xuanyu was made Pacification Commissioner, leading twenty thousand troops to welcome them; halting at the Dadu River, Tibet seized Hesu away.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the chieftain Hesu led the Guichuan tribe and three hundred thousand Dangxiang to surrender; Zhang Xuanyu was sent with twenty thousand men to receive them but, halted at the Dadu River, Tibet seized Hesu.

sentences.zh: 而它酋昝插又率羌、蠻八千自來，玄遇即其部置葉州，用昝插為刺史，刻石大度山以紀功。

translations.literal: But another chieftain Zancha again led eight thousand Qiang and barbarians of himself to come; Xuanyu at once set up Ye Prefecture on their tribe, made Zancha prefect, and carved stone on Dadu Mountain to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Another chieftain, Zancha, then brought eight thousand Qiang and tribesmen of his own accord; Xuanyu established Ye Prefecture for them, made Zancha prefect, and carved a stone on Dadu Mountain to commemorate the feat.

sentences.zh: 是歲，又詔右鷹揚衛將軍王孝傑為武威道行軍總管，率西州都督唐休璟、左武衛大將軍阿史那忠節擊吐蕃，大破其眾，復取四鎮，更置安西都護府於龜茲，以兵鎮守。

translations.literal: That year again an edict made Right Hawk-and-Banner Guard General Wang Xiaojie campaign commander of the Wuwei Route army, leading Protectorate General of Xizhou Tang Xiujing and Left Martial Guard Grand General Ashina Zhongjie to strike Tibet; they greatly broke their masses, recovered the Four Garrisons, and re-established the Anxi Protectorate at Kucha, garrisoned with troops.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Xiaojie was made commander of the Wuwei route with Tang Xiujing and Ashina Zhongjie; they routed the Tibetans, recovered the Four Garrisons, and re-established the Anxi protectorate at Kucha with a garrison.

sentences.zh: 議者請廢四鎮勿有也，右史崔融獻議曰：「戎狄為中國患尚矣，五帝、三王所不臣。

translations.literal: Deliberators asked to abolish the Four Garrisons and not have them; Right Scribe Cui Rong submitted a memorial saying: "The Rong and Di have long been China's affliction—even the Five Emperors and Three Kings did not make them subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged abandoning the Four Garrisons; Right Scribe Cui Rong submitted a memorial: "Barbarians have long plagued China—even the Five Emperors and Three Kings could not fully subdue them.

sentences.zh: 漢以百萬眾困平城，其後武帝赫然發憤，甘心四夷，張騫始通西域，列四郡，據兩關，斷匈奴右臂，稍稍度河、湟，築令居，以絕南羌。

translations.literal: Han with a million troops was trapped at Pingcheng; afterward Emperor Wu blazed with anger, bent on the four barbarians; Zhang Qian first opened the Western Regions, arrayed four commanderies, held the two passes, severed the Xiongnu's right arm, gradually crossed the Huang and Tao rivers, built Lingju, to cut off the Southern Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han was trapped at Pingcheng with a million men; then Emperor Wu roused himself, bent on the four quarters; Zhang Qian opened the west, established four commanderies, held the two passes, severed the Xiongnu right wing, crossed the Huang and Tao, and built Lingju to isolate the Southern Qiang.

sentences.zh: 於是鄣候亭燧出長城數千里，傾府庫，殫士馬，行人使者歲月不絕，至作皮幣，算緡法，稅舟車，榷酒酤。

translations.literal: Thereupon beacon towers and signal posts stretched thousands of li beyond the Long Wall; treasuries were emptied, soldiers and horses exhausted, travelers and envoys unceasing month after month—even leather currency was made, the suanmin law enacted, boats and carts taxed, and wine monopolized.
translations.idiomatic: Beacon towers ran thousands of li beyond the Wall; treasuries were drained and armies exhausted; envoys and merchants never ceased; leather currency, suanmin taxes, boat and cart levies, and wine monopolies followed.

sentences.zh: 夫豈不懷，為長久計然也！

translations.literal: Was this not because they cherished the realm, but planned for the long term!
translations.idiomatic: This was not indulgence but long-range planning!

sentences.zh: 匈奴於是孤特遠竄，遂開西域，置使者領護。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu were thus isolated and fled far; then the Western Regions were opened and envoys were set to lead and protect them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu were isolated and driven far off; the Western Regions were opened and protector envoys were installed.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，皆復內屬，至於延光，三絕三通。

translations.literal: When Guangwu restored the dynasty, all again submitted within; down to Yanguang, thrice broken off and thrice reconnected.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu's restoration all submitted again; by the Yanguang era contact had been broken and restored three times.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝踐漢舊跡，並南山抵蔥嶺，剖裂府鎮，煙火相望，吐蕃不敢內侮。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong the Cultured followed Han's old tracks, joined the southern mountains to the Onion Range, split prefectures and garrisons, beacon fires facing one another, and Tibet dared not insult within.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong followed Han precedent, linked the southern mountains to the Pamirs, divided prefectures and garrisons until beacon fires faced one another, and Tibet dared not raid within.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，有司無狀，棄四鎮不能有，而吐蕃遂張，入焉耆之西，長鼓右驅，逾高昌，歷車師，鈔常樂，絕莫賀延磧，以臨敦煌。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time the officials were shameless, abandoned the Four Garrisons and could not hold them; Tibet then expanded, entered west of Yanqi, long drums on the right driving forward, crossed Gaochang, passed through Cheshi, raided Changle, cut across the Moheyan Desert, to press on Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong incompetent officials abandoned the Four Garrisons; Tibet then expanded west of Yanqi, drove through Gaochang and Cheshi, raided Changle, crossed the Moheyan Desert, and threatened Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 今孝傑一舉而取四鎮，還先帝舊封，若又棄之，是自毀成功而破完策也。

translations.literal: Now Xiaojie in one stroke recovered the Four Garrisons and restored the former emperor's old enfeoffments; if we abandon them again, we destroy our own success and break a complete strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie has now recovered the Four Garrisons and restored the former emperor's frontier; to abandon them again would destroy our success and ruin a sound policy.

sentences.zh: 夫四鎮無守，胡兵必臨西域，西域震則威憺南羌，南羌連衡，河西必危。

translations.literal: If the Four Garrisons are without defense, barbarian troops will surely come upon the Western Regions; if the Western Regions are shaken, authority will cow the Southern Qiang; if the Southern Qiang ally together, the Hexi will surely be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Without the Four Garrisons, barbarian armies will overrun the west; once the west falls, the Southern Qiang will be cowed into alliance and the Hexi corridor will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 且莫賀延磧袤二千里，無水草，若北接虜，唐兵不可度而北，則伊西、北庭、安西諸蕃悉亡。」

translations.literal: Moreover the Moheyan Desert is two thousand li in extent without water or grass; if it joins the barbarians in the north and Tang troops cannot cross northward, then Yixi, Beiting, Anxi, and all the various tribes will perish."
translations.idiomatic: The Moheyan Desert stretches two thousand li without water or grass; if it links to the north and Tang armies cannot cross, Yixi, Beiting, Anxi, and all western tribes will be lost."

sentences.zh: 議乃格。

translations.literal: The deliberation was then blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal to abandon the garrisons was dropped.

sentences.zh: 於是首領勃論贊與突厥偽可汗阿史那俀子南侵，與孝傑戰冷泉，敗走。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chieftain Bolunzan and the Turks' false qaghan Ashina Houzi invaded south; they fought Xiaojie at Lengquan and were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bolunzan and the Turks' puppet qaghan Ashina Houzi then invaded south; Wang Xiaojie defeated them at Lengquan and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 碎葉鎮守使韓思忠破泥熟沒斯城。

translations.literal: Defender of Suyab Han Sizhong broke the city of Nishu Meisi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sizhong, defender of Suyab, took the city of Nishu Meisi.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年，欽陵、贊婆攻濫洮，孝傑以肅邊道大總管戰素羅汗山，虜敗還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengsheng, Qinling and Zanpo attacked Lantao; Xiaojie as Grand Commander of the Subi Route army fought at Suluo Khan Mountain; the barbarians were defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 695 (Zhengsheng 1) Qinling and Zanpo attacked Lantao; Wang Xiaojie as grand commander of the Subi route defeated them at Suluo Khan Mountain and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又攻涼州，殺都督。

translations.literal: They again attacked Liangzhou and killed the protector general.
translations.idiomatic: They again attacked Liangzhou and killed its protector.

sentences.zh: 遣使者請和，約罷四鎮兵，求分十姓地。

translations.literal: They sent envoys to sue for peace, agreeing to withdraw Four Garrisons troops and asking to divide the lands of the Ten Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys seeking peace, offering to withdraw garrison troops from the Four Garrisons and demanding a partition of the Ten Surnames' lands.

sentences.zh: 武後詔通泉尉郭元振往使，道與欽陵遇。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered Tongquan Magistrate Guo Yuanzhen to go as envoy; on the road he met Qinling.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent Tongquan magistrate Guo Yuanzhen as envoy; en route he met Qinling.

sentences.zh: 元振曰：「東贊事朝廷，誓好無窮，今猥自絕，歲擾邊，父通之，子絕之，孝乎？

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said: "Tongtsen served the court and swore endless friendship; now you rashly break it off and yearly harass the border—the father kept ties, the son severs them—is this filial?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen said, "Gar Tongtsen served the court and swore endless friendship; you rashly break it and raid our border yearly—the father kept faith, the son breaks it—is that filial?

sentences.zh: 父事之，子叛之，忠乎？」

translations.literal: The father served them, the son rebels—is this loyal?"
translations.idiomatic: The father served them, the son rebels—is that loyal?"

sentences.zh: 欽陵曰：「然！

translations.literal: Qinling said: "So it is!
translations.idiomatic: Qinling said, "True!

sentences.zh: 然天子許和，得罷二國戍，使十姓突厥、四鎮各建君長，俾其國自守若何？」

translations.literal: Yet if the Son of Heaven grants peace, we could withdraw garrisons of both states, let the Ten Surnames Turks and the Four Garrisons each establish rulers, and enable their states to guard themselves—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the Son of Heaven grants peace, we could withdraw both sides' garrisons, let the Ten Surnames Turks and the Four Garrisons each set up their own rulers, and let them guard themselves—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 元振曰：「唐以十姓、四鎮撫西土，為列國主，道非有它，且諸部與吐蕃異，久為唐編人矣。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said: "Tang uses the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons to pacify the western lands, as lords of the various states—there is no other design; moreover these tribes differ from Tibet and have long been Tang's registered people."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen said, "Tang holds the west through the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons as sovereign over those states—there is no other design; those tribes differ from Tibet and have long been Tang subjects."

sentences.zh: 欽陵曰：「使者意我規削諸部為唐邊患邪？

translations.literal: Qinling said: "Does the envoy think I plot to pare away the tribes to make border trouble for Tang?
translations.idiomatic: Qinling said, "Do you think I mean to strip away those tribes to plague Tang's border?

sentences.zh: 我若貪土地財賦，彼青海、湟川近矣，今舍不爭何哉？

translations.literal: If I coveted land and wealth, Qinghai and Huang River are near—why now leave them uncontested?
translations.idiomatic: If I coveted land and wealth, Qinghai and the Huang River are close—why leave them uncontested now?

sentences.zh: 突厥諸部磧漠廣莽，去中國遠甚，安有爭地萬里外邪？

translations.literal: The various Turkic tribes' desert sands are vast and wild, far from China indeed—how could there be contention over land ten thousand li away?
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic tribes lie in vast deserts far from China—why contend for land ten thousand li away?

sentences.zh: 且四夷唐皆臣並之，雖海外地際，靡不磨滅，吐蕃適獨在者，徒以兄弟小心，得相保耳。

translations.literal: Moreover of the four barbarians Tang has made subjects and annexed them all—even lands beyond the seas at the frontier, none not ground down; Tibet alone happens to remain, only because the brothers are careful and can preserve one another.
translations.idiomatic: Tang has subdued all the four quarters—even distant lands have been crushed; Tibet alone survives only because we brothers have been careful and preserved one another.

sentences.zh: 十姓五咄陸近安西，於吐蕃遠，俟斤距我裁一磧，騎士騰突，不易旬至，是以為憂也。

translations.literal: The Ten Surnames and the five Tulu tribes are near Anxi, far from Tibet; the yabghu is only one desert from us—cavalry can charge forth and reach within less than ten days; that is why we are concerned.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Surnames and the five Tulu tribes lie near Anxi, far from us; their yabghu is only one desert away—horsemen can strike within ten days; that is our worry.

sentences.zh: 烏海、黃河，關源阻奧，多癘毒，唐必不能入；

translations.literal: Wuhai and the Yellow River—the passes at their sources are rugged and deep, with much pestilence; Tang surely cannot enter;
translations.idiomatic: Wuhai and the Yellow River—their headwaters are rugged and pestilent; Tang surely cannot penetrate them;

sentences.zh: 則弱甲孱將易以為蕃患，故我欲得之，非規諸部也。

translations.literal: then weak armor and feeble generals would easily become Tibet's affliction; therefore I wish to obtain them—not plotting against the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: then weak garrisons and poor commanders would easily become a Tibetan menace; that is why I want those lands—not to seize the tribes themselves.

sentences.zh: 甘、涼距積石道二千里，其廣不數百，狹才百里，我若出張掖、玉門，使大國春不耕，秋不獲，不五六年，可斷其右。

translations.literal: Gan and Liang are two thousand li along the Jishi Pass road; their breadth is only several hundred li, the narrowest only a hundred li. If we emerge from Zhangye and Yumen and make the great state unable to plant in spring or harvest in autumn, within five or six years we can cut off its right flank.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou and Liangzhou lie two thousand li along the Jishi Pass road—only a few hundred li wide, and in places barely a hundred. If we march out through Zhangye and Yumen and keep your great state from sowing in spring and reaping in autumn, within five or six years we can sever its right flank.

sentences.zh: 今棄不為，亦無虞於我矣。

translations.literal: Now if we abandon doing this, they will have no worry about us either.
translations.idiomatic: If we forgo this now, they need not fear us either.

sentences.zh: 青海之役，黃仁素約和，邊守不戒，崔知辯徑俟斤掠我牛羊萬計，是以求之。」

translations.literal: In the Qinghai campaign Huang Rensu made a peace agreement, yet border guards were not vigilant; Cui Zhibian went straight to the yabghu's herds and seized tens of thousands of our cattle and sheep—that is why we demand compensation."
translations.idiomatic: At Qinghai, Huang Rensu negotiated peace, yet the border garrisons took no precautions; Cui Zhibian rode straight to the yabghu's pastures and drove off tens of thousands of our cattle and sheep—that is what we seek redress for."

sentences.zh: 使使者固請，元振固言不可許，後從之。

translations.literal: The envoy pressed hard; Yuanzhen firmly said it could not be granted; afterward [the court] followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy pressed his suit, but Yuanzhen insisted it must not be granted; in the end the court took his side.

sentences.zh: 欽陵專國久，常居中制事，諸弟皆領方面兵，而贊婆專東境幾三十年，為邊患。

translations.literal: Qinling had monopolized the state long, always controlling affairs from the center; his younger brothers all commanded regional armies, while Zanpo held the eastern frontier nearly thirty years—a border scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Qinling had long monopolized power, governing from the center while his brothers each held regional armies; Zanpo alone commanded the eastern marches for nearly thirty years and was the scourge of the border.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆才略沈雄，眾憚之。

translations.literal: The brothers were all deep in talent and strategy; the masses feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all formidable in talent and strategy, and the people feared them.

sentences.zh: 器弩悉弄既長，欲自得國，漸不平，乃與大臣論巖等圖去之。

translations.literal: When Qinu Sennong had grown up, wishing to rule in his own right, he grew increasingly resentful and, with ministers such as Lun Yan, plotted to remove [Qinling].
translations.idiomatic: When Qinu Sennong came of age and wished to rule in his own right, resentment grew; he joined ministers such as Lun Yan in plotting Qinling's removal.

sentences.zh: 欽陵方提兵居外，贊普托言獵，即勒兵執其親黨二千餘人殺之，發使者召欽陵、贊婆，欽陵不受命，贊普自討之。

translations.literal: Qinling was just leading troops abroad; the tsenpo, feigning a hunt, immediately mustered troops, seized and killed more than two thousand of his intimates, and sent envoys summoning Qinling and Zanpo; Qinling refused the command, and the tsenpo personally campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Qinling was abroad with the army when the tsenpo, under pretense of a hunt, mustered troops, seized and killed more than two thousand of his partisans, and sent envoys to summon Qinling and Zanpo. Qinling refused; the tsenpo marched against him in person.

sentences.zh: 未戰，欽陵兵潰，乃自殺，左右殉而死者百餘人。

translations.literal: Before battle Qinling's army collapsed; he then killed himself, and over a hundred close attendants died following him.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle was joined Qinling's army collapsed; he took his own life, and more than a hundred attendants died with him.

sentences.zh: 贊婆以所部及兄子莽布支等款塞，遣羽林飛騎迎勞，擢贊婆特進、輔國大將軍、歸德郡王，莽布支左羽林大將軍、安國公，皆賜鐵券，禮尉良厚。

translations.literal: Zanpo, with his division and his brother's son Mangbuzhi and others, submitted to the passes; the court sent Flying Cavalry of the Forest of Plumes to welcome and reward them; Zanpo was promoted to extraordinary deputy and Grand General Who Assists the State, made Prince of Guide commandery; Mangbuzhi made Left General of the Forest of Plumes and Duke of Anguo; all were granted iron certificates; courtesy and comfort were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Zanpo, with his troops and his brother's son Mangbuzhi and others, surrendered at the passes. The court sent Flying Cavalry of the Forest of Plumes to welcome them. Zanpo was made extraordinary deputy minister, Grand General Who Assists the State, and Prince of Guide; Mangbuzhi was made Left General of the Forest of Plumes and Duke of Anguo. Both received iron certificates, and the court treated them with generous courtesy.

sentences.zh: 贊婆即領部兵戍河源，死，贈安西大都護。

translations.literal: Zanpo then led his troops to garrison Heyuan; on his death he was posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zanpo then led his troops to garrison Heyuan; when he died he was posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 又遣左肅政臺御史大夫魏元忠為隴右諸軍大總管，率隴右諸軍大使唐休璟出討。

translations.literal: The court also sent Left Censor of the Bureau of Rectitude Wei Yuanzhong as Grand Commander of all Longyou armies, leading Longyou army commissioners such as Tang Xiujing out to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The court also appointed Wei Yuanzhong, censor-in-chief of the Left Bureau of Rectitude, grand commander of all Longyou armies, and sent him with Longyou commissioners such as Tang Xiujing on campaign.

sentences.zh: 方虜攻涼州，休璟擊之，斬首二千級。

translations.literal: Just as the barbarians attacked Liangzhou, Xiujing struck them and beheaded two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: While the invaders were attacking Liangzhou, Xiujing struck them and took two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 於是論彌薩來朝請和。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lun Misa came to court seeking peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Lun Misa came to court to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 贊普自將萬騎攻悉州，都督陳大慈四戰皆克。

translations.literal: The tsenpo himself led ten thousand horsemen to attack Xizhou; Protector Chen Daci won all four engagements.
translations.idiomatic: The tsenpo himself led ten thousand horsemen against Xizhou; Protector Chen Daci won all four battles.

sentences.zh: 明年，乃獻馬、黃金求昏。

translations.literal: The next year they offered horses and gold seeking marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they offered horses and gold and sought a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 而虜南屬帳皆叛，贊普自討，死於軍。

translations.literal: But all southern subject clans rebelled; the tsenpo campaigned against them personally and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: But all the southern subject clans rebelled; the tsenpo campaigned against them in person and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 諸子爭立，國人立棄隸蹜贊為贊普，始七歲，使者來告喪，且求盟。

translations.literal: Sons contended for the throne; the people enthroned Qilisuzan as tsenpo, only seven years old; envoys came to announce mourning and also request alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Sons fought over the succession; the people enthroned Qilisuzan as tsenpo, a child of seven. Envoys came to announce the death and also to seek alliance.

sentences.zh: 又使大臣悉董熱固求昏，未報。

translations.literal: They also sent the great minister Sidongre firmly to seek marriage; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent the great minister Sidongre to press a marriage request; the court gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 會監察御史李知古建討姚州蠻，削吐蕃向導，詔發劍南募士擊之。

translations.literal: At this time Supervising Censor Li Zhigu proposed attacking the Yao prefecture barbarians and cutting off Tibetan guides; an edict ordered raising soldiers from Jiannan to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Supervising Censor Li Zhigu proposed campaigning against the Yao prefecture tribes and cutting off Tibetan guides; an edict ordered Jiannan to raise troops and attack.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋以情輸虜，殺知古，屍以祭天，進攻蜀漢。

translations.literal: A barbarian chieftain disclosed intelligence to the invaders; they killed Zhigu and offered his corpse to Heaven; they advanced to attack Shu and Han.
translations.idiomatic: A tribal chieftain betrayed intelligence to the Tibetans; they killed Zhigu and offered his body to Heaven, then advanced against Shu and Han.

sentences.zh: 詔靈武監軍右臺御史唐九征為姚巂道討擊使，率兵擊之。

translations.literal: An edict made Lingwu military overseer and Right Bureau Censor Tang Jiuzheng commander of the Yao-Exi punitive route, leading troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Tang Jiuzheng, military overseer at Lingwu and censor of the Right Bureau, commander of the Yao-Exi punitive route, to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 虜以鐵縆梁漾、濞二水，通西洱蠻，築城戍之。

translations.literal: The barbarians spanned the Yang and Bi rivers with iron chains to link with the western Erhai barbarians and built walled forts to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans bridged the Yang and Bi rivers with iron chains to reach the western Erhai tribes and built fortified towns to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 九征毀縆夷城，建鐵柱於滇池以勒功。

translations.literal: Jiuzheng destroyed the Gengyi city, and erected an iron pillar at Dianchi to record merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzheng destroyed the Gengyi stronghold and erected an iron pillar at Dianchi to commemorate the victory.

sentences.zh: 中宗，還其昏使。
