translations.literal: Under Zhongzong, [the court] sent back the marriage envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong the court sent back the Tibetan marriage envoys.

sentences.zh: 或言彼來逆公主，且習聞華言，宜勿遣，帝以中國當以信結夷狄，不許。

translations.literal: Some said they came to receive the princess rebelliously and had grown accustomed to Chinese speech—she should not be sent; the emperor held that the Middle Kingdom ought to bind barbarians with faith and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that the Tibetans came to receive the princess with hostile intent and already understood Chinese—she should not be sent. The emperor held that the Middle Kingdom must bind its neighbors with good faith and would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 明年，吐蕃更遣使者納貢，祖母可敦又遣宗俄請昏。

translations.literal: The next year Tibet again sent envoys to pay tribute; the grandmother khatun again sent Zonge to request marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Tibet again sent tribute envoys, and the grandmother khatun again sent Zonge to request marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝以雍王守禮女為金城公主妻之，吐蕃遣尚贊咄名悉臘等逆公主。

translations.literal: The emperor gave Prince Yong Shouli's daughter as Princess Jincheng in marriage; Tibet sent Shang Zanzhuo Ming Xila and others to meet the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Prince Yong Li Shouli's daughter as Princess Jincheng in marriage; Tibet sent Shang Zanzhuo Ming Xila and others to meet the bride.

sentences.zh: 帝念主幼，賜錦繒別數萬，雜伎諸工悉從，給龜茲樂。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that the princess was young, bestowed several tens of thousands of silks and brocades apart [from the dowry], all sorts of artisans and performers following her, and supplied Kuchean music.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that the princess was still young, the emperor bestowed tens of thousands of brocades and silks beyond the regular dowry, sent every sort of artisan and performer with her, and provided Kuchean musicians.

sentences.zh: 詔左衛大將軍楊矩持節送。

translations.literal: An edict made Left Guard General Yang Ju hold credentials to escort her.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Left Guard General Yang Ju to escort her bearing imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 帝為幸始平，帳飲，引群臣及虜使者宴，酒所帝悲涕噓欷，為赦始平縣，罪死皆免，賜民繇賦一年，改縣為金城，鄉曰鳳池，里曰愴別。

translations.literal: The emperor made a progress to Shiping, pitched tents for drinking, led the officials and barbarian envoys to banquet; at the drinking the emperor wept and sobbed; he pardoned Shiping county—all death sentences remitted; the people granted corvée and tax for one year; the county was renamed Jincheng, the township Fengchi, the lane Cangbie ("parting sorrow").
translations.idiomatic: The emperor traveled to Shiping and held a tent feast, leading officials and Tibetan envoys in banquet. Over the wine he wept aloud, pardoned Shiping county and remitted all capital sentences, granted the people a year's relief from corvée and tax, renamed the county Jincheng, a township Fengchi ("phoenix pool"), and a lane Cangbie ("parting sorrow").

sentences.zh: 公主至吐蕃，自築城以居。

translations.literal: When the princess reached Tibet she built her own walled town to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess reached Tibet she built her own walled settlement to live in.

sentences.zh: 拜矩鄯州都督。

translations.literal: Ju was appointed Protector-General of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was appointed protector-general of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃外雖和而陰銜怒，即厚餉矩，請河西九曲為公主湯沐，矩表與其地。

translations.literal: Outwardly Tibet was friendly yet secretly nursed anger; they richly bribed Ju, requesting the Nine Bendings of the Yellow River as the princess's fief for hot-spring baths; Ju memorialized and ceded the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Tibet was at peace but secretly harbored resentment; they lavished gifts on Ju and asked for the Nine Bendings of the Yellow River in Hexi as the princess's bath fief. Ju memorialized and surrendered the land.

sentences.zh: 九曲者，水甘草良，宜畜牧，近與唐接。

translations.literal: The Nine Bendings had good sweet grass and were fit for pasturage, close to Tang territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Bendings offered sweet grass and good pasture and lay close to Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 自是虜益張雄，易入寇。

translations.literal: From this the barbarians grew more aggressive and raids became easier.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Tibetans grew bolder and raids came more easily.

sentences.zh: 玄宗，其相坌達延上書宰相，請載盟文，定境於河源，丐左散騎常侍解琬涖盟。

translations.literal: Under Xuanzong, his minister Benduyan wrote to the Grand Chancellor, asking to inscribe the alliance text and fix the border at Heyuan, begging Left Regular Attendant Xie Wan to supervise the oath.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong, his minister Benduyan wrote to the chief ministers, asking that the alliance text be inscribed and the border fixed at Heyuan, and begging Left Regular Attendant Xie Wan to preside over the oath.

sentences.zh: 帝令姚崇等報書，命琬持神龍誓往。

translations.literal: The emperor had Yao Chong and others reply; he ordered Wan to bear the Divine Dragon Oath and go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Yao Chong and others answer in writing and ordered Wan to carry the Divine Dragon Oath and go.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃亦遣尚欽藏、御史名悉臘獻載辭。

translations.literal: Tibet also sent Shang Qinzang and Censor Ming Xila to present the inscribed oath words.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet also sent Shang Qinzang and Censor Ming Xila to present the inscribed oath text.

sentences.zh: 未及定，坌達延將兵十萬寇臨洮，入攻蘭、渭，掠監馬。

translations.literal: Before the terms were settled Benduyan led a hundred thousand troops to raid Lintao, entered to attack Lan and Wei, and carried off corral horses.
translations.idiomatic: Before terms were settled Benduyan led a hundred thousand men against Lintao, pushed into Lan and Wei, and drove off the government herds.

sentences.zh: 楊矩懼，自殺。

translations.literal: Yang Ju was afraid and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ju, in fear, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 有詔薛訥為隴右防禦使，與王晙等並力擊。

translations.literal: An edict made Xue Ne Longyou defense commissioner; he and Wang Jun and others jointly struck.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xue Ne Longyou defense commissioner; he and Wang Jun and others joined forces to attack.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下詔自將討之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and issued an edict to lead the campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, enraged, issued an edict to lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 會晙等戰武階，斬首萬七千，獲馬羊無慮二十萬。

translations.literal: At that time Jun and others fought at Wujie; heads taken seventeen thousand; horses and sheep captured, well over two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Jun and the others fought at Wujie, taking seventeen thousand heads and no fewer than two hundred thousand horses and sheep.

sentences.zh: 又戰長子，豐安軍使王海賓戰死。

translations.literal: They fought again at Changzi; Feng'an army commissioner Wang Haibin died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again at Changzi; Feng'an army commissioner Wang Haibin fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 乘之，虜大敗，眾奔突不能去，相枕藉死，洮水為不流。

translations.literal: Pressing the advantage, the barbarians were utterly defeated; the masses fled and could not escape; they lay dead piled upon one another; the Tao River ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory, they routed the Tibetans utterly; the fugitives could not escape and lay dead in heaps; the Tao River was said to have stopped flowing.

sentences.zh: 帝乃罷行。

translations.literal: The emperor then canceled the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then canceled his march.

sentences.zh: 詔紫微舍人倪若水臨按軍實戰功，且吊祭戰亡士，敕州縣並瘞吐蕃露胔。

translations.literal: An edict made Purple Micro Attendant Ni Ruoshui inspect on the spot the army's battle merit and also mourn the fallen soldiers; prefectures and counties were to bury together the Tibetan corpses exposed in the open.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Purple Micro Attendant Ni Ruoshui to verify battle merit on the spot, mourn the fallen, and order prefectures and counties jointly to bury the Tibetan dead left exposed in the field.

sentences.zh: 宰相建言：「吐蕃本以河為境，以公主故，乃橋河築城，置獨山、九曲二軍，距積石二百里。

translations.literal: The Grand Chancellor memorialized: "Tibet originally took the river as its border; because of the princess it bridged the river and built cities, establishing the Dushan and Nine Bendings armies two hundred li from Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers memorialized: "Tibet originally took the river as its border; because of the princess it bridged the river and built fortresses, establishing the Dushan and Nine Bendings garrisons two hundred li from Jishi.

sentences.zh: 今既負約，請毀橋，復守河如約。」

translations.literal: Now that they have broken faith, we ask to destroy the bridges and again guard the river as agreed."
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have broken faith, we ask that the bridges be destroyed and the river again held as the treaty provides."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 遣左驍衛郎將尉遲瑰使吐蕃，慰安公主。

translations.literal: They sent Left Martial Guard Commandant Yuchi Gui as envoy to Tibet to comfort and reassure the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Left Martial Guard Commandant Yuchi Gui as envoy to Tibet to comfort the princess.

sentences.zh: 然小小入犯邊無閑歲，於是郭知運、王君㚟相繼節度隴右、河西，一以捍之。

translations.literal: Yet petty raids on the border came year after year with no idle season; thereupon Guo Zhiyun and Wang Junzhi in succession became commissioners of Longyou and Hexi, using all means to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty border raids came year after year without respite; thereupon Guo Zhiyun and Wang Junzhi in succession took command of Longyou and Hexi and devoted themselves to holding the line.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣宗俄因子到洮水祭戰死士，且請和。

translations.literal: Tibet sent Zong'e's son to the Tao River to sacrifice to the fallen soldiers and also request peace.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent Zong'e's son to the Tao River to sacrifice to the war dead and also to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 然恃盛強，求與天子敵國，語悖傲。

translations.literal: Yet relying on their power they sought parity with the Son of Heaven as a rival state; their words were perverse and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet relying on their strength they demanded to be treated as the Son of Heaven's peer; their language was insolent and perverse.

sentences.zh: 使者至臨洮，詔不內。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Lintao, an edict denied entry.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached Lintao, an edict refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 金城公主上書求聽脩好，且言贊普君臣欲與天子共署誓刻。

translations.literal: Princess Jincheng memorialized asking permission to renew good relations, and also stated that the tsenpo and his ministers wished to affix their names jointly with the Son of Heaven on oath inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jincheng memorialized asking leave to restore good relations, and said that the tsenpo and his ministers wished to affix their names with the Son of Heaven on a new oath stone.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃又遣使者上書言：「孝和皇帝嘗賜盟，是時唐宰相豆盧欽望、魏元忠、李嶠、紀處訥等凡二十二人及吐蕃君臣同誓。

translations.literal: Tibet again sent an envoy memorializing: "Emperor Xiaohé once bestowed alliance; at that time Tang Grand Chancellors Dou Lu Qinwang, Wei Yuanzhong, Li Qiao, Ji Chun'e and twenty-two in all, with Tibetan ruler and ministers, swore together.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet again sent an envoy who wrote: "Emperor Xiaohé once granted alliance; at that time Tang chancellors Dou Lu Qinwang, Wei Yuanzhong, Li Qiao, Ji Chun'e, and twenty-two in all, together with Tibetan ruler and ministers, swore the oath.

sentences.zh: 孝和皇帝崩，太上皇嗣位，脩睦如舊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaohé died the Retired Emperor succeeded; amity was maintained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaohé died the Retired Emperor succeeded, and amity continued as before.

sentences.zh: 然唐宰相在誓刻者皆歿，今宰相不及前約，故須再盟。

translations.literal: Yet the Tang chancellors named on the oath stone have all died; today's chancellors do not match the former covenant; therefore a new oath is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Tang chancellors named on the oath stone have all died, and today's ministers do not match the former covenant; therefore a new oath is required.

sentences.zh: 比使論乞力等前後七輩往，未蒙開許，且張玄表、李知古將兵侵暴甥國，故違誓而戰。

translations.literal: Envoy Lun Qili and others, seven missions before and after, came without receiving approval; moreover Zhang Xuanbiao and Li Zhigu led troops to invade and ravage the nephew-state—therefore we broke oath and fought.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys such as Lun Qili came in seven successive missions without receiving approval; moreover Zhang Xuanbiao and Li Zhigu led troops to ravage the nephew-state—therefore we broke the oath and fought.

sentences.zh: 今舅許湔貸前惡，歸於大和，甥既堅定，然不重盟為未信，要待新誓也。

translations.literal: Now the uncle grants pardon for past crimes and returns to great harmony; the nephew is already firm, yet without renewing the oath there is no trust—we require a new oath.
translations.idiomatic: Now the uncle grants pardon for past wrongs and returns to great harmony; the nephew is already resolute, yet without renewing the oath there can be no trust—we must await a new oath.

sentences.zh: 甥自總國事，不牽於下，欲使百姓久安。

translations.literal: Since the nephew has governed the state I am not bound below and wish the people long peace.
translations.idiomatic: Since the nephew has governed the state I am not swayed by subordinates and wish the people lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 舅雖及和，而意不專，於言何益？」

translations.literal: Though the uncle reaches peace his intent is not single-minded—of what use are words?"
translations.idiomatic: Though the uncle speaks of peace his intent is not wholehearted—what good are words alone?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「舅責乞力徐集兵，且兵以新故相代，非集也。

translations.literal: Again they said: "The uncle blamed Qili for gathering troops, yet troops are replaced old and new in rotation—not a massing.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "The uncle blamed Qili for massing troops, yet troops rotate in relief of old by new—that is not a gathering.

sentences.zh: 往者疆埸自白水皆為閑壤，昨郭將軍屯兵而城之，故甥亦城。

translations.literal: Formerly the frontier from Baishui was all idle land; yesterday General Guo stationed troops and walled; therefore the nephew also walled.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the frontier from Baishui was all idle land; yesterday General Guo stationed troops and built walls, so the nephew built walls as well.

sentences.zh: 假令二國和，以迎送；

translations.literal: Suppose the two states are at peace, to receive and send envoys;
translations.idiomatic: If the two states are at peace, they may receive and send envoys;

sentences.zh: 有如不通，因以守境。

translations.literal: if communication should fail, then to hold the border by that means.
translations.idiomatic: if communication should fail, then to hold the border accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又疑與突厥骨咄祿善者，舊與通聘，即日舅甥如初，不與交矣。

translations.literal: Also suspecting friendship with the Turk Kutlug, though we formerly exchanged envoys with him—from this day uncle and nephew are as at first; we shall not associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: They also suspected friendship with the Turk Kutlug; though we once exchanged envoys with him, from this day uncle and nephew are as before and we shall have no dealings with him.

sentences.zh: 因奉寶瓶、杯以獻。」

translations.literal: Thereupon presenting a treasure flask and cups as tribute."
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon presented a treasure flask and cups as tribute."

sentences.zh: 帝謂昔已和親，有成言，尋前盟可矣，不許復誓。

translations.literal: The emperor said alliance by marriage had already been made with established words; searching the former oath sufficed—he would not permit a renewed oath.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said that marriage alliances had long since been made with binding words; the former oath would suffice, and he would not permit a renewed oath.

sentences.zh: 禮其使而遣，且厚賜贊普，自是歲朝貢不犯邊。

translations.literal: They treated the envoy with ritual and dismissed him, and richly bestowed the tsenpo; from this yearly tribute came without border raids.
translations.idiomatic: The court treated the envoy with ceremony and sent him home, richly rewarding the tsenpo; from then on yearly tribute came and the border was not violated.

sentences.zh: 十年，攻小勃律國，其王沒謹忙詒書北庭節度使張孝嵩曰：「勃律，唐西門。

translations.literal: In the tenth year [they] attacked Lesser Bolü; its king Mujinmang sent a letter to Beiting commissioner Zhang Xiaosong saying: "Bolü is Tang's western gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Tibet attacked Lesser Bolü; its king Mujinmang wrote Beiting commissioner Zhang Xiaosong: "Bolü is Tang's western gate.

sentences.zh: 失之，則西方諸國皆墯吐蕃，都護圖之。」

translations.literal: Lose it and all western states will fall to Tibet—Protector-General, plan for this."
translations.idiomatic: Lose it and every western state will fall to Tibet—Protector-General, take thought for this."

sentences.zh: 孝嵩聽許，遣疏勒副使張思禮以步騎四千晝夜馳，與謹忙兵夾擊吐蕃，死者數萬，多取鎧仗、馬羊，復九城故地。

translations.literal: Xiaosong heeded the plea and sent Sule deputy commissioner Zhang Silu with four thousand infantry and cavalry day and night at forced march; together with Jinmang's troops they struck Tibet from both sides; tens of thousands died; they took much armor, horses and sheep and recovered the nine walled towns' former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosong agreed and sent Sule deputy commissioner Zhang Silu with four thousand foot and horse at forced march day and night; together with Jinmang's troops they struck Tibet from both flanks. Tens of thousands perished; they seized much armor, horses, and sheep and recovered the nine walled towns' former territory.

sentences.zh: 始勃律王來朝，父事帝。

translations.literal: At first the Bolü king had come to court and addressed the emperor as father.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the king of Bolü had come to court and addressed the emperor as father.

sentences.zh: 還國，置綏遠軍以捍吐蕃，故歲常戰。

translations.literal: Returning home he established the Pacification-far Army to hold off Tibet; therefore they fought yearly.
translations.idiomatic: On returning home he established the Pacify-the-Distance Army to hold off Tibet, and they fought every year.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃每曰：「我非利若國，我假道攻四鎮爾。」

translations.literal: Tibet would always say: "We do not covet your state; we borrow the road to strike the Four Garrisons."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet would always say, "We do not covet your kingdom; we only borrow the road to strike the Four Garrisons."

sentences.zh: 及是，累歲不出兵。

translations.literal: At this, for successive years they sent out no troops.
translations.idiomatic: After this, for years they sent out no armies.

sentences.zh: 於是隴右節度使王君㚟請深入取償。

translations.literal: Thereupon Longyou commissioner Wang Junzhi requested a deep strike to take compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Longyou commissioner Wang Junzhi asked to strike deep into Tibet for compensation.

sentences.zh: 十二年，破吐蕃，獻俘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they broke Tibet and presented captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year they defeated Tibet and presented captives at court.

sentences.zh: 後二年，悉諾邏兵入大斗拔谷，遂攻甘州，火鄉聚。

translations.literal: Two years later Sinuoluo's troops entered the Great Douba valley, then attacked Ganzhou and burned village clusters.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Sinuoluo's army entered the Great Douba valley, then attacked Ganzhou and burned the countryside.

sentences.zh: 王君㚟勒兵避其銳，不戰。

translations.literal: Wang Junzhi drew up troops to avoid their sharp edge and did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junzhi drew up his troops to avoid their spearhead and did not give battle.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，吐蕃皸凍如積，乃逾積石軍趨西道以歸。

translations.literal: Just then heavy snow fell; Tibet's frostbite piled like heaps; they then crossed Jishi army and headed the western route to return.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell; Tibetan dead of frostbite piled like heaps; they then crossed past Jishi garrison and took the western route homeward.

sentences.zh: 君㚟豫遣諜出塞，燒野草皆盡，悉諾邏頓大非川，無所牧，馬死過半。

translations.literal: Junzhi had beforehand sent spies beyond the passes; they burned all the wild grass; Sinuoluo halted at the Da Fei River with nothing to pasture; more than half the horses died.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhi had sent spies ahead beyond the passes to burn all the pasture; Sinuoluo halted at the Da Fei River with nothing to graze, and more than half his horses died.

sentences.zh: 君㚟率秦州都督張景順約賫窮躡，出青海西，方冰合，師乘而度。

translations.literal: Junzhi led Qinzhou protector-general Zhang Jingshun to pursue to the limit; they went out west of Qinghai; the ice had just formed and the army crossed riding it.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhi led Qinzhou protector-general Zhang Jingshun in relentless pursuit west of Qinghai; the ice had just frozen, and the army crossed on it.

sentences.zh: 於時虜已逾大非山，留輜重疲弱濱海，君㚟縱兵俘以旋。

translations.literal: By then the barbarians had already crossed Mount Da Fei; they left baggage and the weak along the lake shore; Junzhi unleashed troops, captured them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: By then the enemy had crossed Mount Da Fei, leaving baggage and the weak along the lakeshore; Junzhi unleashed his troops, took them captive, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時中書令張說以吐蕃出入數十年，勝負略相當，甘、涼、河、鄯之人奉調發困甚，願聽其和。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Secretariat Zhang Yue—because Tibet had raided in and out for decades, victory and defeat roughly equal, and the people of Gan, Liang, He, and Shan were exhausted furnishing corvée and levies—wished to permit peace.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretariat Zhang Yue urged that after decades of Tibetan raids, with victory and defeat roughly balanced, the people of Gan, Liang, He, and Shan were exhausted by levies and corvée, and wished the court to permit peace.

sentences.zh: 帝方寵君㚟，不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor was then favoring Junzhi and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then favoring Junzhi and would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，悉諾邏恭祿、燭龍莽布支入陷瓜州，毀其城，執刺史田元獻及君㚟父，遂攻玉門軍，圍常樂，不能拔，回寇安西，副都護趙頤貞擊卻之。

translations.literal: Before long Sinuoluo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi entered and took Guazhou, destroyed its walls, seized prefect Tian Yuanxian and Junzhi's father; they then attacked Yumen army, besieged Changle but could not take it; turned back to raid Anxi; vice protector-general Zhao Yizhen repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sinuoluo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi took Guazhou, destroyed its walls, and seized prefect Tian Yuanxian and Junzhi's father; they then attacked Yumen garrison and besieged Changle without success, turned back to raid Anxi, and vice protector-general Zhao Yizhen drove them off.

sentences.zh: 會君㚟為回紇所殺，功不遂。

translations.literal: Just then Junzhi was killed by the Uyghurs; success was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: But Junzhi was killed by the Uyghurs, and the campaign came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝乃用蕭嵩為河西節度使，左金吾將軍張守珪瓜州刺史，復城之。

translations.literal: The emperor then appointed Xiao Song Hexi commissioner, Left Golden Crow Guard General Zhang Shougui Guazhou prefect, and restored the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed Xiao Song Hexi commissioner and Left Golden Crow Guard General Zhang Shougui prefect of Guazhou, and the city was rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 嵩縱反間，殺悉諾邏恭祿。

translations.literal: Song used a counter-intelligence plot and killed Sinuoluo Gonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Song used a counter-intelligence stratagem and had Sinuoluo Gonglu killed.

sentences.zh: 明年，大將悉末朗攻瓜州，守珪擊走之；

translations.literal: The next year great commander Ximolang attacked Guazhou; Shougui struck and drove him off;
translations.idiomatic: The next year the great commander Ximolang attacked Guazhou; Shougui struck and drove him off;

sentences.zh: 鄯州都督張志亮又戰青海西，破大莫門城，焚橐它橋；

translations.literal: Shanzhou protector-general Zhang Zhiliang again fought west of Qinghai, took the city of Damomen, and burned the Tuota bridge;
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhou protector-general Zhang Zhiliang again fought west of Qinghai, took Damomen city, and burned the Tuota bridge;

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使杜賓客以強弩四千射虜，破之祁連城下，斬副將一，上級五千首。

translations.literal: Longyou commissioner Du Binke with four thousand strong crossbows shot the barbarians, defeated them below Qilian walled city, beheaded one vice commander, and sent up five thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou commissioner Du Binke with four thousand powerful crossbows shot the enemy, routed them below Qilian fortress, beheaded one vice commander, and reported five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 虜敗，慟而走山。

translations.literal: The barbarians were defeated and fled wailing into the hills.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans were defeated and fled wailing into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 又明年，守珪率伊、沙等州兵破虜大同軍；

translations.literal: The next year Shougui led Yi, Sha, and other prefecture troops and broke the barbarians' Datong army;
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shougui led troops from Yi, Sha, and other prefectures and defeated the Tibetan Datong garrison;

sentences.zh: 又信安王祎出隴西，拔石堡城，即之置振武軍，獻俘於廟。

translations.literal: Also Prince Xin'an Wang Yi marched out Longxi, took Shibao walled city, immediately established Zhenwu Army there, and presented captives at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Wang Yi also marched out of Longxi, took Shibao fortress, immediately established the Quell-the-Barbarians Army there, and presented captives at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 帝以書賜將軍裴旻曰：「敢有掩戰功不及賞者，士自陳，將吏皆斬。

translations.literal: The emperor with a letter bestowed on General Pei Min: "If anyone conceals battle merit and fails to reward it, soldiers may state it themselves; officers and officials shall all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote to General Pei Min: "If anyone conceals battle merit and fails to reward it, let the soldiers report it themselves; the officers shall all be executed.

sentences.zh: 戰有逗留，舉隊如軍法。

translations.literal: If in battle there is delay or tarrying, the whole unit is punished according to military law.
translations.idiomatic: Any delay in battle was punished—entire units held to account under military law.

sentences.zh: 能禽其王者，授大將軍。」

translations.literal: Whoever could capture their king was appointed Grand General."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever captured the Tibetan king would be made Grand General."

sentences.zh: 於是士益奮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers strove all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The troops fought all the harder thereafter.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃令曩骨委書塞下，言：「論莽熱、論泣熱皆萬人將，以贊普命，謝都督刺史：二國有舅甥好，昨彌不弄羌、党項交構二國，故失歡，此不聽，唐亦不應聽。」

translations.literal: The Tibetans had Nanggu entrust a letter to the frontier, saying: "Lun Mangre and Lun Qire are each commanders of ten thousand; by the zanpu's order they thank the governors and prefects: the two states have uncle-nephew friendship; recently the Mibu Nong Qiang and the Tangut tribes stirred strife between the two states, so goodwill was lost—this we will not heed, and Tang should not heed it either."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent Nanggu to write to the frontier garrisons, saying, "Lun Mangre and Lun Qire, each commanding ten thousand men, bring the zanpu's thanks to the governors and prefects. Our two states share the tie of uncle and nephew, but lately the Mibu Nong Qiang and the Tangut tribes have sown discord between us and goodwill has soured. Neither side should listen to such agents of strife—including Tang."

sentences.zh: 都督遣腹心吏與曩骨還議盟事。

translations.literal: The governor dispatched a trusted clerk with Nanggu to return and discuss alliance matters.
translations.idiomatic: The governor sent a trusted clerk back with Nanggu to negotiate the treaty.

sentences.zh: 曩骨，猶千牛官也。

translations.literal: Nanggu was like the Thousand-Oxen Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Nanggu held a rank comparable to the Palace's Thousand-Ox attendant.

sentences.zh: 於是忠王友皇甫惟明並言約和便。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Zhong's friend Huangfu Weiming together spoke that treaty and peace were expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Then Huangfu Weiming, a companion of Prince Zhong, joined others in urging that peace talks would serve both courts well.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「贊普向上書悖慢，朕必滅之，毋議和！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The zanpu in his letter upward to Us was insolent and remiss; We shall destroy him—do not discuss peace!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The zanpu's letter to the throne was brazen and insolent. I shall destroy him—no talk of peace!"

sentences.zh: 惟明曰：「昔贊普幼，是必邊將好功之人為之，以激怒陛下。

translations.literal: Weiming said: "Formerly the zanpu was young; this must have been done by frontier generals who love merit, to provoke Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Weiming replied, "When the zanpu was still young, frontier officers hungry for glory must have written that letter to provoke Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 且二國交惡必興師，師興則隱盜財利，詐功級，希陛下過賞以甘心焉。

translations.literal: Moreover when the two states turn hostile troops are surely raised; when troops are raised they secretly steal wealth and profit, feign merit tallies, hoping Your Majesty will over-reward to their satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: When the two powers fall out, war follows; and when war follows, men steal and loot in secret, pad the body counts, and angle for excessive rewards from Your Majesty to line their pockets.

sentences.zh: 今河西、隴右貲耗力窮，陛下幸詔金城公主許贊普約，以紓邊患，息民之上策也。」

translations.literal: Now Hexi and Longyou are drained of goods and strength exhausted; Your Majesty would do well to order the Princess Jincheng to permit the zanpu a treaty, to ease frontier troubles—the supreme policy to give the people rest."
translations.idiomatic: Hexi and Longyou are spent of treasure and exhausted of strength. Your Majesty would do well to have Princess Jincheng approve a treaty with the zanpu—to ease the border and give the people rest. That is the best policy."

sentences.zh: 帝采其言，敕惟明及中人張元方往聘，以書賜公主。

translations.literal: The emperor took his words, ordered Weiming and the eunuch Zhang Yuanfang to go on an embassy, with a letter bestowed on the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this counsel and ordered Weiming and the eunuch Zhang Yuanfang on an embassy, with a letter for the princess.

sentences.zh: 惟明見贊普言天子意，贊普大喜，因悉出貞觀以來書詔示惟明，厚饋獻。

translations.literal: Weiming saw the zanpu and stated the Son of Heaven's intent; the zanpu was greatly pleased, and therefore brought out in full all letters and edicts since Zhenguan to show Weiming, with lavish gifts presented.
translations.idiomatic: Weiming presented the emperor's wishes to the zanpu, who was overjoyed and brought out every letter and edict since the Zhenguan era to show him, lavish with gifts.

sentences.zh: 使名悉臘隨使者入朝，奉表言：「甥，先帝舅顯親也。

translations.literal: He sent one named Xila with the envoys to enter court and present a memorial saying: "Your nephew, the Former Emperor's nephew by kin manifest and honored.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xila with the embassy to court with a memorial: "Your nephew—I am the Former Emperor's nephew by blood, kin manifest and honored.

sentences.zh: 曩為張玄表、李知古交鬥，遂成大釁。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhang Xuanbiao and Li Zhigu quarreled and fought, and thus a great breach arose.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zhang Xuanbiao and Li Zhigu quarreled and war followed—a great breach.

sentences.zh: 甥以文成、金城公主，敢失禮乎？

translations.literal: Your nephew, for Princess Wencheng and Princess Jincheng, dares fail in courtesy?
translations.idiomatic: With Princess Wencheng and Princess Jincheng between us, how dare your nephew fail in courtesy?

sentences.zh: 特以沖幼，枉為邊將讒亂。

translations.literal: Only because young and tender, wrongly slandered and disturbed by frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: I was young and tender, and frontier generals slandered and misled me.

sentences.zh: 如蒙澄亮，死且萬足，千萬歲不敢先負盟。」

translations.literal: If We receive clarity and brightness, death itself would be more than enough; for ten thousand years We dare not first break the alliance."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will clear and forgive, death itself would be more than enough; for ten thousand years I dare not be the first to break our pact."

sentences.zh: 且獻怪寶。

translations.literal: He also presented curious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented rare and curious treasures.

sentences.zh: 使者至，帝御前殿，列羽林仗內之。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, the emperor received them in the front hall, with Feathered Forest guards arrayed within.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived, the emperor received them in the front hall, with Feathered Forest guards drawn up within.

sentences.zh: 悉臘略通華文，既宴與語，禮甚厚，賜紫服、金魚。

translations.literal: Xila had some grasp of written Chinese; after a banquet and conversation with him, courtesy was very generous, and he was granted purple robes and gold fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Xila had some command of written Chinese; after a banquet and conversation the court treated him with great honor, granting purple robes and a gold fish tally.

sentences.zh: 悉臘受服辭魚，曰：「國無是，不敢當。」

translations.literal: Xila accepted the robes but declined the fish, saying: "My state has not these; I dare not receive them."
translations.idiomatic: Xila accepted the robes but declined the fish tally, saying, "My country has no such custom; I dare not accept it."

sentences.zh: 帝遣御史大夫崔琳報聘。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Cui Lin on a return embassy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Cui Lin on a return embassy.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃又請交馬於赤嶺，互市於甘松嶺。

translations.literal: Tibet again requested horse exchange at Chiling and mutual markets at Gansong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet again asked to exchange horses at Chiling and to trade at Gansong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴光庭曰：「甘松中國阻，不如許赤嶺。」

translations.literal: Chief minister Pei Guangting said: "Gansong lies within China's barrier zones—better to permit Chiling."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Pei Guangting said, "Gansong lies within China's interior barriers—better to allow Chiling."

sentences.zh: 乃聽以赤嶺為界，表以大碑，刻約其上。

translations.literal: They then approved Chiling as the boundary, raised a great stele, and carved the treaty upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved Chiling as the border, set up a great stele, and carved the treaty upon it.

sentences.zh: 又請《五經》，敕秘書寫賜，並遣工部尚書李暠往聘，賜物萬計。

translations.literal: They also requested the Five Classics; an edict ordered the Secretariat to copy and bestow them, and Minister of Works Li Hao was sent on an embassy, with gifts numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested the Five Classics; the emperor ordered the Secretariat to copy and present them, and sent Minister of Works Li Hao on an embassy with gifts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣使謝，且言：「唐、吐蕃皆大國，今約和為久長計，恐邊吏有妄意者，請以使人對相曉敕，令昭然具知。」

translations.literal: Tibet sent envoys to give thanks, and also said: "Tang and Tibet are both great states; now the treaty is for a long-term plan—we fear frontier officials may have reckless intent; we request that envoys face each other and jointly proclaim the edict, so that all may know clearly."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent envoys to give thanks and said, "Tang and Tibet are both great powers; this treaty is meant to last. We fear some frontier officer may act rashly—let our envoys meet face to face and proclaim the edict together, so all may know it plainly."

sentences.zh: 帝又令金吾將軍李佺監赤嶺樹碑，詔張守珪與將軍李行祎、吐蕃使者莽布支分諭劍南、河西州縣曰：「自今二國和好，無相侵暴。」

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Golden Crow General Li Quan to oversee erecting the stele at Chiling, and decreed Zhang Shougui with General Li Xingyi and the Tibetan envoy Mangbuzhi to go separately and instruct the prefectures and counties of Jiannan and Hexi, saying: "From now the two states are in harmony; there shall be no mutual invasion or violence."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Golden Crow General Li Quan to supervise the stele at Chiling and decreed that Zhang Shougui, General Li Xingyi, and the Tibetan envoy Mangbuzhi should proclaim throughout Jiannan and Hexi: "From this day the two realms are at peace; neither shall invade the other."

sentences.zh: 乃使悉諾渤海納貢，並以幣器遍遺執政。

translations.literal: He then had Sinuo Bohai present tribute, and with silks and vessels bestowed gifts on all the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet then sent Sinuo Bohai with tribute and distributed silks and vessels among the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 明年，上寶器數百具，制冶詭殊，詔置提象門示群臣。

translations.literal: The next year they presented several hundred pieces of precious vessels, wrought in strange and marvelous fashion; an edict ordered them set out at the Elephant-Presentation Gate to show the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they presented several hundred precious vessels of bizarre and marvelous workmanship; the emperor ordered them displayed at the Elephant-Presentation Gate for the ministers to see.

sentences.zh: 其後吐蕃西擊勃律，勃律告急，帝諭令罷兵，不聽，卒殘其國。

translations.literal: Afterward Tibet attacked Boli in the west; Boli reported urgent distress; the emperor instructed them to cease troops, but they did not listen, and in the end ravaged that state.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tibet struck Boli in the west; Boli sent urgent appeals, and the emperor ordered them to withdraw, but they refused and in the end laid waste to the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 於是崔希逸為河西節度使，鎮涼州，故時疆畔皆樹壁守捉，希逸謂虜戍將乞力徐曰：「兩國約好，而守備不廢，云何？

translations.literal: Thereupon Cui Xiyi became Hexi military governor, stationed at Liangzhou; formerly along the border all had planted walls and guard posts; Xiyi said to the barbarian garrison general Qili Xu: "The two states have pledged friendship, yet defenses are not abandoned—how is this?
translations.idiomatic: Then Cui Xiyi became military governor of Hexi and took post at Liangzhou. Along the old frontier every post had walls and garrisons. Xiyi said to the Tibetan frontier commander Qili Xu, "Our two states have sworn friendship—why keep defenses up?

sentences.zh: 請皆罷，以便人。」

translations.literal: We request that all be abolished, to benefit the people."
translations.idiomatic: Let us abolish them all, for the people's ease."

sentences.zh: 乞力徐曰：「公忠誠，無不可，恐朝廷未皆信，脫掩吾不備，其可悔？」

translations.literal: Qili Xu said: "Your lordship is loyal and sincere—nothing is impossible; yet I fear the court may not all trust this; if you should strike when we are unprepared, what regret would there be?"
translations.idiomatic: Qili Xu replied, "Your sincerity leaves nothing impossible—but I fear the court may not all trust us. If you strike when we are unready, what regret would there be?"

sentences.zh: 希逸固邀，乃許。

translations.literal: Xiyi pressed him firmly, and he then agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi pressed him again and again, and at last he agreed.

sentences.zh: 即共刑白犬盟，而後悉徹障壁，虜畜牧被野。

translations.literal: Immediately they together sacrificed a white dog in covenant, and afterward wholly removed the barrier walls; the barbarians' herds and flocks covered the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: They sacrificed a white dog in covenant together, then tore down every barrier wall, and Tibetan herds spread across the open country.

sentences.zh: 明年，傔史孫誨奏事，妄言「虜無備，可取也」。

translations.literal: The next year the clerk Sun Hui reported at court, falsely saying "The barbarians are unprepared—they can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: The next year the clerk Sun Hui reported at court, falsely claiming, "The Tibetans are unprepared—we can strike them."

sentences.zh: 帝采之，詔內豎趙惠琮共往按狀。

translations.literal: The emperor took this up and decreed the inner attendant Zhao Huizong to go together and investigate the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him and ordered the eunuch Zhao Huizong to go with him and verify the report.

sentences.zh: 小人欲僥幸，至涼州，因共矯詔，詔希逸發兵襲破吐蕃青海上，斬獲不貲，乞力徐遁走。

translations.literal: Petty men wished for windfall gain; arriving at Liangzhou, they together forged an edict, ordering Xiyi to raise troops and strike, breaking the Tibetans on the Qinghai, beheadings and captures beyond reckoning; Qili Xu fled.
translations.idiomatic: These petty men sought their chance; reaching Liangzhou, they forged an edict together and ordered Xiyi to attack, routing the Tibetans on the Qinghai with slaughter and captures beyond count; Qili Xu fled.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃恚，不朝。

translations.literal: Tibet was enraged and ceased coming to court.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was furious and stopped sending tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，大入河西，希逸拒破之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year they invaded Hexi on a great scale; Xiyi repelled and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan they invaded Hexi in force; Xiyi repelled and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 鄯州都督杜希望又拔新城，更號威戎軍。

translations.literal: Shazhou governor Du Xiwang again took the new walled city and renamed it Weirong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shazhou governor Du Xiwang also took the new fortress and renamed it the Quell-the-Barbarians Army.

sentences.zh: 希逸顧失信，悒悒悵恨，召拜河南尹。

translations.literal: Xiyi, mindful that faith had been broken, was depressed and resentful; he was summoned and appointed Henan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi, brooding over the broken faith, grew despondent and bitter; he was recalled and made governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 既而與惠琮俱見犬崇，疑而死，誨亦及它誅。

translations.literal: Before long he and Huizong together saw a dog howling; in suspicion he died; Hui also met other punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he and Huizong both saw a dog baying at the moon; Xiyi took it as an omen and died of anxiety, and Hui was executed along with others.

sentences.zh: 蕭炅代為河西節度留後，杜希望隴右節度留後，王昱劍南節度使，分道經略，碎赤嶺碑。

translations.literal: Xiao Jiong replaced him as Hexi military governor designate; Du Xiwang as Longyou military governor designate; Wang Yu as Jiannan military governor—they divided forces for campaigns and smashed the Chiling stele.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jiong became acting military governor of Hexi, Du Xiwang of Longyou, and Wang Yu of Jiannan; they campaigned on separate fronts and smashed the Chiling stele.

sentences.zh: 希望發鄯州兵奪虜河橋，並河築鹽泉城，號鎮西軍，破吐蕃兵三萬。

translations.literal: Xiwang raised Shazhou troops to seize the barbarians' river bridge, built Yanchuan walled city along the river, styled it Zhenxi Army, and broke thirty thousand Tibetan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwang led Shazhou troops to seize the Tibetan river bridge, built Salt Spring fortress along the river, named it the Pacify-the-West Army, and routed thirty thousand Tibetan soldiers.

sentences.zh: 昱以劍南兵入攻安戎城，築二少壘左右之，兵次蓬婆嶺，輸劍南粟餉軍。

translations.literal: Yu led Jiannan troops in to attack Anrong walled city, built two lesser forts flanking it, troops halted at Pengpo Ridge, and transported Jiannan grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yu led Jiannan troops against Anrong fortress, built two outworks on either flank, advanced to Pengpo Ridge, and shipped grain from Jiannan to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃悉銳來救，昱大敗，少壘皆沒，士死凡數萬。

translations.literal: Tibet sent all its elite to rescue; Yu was greatly defeated, the lesser forts all lost, and soldiers dead numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet threw every elite unit into the relief; Yu was routed, both outworks were lost, and tens of thousands of his men died.

sentences.zh: 昱貪妄，非將選，故敗，貶死高要。

translations.literal: Yu was greedy and reckless, not a chosen general—therefore he was defeated; he was demoted and died at Gaoyao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was greedy and rash, no proper choice for command—hence his defeat; he was demoted and died in exile at Gaoyao.

sentences.zh: 明年，吐蕃攻白草、安人軍，詔臨洮、朔方分援。

translations.literal: The next year Tibet attacked Baicao and Anren armies; an edict ordered Lintao and Shuofang to send separate relief.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Tibet attacked the Baicao and Anren garrisons; the emperor ordered Lintao and Shuofang to send relief columns.

sentences.zh: 虜絕臨洮道，白水軍使高柬於拒守，虜引去。

translations.literal: The barbarians cut the Lintao road; Baishui Army commissioner Gao Jianyu held them off in defense, and the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans cut the Lintao road; Baishui garrison commander Gao Jian-yu held them off, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 炅遣將追尾，有雲出軍上，白兔舞，大破吐蕃。

translations.literal: Jiong sent generals in pursuit; clouds rose above the army and a white hare danced—Tibet was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent troops in pursuit; clouds gathered over the army and a white hare was seen leaping—a great victory over Tibet.

sentences.zh: 昱之敗，以張宥代節度劍南，以章仇兼瓊為益州司馬。

translations.literal: After Yu's defeat, Zhang You replaced him as Jiannan military governor, and Zhang Qiu Jianqiong was made Yizhou vice-governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu's defeat, Zhang You was made military governor of Jiannan and Zhang Qiu Jianqiong was appointed vice-governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 宥，文吏，不知兵，委事兼瓊。

translations.literal: You was a civil official, ignorant of warfare, and entrusted affairs to Jianqiong.
translations.idiomatic: You was a civil officer who knew nothing of war and left everything to Jianqiong.

sentences.zh: 兼瓊因得入奏，天子果其議，拔兼瓊代宥節度。

translations.literal: Jianqiong thereby gained entry to report at court; the Son of Heaven found his counsel sound and promoted Jianqiong to replace You as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiong thus gained access to report at court; the emperor approved his counsel and promoted Jianqiong to replace You as military governor.

sentences.zh: 兼瓊諜誘吐蕃安戎城主為應，導官軍入，盡殺虜戍，以監察御史許遠守之。

translations.literal: Jianqiong by espionage enticed the Tibetan lord of Anrong walled city to respond within, guided the official army in, slaughtered all barbarian garrisons, and appointed investigating censor Xu Yuan to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiong suborned the Tibetan commander of Anrong to open the gates, led the imperial army in, slaughtered the garrison, and left investigating censor Xu Yuan to hold the fortress.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃圍安戎，絕水泉，會石裂泉湧，虜驚引去。

translations.literal: Tibet besieged Anrong and cut off water springs; then stones split and springs gushed forth—the barbarians were startled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet besieged Anrong and cut off its water; then the rock split and springs burst forth—the Tibetans fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 復攻維州，不得志。

translations.literal: They again attacked Weizhou but did not achieve their aim.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Weizhou again but gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 詔乃改安戎曰平戎云。

translations.literal: An edict then changed Anrong to Pingrong, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Anrong to Pingrong—the Pacified Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 是歲，金城公主薨。

translations.literal: That year Princess Jincheng died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Princess Jincheng died.

sentences.zh: 明年，為發哀，吐蕃使者朝，因請和，不許。

translations.literal: The next year mourning was proclaimed; Tibetan envoys came to court and thereupon requested peace—it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court proclaimed mourning; Tibetan envoys came to court and asked for peace, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 虜乃悉眾四十萬攻承風堡，抵河源軍，西入長寧橋、安仁軍，渾崖烽騎將臧希液以銳兵五千破之。

translations.literal: The barbarians then mustered four hundred thousand to attack Chengfeng fortress, reached Heyuan Army, entered west to Changning Bridge and Anren Army; Hunya beacon cavalry general Zang Xiye with five thousand elite troops defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans then raised four hundred thousand men against Chengfeng fortress, reached Heyuan garrison, and pushed west to Changning Bridge and Anren Army; beacon-cavalry general Zang Xiye with five thousand picked troops routed them.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃又襲廓州，敗一縣，屠吏人。

translations.literal: Tibet again raided Kuozhou, defeated one county, and slaughtered officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet raided Kuozhou again, overran a county, and massacred officials and civilians.

sentences.zh: 攻振武軍石堡城，蓋嘉運不能守，

translations.literal: They attacked Zhenwu Army's Shibao walled city; Gai Jiayun could not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Shibao fortress of the Quell-the-Barbarians Army; Gai Jiayun could not hold it.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，隴右節度使皇甫惟明破虜大嶺軍；

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, Longyou military governor Huangfu Weiming broke the barbarians' Daling army;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao (742), Longyou military governor Huangfu Weiming defeated the Tibetan Daling garrison;

sentences.zh: 戰青海，破莽布支，斬首三萬級。

translations.literal: fought at Qinghai, defeated Mangbuzhi, and beheaded thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: fought on the Qinghai, routed Mangbuzhi, and took thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 明年，破洪濟城，戰石堡，不克，副將諸葛誗死之。

translations.literal: The next year he took Hongji walled city; fought at Shibao but could not take it—the vice-general Zhuge Bang died in the action.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took Hongji fortress; fought at Shibao but failed to capture it, and vice-general Zhuge Bang was killed.

sentences.zh: 又明年，惟明破虜，獻俘京師。

translations.literal: The year after that, Weiming defeated the barbarians and presented captives at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, Weiming defeated the Tibetans and presented captives at the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝以哥舒翰節度隴右，翰攻拔石堡，更號神武軍。

translations.literal: The emperor made Geshu Han military governor of Longyou; Han attacked and took Shibao, renaming it Shenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Geshu Han military governor of Longyou; Han stormed and took Shibao, renaming it the Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 又禽其相兀論樣郭。

translations.literal: He also captured their chancellor Wulun Yangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured their chancellor Wulun Yangguo.

sentences.zh: 十載，安西節度使高仙芝俘大酋以獻。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Anxi military governor Gao Xianzhi captured a great chieftain and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao (751), Anxi military governor Gao Xianzhi captured a great chieftain and presented him at court.

sentences.zh: 是時，吐蕃與蠻閣羅鳳聯兵攻瀘南，劍南節度使楊國忠方以奸罔上，自言：「破蠻眾六萬於雲南，拔故洪州等三城，獻俘口。」

translations.literal: At this time Tibet and the barbarian Geluofeng joined forces to attack Ludnan; Jiannan military governor Yang Guozhong was just deceiving the sovereign upward, himself saying: "We broke sixty thousand barbarian troops at Yunnan, took the former Hongzhou and three other walled cities, and presented captives."
translations.idiomatic: At this time Tibet allied with the Nanzhao king Geluofeng to attack southern Luzhou; Jiannan military governor Yang Guozhong was deceiving the throne and claimed, "I defeated sixty thousand barbarians in Yunnan, recovered the former Hongzhou and two other cities, and presented captives."

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰破洪濟、大莫門諸城，收九曲故地，列郡縣，實天寶十二載。

translations.literal: Geshu Han broke Hongji, Damen, and other walled cities, recovered the old Nine-Bends territory, established prefectures and counties—in fact the twelfth year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han took Hongji, Damen, and other fortresses, recovered the old Nine-Bends territory, and established prefectures and counties—in the twelfth year of Tianbao (753).

sentences.zh: 於是置神策軍於臨洮西、澆河郡於積石西、及宛秀軍以實河曲。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established Shence Army west of Lintao, Jiaohe prefecture west of Jishi, and Wanyou Army to fill the River Bend.
translations.idiomatic: The court then established the Divine Strategy Army west of Lintao, Jiaohe prefecture west of Jishi, and the Wanyou garrison to hold the River Bend.

sentences.zh: 後二年，蘇毗子悉諾邏來降，封懷義王，賜李氏。

translations.literal: Two years later, the Supi chieftain's son Sinuoluo came to surrender; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Cherishing Righteousness and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Sinuoluo, son of a Supi chieftain, surrendered; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Cherishing Righteousness and given the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 蘇毗，強部也。

translations.literal: Supi was a powerful tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Supi were a powerful tribe.

sentences.zh: 是歲，贊普乞黎蘇籠臘贊死，子挲悉籠臘贊嗣，遣使者脩好，詔京兆少尹崔光遠持節賫冊吊祠。

translations.literal: That year the zanpu Qilisuolongzan died; his son Suoxisulongzan succeeded, sent envoys to renew friendship; an edict ordered Capital Assistant Governor Cui Guangyuan to bear credentials and present the patent, condolences, and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: That year the zanpu Qilisuolongzan died and his son Suoxisulongzan succeeded; Tibet sent envoys to renew friendship, and the emperor ordered Capital Assistant Governor Cui Guangyuan to bear credentials with patents of investiture and offerings of condolence.

sentences.zh: 還而安祿山亂，哥舒翰悉河、隴兵東守潼關，而諸將各以所鎮兵討難，始號行營，邊候空虛，故吐蕃得乘隙暴掠。

translations.literal: On his return the An Lushan rebellion broke out; Geshu Han mustered all He-Long troops east to guard Tong Pass, while each general led troops from his command to suppress the crisis—they were first styled mobile camps; frontier posts stood empty, so Tibet could seize the gap and raid violently.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the An Lushan rebellion erupted; Geshu Han marched every He-Long soldier east to hold Tong Pass while other generals led their garrisons to suppress the revolt—the first mobile campaigning armies. The frontier was left bare, and Tibet seized the chance to raid at will.

sentences.zh: 至德初，取巂州及威武等諸城，入屯石堡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide they took Xizhou and Weiwu and other walled cities, and entered to garrison Shibao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhide era (756) they took Xizhou, Weiwu, and other cities and garrisoned Shibao.

sentences.zh: 其明年，使使來請討賊且脩好。

translations.literal: The next year they sent envoys requesting to campaign against the rebels and also to renew friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they sent envoys offering to fight the rebels and renew the alliance.

sentences.zh: 肅宗遣給事中南巨川報聘。

translations.literal: Suzong dispatched Supervising Secretary Nan Juchuan on a return embassy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong sent Supervising Secretary Nan Juchuan on a return embassy.

sentences.zh: 然歲內侵，取廓、霸、岷等州及河源、莫門軍。

translations.literal: Yet within the year they invaded inward, taking Kuo, Ba, Min, and other prefectures and Heyuan and Momen armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within the year they invaded again, seizing Kuo, Ba, Min, and other prefectures and the Heyuan and Momen garrisons.

sentences.zh: 使數來請和，帝雖審其譎，姑務紓患，乃詔宰相郭子儀、蕭華、裴遵慶等與盟。

translations.literal: Envoys came repeatedly requesting peace; though the emperor saw through their deceit, for the moment he sought to ease troubles, and decreed chief ministers Guo Ziyi, Xiao Hua, Pei Zunqing, and others to ally with them.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys came again and again to sue for peace; though the emperor saw their treachery, he sought a respite and decreed that chief ministers Guo Ziyi, Xiao Hua, Pei Zunqing, and others should treat with them.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，陷臨洮，取秦、成、渭等州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying they took Lintao and seized Qin, Cheng, Wei, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying (762) they overran Lintao and seized Qin, Cheng, Wei, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明年，使散騎常侍李之芳、太子左庶子崔倫往聘，吐蕃留不遣。

translations.literal: The next year they sent Regular Attendant Li Zhifang and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Cui Lun on an embassy; Tibet detained them and would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court sent Regular Attendant Li Zhifang and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Cui Lun on an embassy; Tibet detained them and refused to let them return.

sentences.zh: 破西山合水城。

translations.literal: They broke Western Mountain Heshui walled city.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Heshui fortress in the western mountains.

sentences.zh: 明年，入大震關，取蘭、河、鄯、洮等州，於是隴右地盡亡。

translations.literal: The next year they entered Dazhen Pass, took Lan, He, Shan, Tao, and other prefectures—thereupon all Longyou territory was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they forced Dazhen Pass and took Lan, He, Shan, Tao, and other prefectures; all of Longyou was lost.

sentences.zh: 進圍涇州，入之，降刺史高暉。

translations.literal: They advanced to besiege Jingzhou, entered it, and Jingzhou governor Gao Hui surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced on Jingzhou, took it, and its governor Gao Hui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又破邠州，入奉天，副元帥郭子儀禦之。

translations.literal: They again broke Binzhou, entered Fengtian; Vice Grand Marshal Guo Ziyi opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Binzhou and entered Fengtian; Vice Grand Marshal Guo Ziyi met them in defense.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以吐谷渾、党項兵二十萬東略武功，渭北行營將呂日將戰盩厔西，破之。

translations.literal: Tibet with Tuyuhun and Tangut troops two hundred thousand raided east toward Wugong; Weibei mobile-camp general Lü Rijiang fought west of Zhouzhi and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet marched two hundred thousand Tuyuhun and Tangut troops east against Wugong; Weibei campaigning general Lü Rijiang fought them west of Zhouzhi and routed them.

sentences.zh: 又戰終南，日將走。

translations.literal: They fought again at Zhongnan; Rijiang fled.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again on Zhongnan Mountain, and Rijiang was driven off.

sentences.zh: 代宗幸陜，子儀退趨商州。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong went in person to Shan; Ziyi withdrew toward Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong fled to Shan prefecture; Guo Ziyi withdrew toward Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高暉導虜入長安，立廣武王承宏為帝，改元，擅作赦令，署官吏。

translations.literal: Gao Hui guided the barbarians into Chang'an, installed Prince of Guangwu Chenghong as emperor, changed the reign title, presumptuously issued amnesties, and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui guided the Tibetans into Chang'an, set up Prince of Guangwu Chenghong as emperor, changed the reign title, issued amnesties on his own authority, and appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 衣冠皆南奔荊、襄，或逋棲山谷，亂兵因相攘鈔，道路梗閉。

translations.literal: Officials and gentry all fled south to Jing and Xiang, or hid in mountain valleys; disorderly troops plundered one another, and roads were blocked shut.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and gentry fled south to Jing and Xiang or hid in the hills; marauding soldiers looted one another and the roads were cut off.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿殷仲卿率千人壁藍田，選二百騎度浐，或紿虜曰：「郭令公軍且來！」

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Household Yin Zhongqing led a thousand men to fortify Lantian, chose two hundred cavalry to cross Chan, and someone deceived the barbarians, saying: "Lord Guo's army is about to come!"
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Household Yin Zhongqing led a thousand men to hold Lantian, sent two hundred horsemen across the Chan River, and someone deceived the Tibetans, crying, "Lord Guo's army is coming!"

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大震。

translations.literal: Tibet was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans panicked.

sentences.zh: 會少將王甫與惡少年伐鼓噪苑中，虜驚，夜引去。

translations.literal: Then Junior General Wang Fu with ruffian youths beat drums and clamored in the imperial park; the barbarians were startled and withdrew by night.
translations.idiomatic: Then Junior General Wang Fu and some rowdy youths beat drums and raised an uproar in the imperial park; the Tibetans were alarmed and withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 子儀入長安，高暉東奔至潼關，守將李日越殺之。

translations.literal: Ziyi entered Chang'an; Gao Hui fled east to Tong Pass, and garrison commander Li Riyue killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi re-entered Chang'an; Gao Hui fled east to Tong Pass, where garrison commander Li Riyue killed him.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃留京師十五日乃走，天子還京。

translations.literal: Tibet remained in the capital fifteen days then fled; the Son of Heaven returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans occupied the capital for fifteen days and then withdrew; the emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃退圍鳳翔，節度使孫志直拒守，鎮西節度使馬璘以千騎戰卻之，吐蕃屯原、會、成、渭間，自如也。

translations.literal: Tibet withdrew from besieging Fengxiang; military governor Sun Zhizhi held them off in defense. Western Frontier military governor Ma Lin with a thousand cavalry fought and drove them back. Tibet camped between Yuan, Hui, Cheng, and Wei and did as it pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans lifted the siege of Fengxiang; military governor Sun Zhizhi held the city, and Western Frontier governor Ma Lin drove them back with a thousand horsemen. They then camped across Yuan, Hui, Cheng, and Wei and ranged at will.

sentences.zh: 是歲，南入松、維、保等州及雲山新籠城。

translations.literal: That year they entered south into Song, Wei, Bao, and other prefectures and Yunshan New Cage walled city.
translations.idiomatic: That year they pushed south into Song, Wei, Bao, and other prefectures and took Yunshan New Cage fortress.

sentences.zh: 明年，還使人李之芳等。

translations.literal: The next year they sent back envoys Li Zhifang and others.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent envoys back, including Li Zhifang.

sentences.zh: 劍南嚴武破吐蕃南鄙兵七萬，拔當狗城。

translations.literal: Jiannan Yan Wu defeated seventy thousand Tibetan southern-border troops and took Danggou walled city.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiannan, Yan Wu routed seventy thousand Tibetan troops on the southern frontier and captured Danggou fortress.

sentences.zh: 會仆固懷恩反，自靈武遣其將范志誠、任敷合吐蕃、吐谷渾兵攻邠州，白孝德、郭晞嬰壘守，乃入居奉天西。

translations.literal: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, from Lingwu he sent his generals Fan Zhicheng and Ren Fu to join Tibetan and Tuyuhun troops in attacking Binzhou. Bai Xiaode and Guo Xi held fast behind ramparts in defense, and the barbarians then entered and encamped west of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, he sent Fan Zhicheng and Ren Fu from Lingwu with Tibetan and Tuyuhun forces against Binzhou. Bai Xiaode and Guo Xi walled up and held out, whereupon the allies moved in and camped west of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 子儀入奉天，按軍不戰。

translations.literal: Ziyi entered Fengtian and restrained the army from fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi entered Fengtian and held his army back from battle.

sentences.zh: 郭晞以銳士夜搗其營，斬首數千級，奪馬五百，取四將，吐蕃引去。

translations.literal: Guo Xi with elite troops raided their camp by night, beheaded several thousand, seized five hundred horses, captured four generals, and Tibet withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xi led picked troops in a night assault on their camp, took several thousand heads and five hundred horses, captured four generals, and the Tibetans withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是時嚴武拔鹽川，又戰西山，取其眾八萬。

translations.literal: At this time Yan Wu took Yanchuan, again fought on the Western Hills, and took eighty thousand of their force.
translations.idiomatic: About then Yan Wu seized Yanchuan, fought again in the western hills, and took eighty thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 虜圍涼州，河西節度使楊志烈不能守，跳保甘州，而涼州亡，

translations.literal: The barbarians besieged Liangzhou. Hexi military governor Yang Zhilie could not hold it, leapt away to shelter at Ganzhou, and Liangzhou perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans besieged Liangzhou. Hexi military governor Yang Zhilie could not hold the city, fled to Ganzhou for safety, and Liangzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，吐蕃請和，詔宰相元載、杜鴻漸與虜使者同盟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Tibet requested peace; an edict ordered chief ministers Yuan Zai and Du Hongjian to ally with the barbarian envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, the Tibetans sued for peace, and the emperor ordered chief ministers Yuan Zai and Du Hongjian to conclude an alliance with their envoys.

sentences.zh: 懷恩不得志，導虜與回紇、党項羌、渾、奴刺犯邊，吐蕃大酋尚結息、贊摩、尚悉東贊等眾二十萬至醴泉、奉天，邠將白孝德不能亢，任敷以兵略鳳翔、盩厔，於是京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: Huai'en did not achieve his aim and guided the barbarians with the Uyghurs, Tangut Qiang, Hun, and Nuci to violate the border. Tibetan great chiefs Shang Jiexi, Zanmo, Shang Sidongzan, and others with two hundred thousand reached Liquan and Fengtian. Bin general Bai Xiaode could not resist; Ren Fu with troops raided Fengxiang and Zhouzhi—thereupon the capital was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated, Huai'en led the Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tangut Qiang, Hun, and Nuci against the frontier. Great chiefs Shang Jiexi, Zanmo, and Shang Sidongzan marched two hundred thousand men to Liquan and Fengtian. Binzhou general Bai Xiaode could not hold them; Ren Fu raided Fengxiang and Zhouzhi, and the capital went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 朔方兵馬使渾日時、孫守亮屯奉天，詔子儀以河中兵屯涇陽，李忠臣屯東渭橋，李光進屯雲陽，馬璘、郝廷玉屯便橋，駱奉先、李日越屯盩厔，李抱玉屯鳳翔，周智光屯同州，杜冕屯坊州，天子自率六軍屯於苑。

translations.literal: Shuofang army horse commissioner Hun Rishi and Sun Shouliang encamped at Fengtian. An edict ordered Ziyi with Hezhong troops to encamp at Jingyang; Li Zhongchen at East Wei Bridge; Li Guangjin at Yunyang; Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Bian Bridge; Luo Fengxian and Li Riyue at Zhouzhi; Li Baoyu at Fengxiang; Zhou Zhiguang at Tongzhou; Du Mian at Fangzhou; the Son of Heaven himself led the Six Armies to encamp in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang commissioners Hun Rishi and Sun Shouliang held Fengtian. The emperor ordered Guo Ziyi with Hezhong troops to Jingyang, Li Zhongchen to the East Wei Bridge, Li Guangjin to Yunyang, Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu to Bian Bridge, Luo Fengxian and Li Riyue to Zhouzhi, Li Baoyu to Fengxiang, Zhou Zhiguang to Tongzhou, and Du Mian to Fangzhou, while he himself led the Six Armies into the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃逼奉天，日進以單騎馳之，士二百踵進，左右擊刺，射皆應弦仆，虜大驚辟易。

translations.literal: Tibet pressed Fengtian. Ri Jin with a single horse charged them; two hundred soldiers followed close behind, striking left and right with thrusts; every shot fell as the bowstring sounded—the barbarians were greatly startled and gave way.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans pressed Fengtian. Ri Jin charged alone at the head of two hundred men who closed behind him, cutting left and right; every arrow found its mark, and the enemy recoiled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 日進挾虜一將躍出，舉軍望而噪，士還，無一矢著身者。

translations.literal: Ri Jin seized one barbarian general and leapt out; the whole army looked on and cheered. The men returned, and not one arrow had struck their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Ri Jin seized a Tibetan officer and burst back through the lines; the army roared its approval. His men returned unscathed—not an arrow had touched them.

sentences.zh: 明日，虜薄城，日進發機石勁弩，故兵多死。

translations.literal: The next day the barbarians pressed the city. Ri Jin deployed catapults and powerful crossbows, so many of the enemy died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Tibetans pressed the walls. Ri Jin brought up catapults and heavy crossbows, and the enemy suffered heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 凡三日，虜斂軍入壁，日進知虜曲折，即夜斫其營，斬千餘級，生禽五百。

translations.literal: In all three days the barbarians drew in their army behind walls. Ri Jin knew their movements and that night cut into their camp, beheading more than a thousand and taking five hundred alive.
translations.idiomatic: After three days the Tibetans pulled back behind their ramparts. Knowing their dispositions, Ri Jin struck their camp that night, killing more than a thousand and capturing five hundred alive.

sentences.zh: 又戰馬嵬，凡七日，破賊萬人，斬首五千，獲馬、橐它、幟械甚眾。

translations.literal: They again fought at Mawei. In all seven days they broke ten thousand rebels, beheaded five thousand, and obtained horses, camels, banners, and weapons in great number.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again at Mawei. In seven days they routed ten thousand of the enemy, took five thousand heads, and seized horses, camels, banners, and arms in abundance.

sentences.zh: 帝欲自討賊，下詔大搜馬，京師始置團練，都人震擾，鑿垣亡去者十八，詔中人戶都門，不能止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to campaign against the rebels in person and issued an edict for a great search for horses. The capital for the first time established militia training; the metropolitan people were shaken and disturbed—eight in ten broke through walls and fled. An edict placed middle men at every gate of the capital, yet it could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to take the field himself and ordered a sweeping levy of horses. For the first time the capital raised militia regiments. Panic spread through the city; eight households in ten broke through their walls and fled. Edicts posted men at every gate could not stem the flight.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遊騎四百略武功，鎮西節度使馬璘使健士五十擊之，殲，士氣益奮。

translations.literal: Four hundred Tibetan scouting cavalry raided Wugong. Western Frontier military governor Ma Lin sent fifty stalwart warriors to strike them and annihilated them; troop morale grew still bolder.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred Tibetan scouts raided Wugong. Ma Lin sent fifty picked warriors who wiped them out, and army morale soared.

sentences.zh: 虜徙營九𡼇之陰，掠醴泉居人數萬，焚室廬，田皆赤地。

translations.literal: The barbarians moved camp to the shade of Jiuling, plundered tens of thousands of Liquan inhabitants, burned houses and huts, and the fields all became bare red earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans shifted camp to the slopes of Jiuling, carried off tens of thousands of people from Liquan, burned their homes, and left the countryside a scorched wasteland.

sentences.zh: 周智光與虜戰澄城，破之。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhiguang fought the barbarians at Chengcheng and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhiguang met the Tibetans at Chengcheng and routed them.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃至邠北，復與回紇合，還攻奉天，抵馬嵬。

translations.literal: Tibet reached north of Bin, again joined with the Uyghurs, returned to attack Fengtian, and reached Mawei.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans reached the country north of Bin, allied again with the Uyghurs, turned back to assault Fengtian, and advanced as far as Mawei.

sentences.zh: 任敷以兵五千掠白水，殘同州。

translations.literal: Ren Fu with five thousand troops plundered Baishui and ravaged Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fu led five thousand men to plunder Baishui and lay waste to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是城中渭橋、鄠以屯兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon within the city troops were stationed at Wei Bridge and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were then posted within the capital at the Wei Bridge and at Ye.

sentences.zh: 會懷恩死，虜謀無主，遂與回紇爭長。

translations.literal: When Huai'en died, the barbarians' plans had no leader, and they then contended for precedence with the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en died the allied campaign lost its leader, and the Tibetans soon quarreled with the Uyghurs over who should command.

sentences.zh: 回紇怒，詣子儀請擊吐蕃自效，子儀許之，使白元光合兵攻吐蕃於靈臺西，大破之，降仆固名臣，帝乃班師。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs were angry and went to Ziyi requesting to attack Tibet to prove their merit. Ziyi assented and sent Bai Yuanguang to join forces and attack Tibet west of Lingtai, greatly defeating them. Pugu Mingchen surrendered, and the emperor then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the Uyghurs asked Guo Ziyi to let them prove themselves against Tibet. He agreed and sent Bai Yuanguang to join them west of Lingtai, where they inflicted a crushing defeat. Pugu Mingchen surrendered, and the emperor recalled his armies.

sentences.zh: ◎吐蕃下

translations.literal: ◎ Tibet (Part Two)
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Tibet (Part Two)

sentences.zh: 永泰、大歷間，再遣使者來聘，於是戶部尚書薛景仙往報。

translations.literal: Between the Yongtai and Dali reign periods they again sent envoys on friendly missions; thereupon Minister of Revenue Xue Jingxian went in return.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongtai and early Dali years they again sent friendly embassies, and Minister of Revenue Xue Jingxian was dispatched in reply.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相與吐蕃使者盟。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the chief ministers to ally with the Tibetan envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his chief ministers to conclude an alliance with the Tibetan envoys.

sentences.zh: 俄寇靈州，掠宜祿，郭子儀精甲三萬戍涇陽，入屯奉天。

translations.literal: Soon they raided Lingzhou and plundered Yilu. Guo Ziyi with thirty thousand elite armored troops garrisoned Jingyang and entered to encamp at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they raided Lingzhou and plundered Yilu. Guo Ziyi posted thirty thousand picked troops at Jingyang and moved into Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 靈州兵破虜二萬，上級五百首。

translations.literal: Lingzhou troops defeated twenty thousand barbarians and presented five hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhou troops routed twenty thousand Tibetans and sent up five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 景仙與倫泣陵偕來，請境鳳林關，而路悉等十五人又來。

translations.literal: Jingxian came together with Lun Qiling, requesting the border at Fenglin Pass, while Lu Xi and fifteen others also came.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian returned with Lun Qiling, who asked that the border be fixed at Fenglin Pass, while Lu Xi and fifteen other envoys also arrived.

sentences.zh: 三年，虜引眾十萬復攻靈州，略邠州。

translations.literal: In the third year the barbarians led one hundred thousand again to attack Lingzhou and raided Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dali they mustered one hundred thousand men, attacked Lingzhou again, and raided Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，尚悉結自寶應後數入邊，以功高請老，而贊磨代之，為東面節度使，專河、隴。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shang Xijie since Baoying had repeatedly entered the border. Because his merit was high he requested retirement, and Zanmo replaced him as eastern frontier military commissioner, in charge of the He and Long circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shang Xijie had raided the frontier repeatedly since the Baoying era. Citing his long service, he asked to retire; Zanmo replaced him as eastern commander with authority over the He and Long regions.

sentences.zh: 邠寧馬璘、朔方將白元光再破其眾，獲馬羊數千，劍南亦破虜萬人。

translations.literal: Binning Ma Lin and Shuofang general Bai Yuanguang again defeated their force and obtained several thousand horses and sheep; Jiannan also defeated ten thousand barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin of Binning and Shuofang general Bai Yuanguang again routed the Tibetans and seized thousands of horses and sheep; Jiannan forces also defeated ten thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 尚悉摩復來朝。

translations.literal: Shang Ximo again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ximo came to court again.

sentences.zh: 天子以虜數入塞，詔治守障，徙當、悉、柘、靜、恭五州，皆據險以守。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, because the barbarians repeatedly entered the passes, ordered repair of border defenses and moved the five prefectures Dang, Xi, Zhe, Jing, and Gong—all to hold strategic terrain in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Tibetans kept crossing the frontier, the emperor ordered the border defenses repaired and relocated the five prefectures of Dang, Xi, Zhe, Jing, and Gong to strong positions.

sentences.zh: 八年，虜六萬騎侵靈州，敗民稼，進寇涇、邠，渾瑊與戰不利，副將死，略數千戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year sixty thousand barbarian cavalry invaded Lingzhou, ruined the people's crops, and advanced to raid Jing and Bin. Hun Zhen fought them with ill success; a vice-general died, and several thousand households were plundered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali sixty thousand Tibetan horsemen invaded Lingzhou, destroyed the harvest, and pushed on against Jing and Bin. Hun Zhen fought them without success; a deputy commander was killed and several thousand households were carried off.

sentences.zh: 瑊整卒夜襲其營；

translations.literal: Zhen reorganized his troops and raided their camp by night;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen rallied his men and struck their camp that night;

sentences.zh: 涇原馬璘以兵掩之潘原，射豹皮將死，軍中哭，乃遁去。

translations.literal: Jingyuan Ma Lin with troops ambushed them at Panyuan, shot the leopard-skin general dead, and the army within wept—thereupon they fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin of Jingyuan ambushed them at Panyuan and killed their leopard-skin commander; the enemy camp broke into mourning wails and they fled.

sentences.zh: 璘收所俘士及男女而還。

translations.literal: Lin gathered the captured soldiers and men and women and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin gathered the soldiers and civilians he had rescued and marched back.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀又破其眾十萬。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi again defeated one hundred thousand of their force.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi again routed one hundred thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 九年，帝遣諫議大夫吳損修好，虜亦使使者入朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor sent Remonstrating Censor Wu Sun to restore good relations; the barbarians also sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dali the emperor sent Remonstrating Censor Wu Sun to renew friendly ties, and the Tibetans also sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 於是子儀屯邠州，李抱玉屯高壁，馬璘屯原州，李忠臣屯涇州，李忠誠屯鳳翔，臧希讓屯渭北，備虜之入。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ziyi encamped at Binzhou, Li Baoyu at Gaobi, Ma Lin at Yuanzhou, Li Zhongchen at Jingzhou, Li Zhongcheng at Fengxiang, and Zang Xianrang north of Wei—to guard against barbarian entry.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi then held Binzhou, Li Baoyu Gaobi, Ma Lin Yuanzhou, Li Zhongchen Jingzhou, Li Zhongcheng Fengxiang, and Zang Xianrang the country north of the Wei River, all to block Tibetan incursions.

sentences.zh: 明年，西川節度使崔寧破虜於西山。

translations.literal: The next year Western Sichuan military governor Cui Ning defeated the barbarians on the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Western Sichuan military governor Cui Ning defeated the Tibetans in the western hills.

sentences.zh: 虜攻臨涇、隴州，次普潤，焚掠人畜；

translations.literal: The barbarians attacked Linjing and Longzhou, halted at Purun, and burned and plundered people and livestock;
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans attacked Linjing and Longzhou, pushed on to Purun, and burned and looted people and herds;

sentences.zh: 與抱玉戰義寧，破之；

translations.literal: fought Baoyu at Yining, and he defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: fought Li Baoyu at Yining and were beaten;

sentences.zh: 道涇州，璘尾追，敗之於百里。

translations.literal: passed by Jingzhou; Lin pursued their rear and defeated them at Baili.
translations.idiomatic: retreated past Jingzhou; Ma Lin pursued and routed them at Baili.

sentences.zh: 又明年，崔寧破虜故洪節度、氐、蠻、党項等兵，斬首萬級，禽酋領千人，牛羊廩鎧甚眾，獻之朝。

translations.literal: The year after that, Cui Ning defeated barbarian troops of the former Hong circuit, Di, Man, Tangut, and others—beheaded ten thousand, captured a thousand chieftains, and obtained cattle, sheep, granaries, and armor in great number, which he presented at court.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Cui Ning routed Tibetan forces of the old Hong circuit together with Di, Man, and Tangut allies, took ten thousand heads and a thousand chieftains, and sent up vast herds, stores, and armor to the court.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃不得志，入掠黎、雅，於是劍南兵合南詔與戰，破之，禽大籠官論器然。

translations.literal: Tibet did not achieve its aim, entered to plunder Li and Ya, and thereupon Jiannan troops joined Nanzhao in battle, defeated them, and captured the great cage officer Lun Qiran.
translations.idiomatic: Thwarted in the north, the Tibetans raided Li and Ya; Jiannan troops then joined Nanzhao, defeated them, and captured the great frontier officer Lun Qiran.

sentences.zh: 又侵坊州，取党項牧馬。

translations.literal: They again invaded Fangzhou and took Tangut pasture horses.
