translations.idiomatic: They raided Fangzhou again and drove off Tangut horse herds.

sentences.zh: 崔寧攻望漢城，破之。

translations.literal: Cui Ning attacked Wanghan walled city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning stormed Wanghan fortress and captured it.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使張獻恭戰岷州，吐蕃走。

translations.literal: Southwestern Shannan military governor Zhang Xiangong fought at Minzhou and Tibet fled.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern Shannan military governor Zhang Xiangong fought them at Minzhou and the Tibetans withdrew.

sentences.zh: 寧破西山三路及邛南兵，斬首八千級。

translations.literal: Ning defeated the three western-hill routes and Qiongnan troops, beheading eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning routed the three western-hill columns and Qiongnan forces, taking eight thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 十三年，虜大酋馬重英以四萬騎寇靈州，塞漢、御史、尚書三渠以擾屯田，為朔方留後常謙光所逐，重英殘鹽、慶而去。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the barbarian great chief Ma Chongying with forty thousand cavalry raided Lingzhou, blocked the Han, Yushi, and Shangshu three canals to disrupt frontier farming, was driven off by Shuofang acting military commissioner Chang Qian'guang, and Chongying ravaged Yan and Qing and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Dali the Tibetan great chief Ma Chongying led forty thousand horsemen against Lingzhou, dammed the Han, Yushi, and Shangshu canals to ruin the frontier farms, was driven off by Shuofang acting commissioner Chang Qian'guang, and after ravaging Yan and Qing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乃南合南詔眾二十萬攻茂州，略扶、文，遂侵黎、雅。

translations.literal: He then united south with two hundred thousand Nanzhao troops to attack Maozhou, raided Fu and Wen, and thereupon invaded Li and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined two hundred thousand Nanzhao troops in the south, attacked Maozhou, overran Fu and Wen, and pushed on into Li and Ya.

sentences.zh: 時天子已發幽州兵馳拒，虜大奔破。

translations.literal: At this time the Son of Heaven had already dispatched Youzhou troops in haste to resist; the barbarians fled in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had already rushed Youzhou troops to meet them, and the Tibetans fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 初，虜使數至，留不遣，所俘虜口，悉部送江南。

translations.literal: Initially Tibetan envoys came repeatedly but were detained and not sent back; all captured barbarian persons were escorted in groups to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tibetan envoys came again and again but were held and not returned, while every Tibetan captive was marched off to the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，先內靖方鎮，顧歲與虜確，其亡獲相償，欲以德綏懷之，遣太常少卿韋倫持節歸其俘五百，厚給衣褚，切敕邊吏護亭障，無輒侵虜地。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne he first pacified the interior regional commands within, looked to the yearly balance of losses and gains with the barbarians offsetting one another, and wished to soothe them through virtue. He sent Taichang Vice Minister Wei Lun bearing credentials to return five hundred of their captives, gave them thick supplies of clothing, and sternly charged border officials to guard posts and barriers and not rashly invade barbarian territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong came to the throne he first pacified the internal military governors, reckoned that yearly border losses and gains had largely canceled out, and wished to win the Tibetans by kindness. He sent Taichang Vice Minister Wei Lun with credentials to return five hundred captives, furnished them generously with clothing, and strictly ordered frontier officials to guard the posts and not cross into Tibetan lands.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃始聞未信，使者入境，乃皆感畏。

translations.literal: Tibet at first heard and did not believe; when the envoys entered the border, all were moved and in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans at first would not believe it; once the envoys crossed the frontier, they were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 是時，乞立贊為贊普，姓戶虜提氏，曰：「我乃有三恨：不知天子喪，不及吊，一也；

translations.literal: At this time Qili Zan was Zanpu, surname of the Hutudi clan. He said: "I have three resentments: not knowing the Son of Heaven had died and being unable to offer mourning—one;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Zanpu was Qili Zan of the Hutudi clan. He said, "I bear three grievances: I did not know the emperor had died and could not send condolences—that is the first;

sentences.zh: 山陵不及賻，二也；

translations.literal: being unable to present funeral gifts at the imperial tomb—two;
translations.idiomatic: I could not present funeral gifts at the imperial tomb—that is the second;

sentences.zh: 不知舅即位，而發兵攻靈州，入扶、文，侵灌口，三也。」

translations.literal: not knowing my uncle-by-marriage had taken the throne yet sending troops to attack Lingzhou, entering Fu and Wen, and invading Guankou—three."
translations.idiomatic: I did not know my imperial uncle had succeeded, yet I sent troops against Lingzhou, entered Fu and Wen, and raided Guankou—that is the third."

sentences.zh: 即發使者隨倫入朝。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent envoys to follow Lun into court.
translations.idiomatic: With that he dispatched envoys to accompany Lun to court.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣倫還蜀俘。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Lun to return Shu captives.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Lun to return Sichuan captives.

sentences.zh: 虜以倫再至，歡甚，授館，作聲樂，九日留，以論欽明思等五十人從獻方物。

translations.literal: The barbarians, because Lun came again, were very pleased, lodged him, made music and song, detained him nine days, and had Lun Qinmingsi and fifty others follow to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted that Lun had come again, the Tibetans lodged him, entertained him with music, kept him nine days, and sent Lun Qinmingsi and fifty others back with him bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年，殿中少監崔漢衡往使，贊普猥曰：「我與唐舅甥國，詔書乃用臣禮卑我。」

translations.literal: The next year Palace Vice Director Cui Hanheng went on mission. The Zanpu rudely said: "I and Tang are an uncle-and-nephew state, yet the edicts use subject rites to demean me."
translations.idiomatic: The following year Palace Vice Director Cui Hanheng was sent as envoy. The Zanpu said bluntly, "Tang and Tibet are uncle and nephew, yet your edicts treat me as a subject and demean me."

sentences.zh: 又請雲州西盡賀蘭山為吐蕃境，邀漢衡奏天子。

translations.literal: He also requested that west of Yunzhou as far as Helan Mountain be Tibetan territory, and urged Hanheng to report this to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded that everything west of Yunzhou to Helan Mountain be Tibetan territory and pressed Hanheng to report this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 乃遣入蕃使判官常魯與論悉諾羅入朝，道贊普語，且引景龍詔書曰「唐使至，甥先與盟，蕃使至，舅亦將親盟」；

translations.literal: He then sent border envoy judge Chang Lu with Lun Sinoluo to court, conveying the Zanpu's words and also citing the Jinglong edict: "When the Tang envoy arrives, the nephew first allies; when the Tibetan envoy arrives, the uncle also will ally in person";
translations.idiomatic: He then sent border envoy judge Chang Lu with Lun Sinoluo to court, relayed the Zanpu's message, and cited the Jinglong edict: "When a Tang envoy comes, the nephew shall ally first; when a Tibetan envoy comes, the uncle shall ally in person";

sentences.zh: 贊普曰「其禮本均。」

translations.literal: the Zanpu said, "the rites are originally equal."
translations.idiomatic: the Zanpu said, "the ceremonial standing was always meant to be equal."

sentences.zh: 帝許之，以「獻」為「進」，「賜」為「寄」，「領取」為「領之」。

translations.literal: The emperor assented, changing "present" to "forward," "bestow" to "send," and "receive and take" to "receive."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, substituting "forward" for "present," "send" for "bestow," and "receive" for "receive and take."

sentences.zh: 以前宰相楊炎不通故事為解，並約地於賀蘭。

translations.literal: He explained this by saying the former chief minister Yang Yan did not understand precedent, and also fixed the border at Helan.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed the change on former chief minister Yang Yan's ignorance of precedent and also agreed to set the frontier at Helan.

sentences.zh: 其大相尚悉結嗜殺人，以劍南之敗未報，不助和議，次相尚結贊有謀，固請休息邊人，贊普卒用結贊為大相，乃講好。

translations.literal: Their great minister Shang Xijie was addicted to killing people; because the Jiannan defeat was unavenged he did not support the peace talks. The second minister Shang Jiezan was scheming and firmly urged resting the border people. The Zanpu finally made Jiezan great minister, and thereupon they sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: The great minister Shang Xijie was bloodthirsty; still smarting from the defeat in Jiannan, he opposed peace. The second minister Shang Jiezan was shrewder and pressed to give the frontier a rest. The Zanpu finally made Jiezan great minister, and peace talks followed.

sentences.zh: 漢衡與其使區頰贊偕來，約盟境上。

translations.literal: Hanheng came together with their envoy Qu Zan and agreed to ally on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Hanheng returned with the Tibetan envoy Qu Zan and arranged to conclude an alliance on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 拜漢衡鴻臚卿，以都官員外郎樊澤為計會使，與結贊約；

translations.literal: Hanheng was appointed Honglu Director; Bureau of Revenue Vice Fan Ze was made accountant envoy to ally with Jiezan;
translations.idiomatic: Hanheng was made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Receptions; Bureau of Revenue Vice Fan Ze was appointed accountant envoy to treat with Jiezan;

sentences.zh: 且告隴右節度使張鎰同盟。

translations.literal: and Longyou military governor Zhang Yian was also informed to ally.
translations.idiomatic: and Longyou military governor Zhang Yian was told to join the alliance as well.

sentences.zh: 澤與結贊約盟清水，以牛馬為牲。

translations.literal: Fan Ze and Jiezan allied at Qingshui, using oxen and horses as sacrificial victims.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ze and Jiezan concluded the alliance at Qingshui with oxen and horses as sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 鎰欲末其禮，乃紿結贊曰：「唐非牛不田，蕃非馬不戰，請用犬、豕、羊。」

translations.literal: Yian wished to reduce the ceremony and therefore deceived Jiezan, saying: "Tang does not plow without oxen; Tibet does not fight without horses—please use dogs, pigs, and sheep."
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to scale back the rites, Zhang Yian deceived Jiezan, saying, "Tang cannot farm without oxen, nor can Tibet fight without horses—let us sacrifice dogs, pigs, and sheep instead."

sentences.zh: 結贊聽諾。

translations.literal: Jiezan listened and assented.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan agreed.

sentences.zh: 將盟，乃除地為壇，約二國各以二千士列壝外，冗從立壇下。

translations.literal: When they were about to ally, they cleared ground for an altar, agreeing that each state would array two thousand soldiers outside the rampart while attendants stood below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rites they cleared ground for an altar, posted two thousand soldiers from each side outside the embankment, and stationed attendants below the platform.

sentences.zh: 鎰與幕府齊映齊抗、鴻臚漢衡、計會使於頔及澤、魯皆朝服，結贊與論悉頰藏、論臧熱、論利陀、論力徐等對升壇，刑牲壇北，雜其血以進，約：「唐地涇州右盡彈箏峽，隴州右極清水，鳳州西盡同谷，劍南盡西山、大度水。

translations.literal: Yian with staff Qi Ying and Qi Kang, Honglu Director Hanheng, accountant envoy Yu Hao, Fan Ze, and Chang Lu all in court dress, and Jiezan with Lun Xizang, Lun Zangre, Lun Lituo, Lun Lixu, and others facing one another ascending the altar—sacrificial victims were slain north of the altar, their blood mixed and presented. The covenant read: "Tang territory: from Jingzhou's right as far as Tanji Gorge; Longzhou's right to the limit at Qingshui; Fengzhou west to Tonggu; Jiannan to the Western Hills and the Dadu River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yian with his staff Qi Ying and Qi Kang, Honglu Director Hanheng, accountant envoy Yu Hao, Fan Ze, and Chang Lu—all in court dress—faced Jiezan, Lun Xizang, Lun Zangre, Lun Lituo, Lun Lixu, and others as they mounted the altar together. Victims were slaughtered north of the altar, their blood mingled and offered. The treaty fixed Tang territory from the right of Jingzhou to Tanji Gorge, from the right of Longzhou to Qingshui, from the west of Fengzhou to Tonggu, and all of Jiannan to the western hills and the Dadu River.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃守鎮蘭、渭、原、會，西臨洮，東成州，抵劍南西磨些諸蠻、大度水之西南。

translations.literal: Tibet would hold garrisons at Lan, Wei, Yuan, and Hui, west to Lintao, east to Chengzhou, reaching the Mosuo barbarians southwest of Jiannan's western hills and the Dadu River.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet would hold Lan, Wei, Yuan, and Hui, with Lintao on the west, Chengzhou on the east, and the southwest as far as the Mosuo tribes beyond Jiannan's western hills and the Dadu River.

sentences.zh: 盡大河北自新泉軍抵大磧，南極賀蘭橐它嶺，其間為閑田。

translations.literal: North of the great Yellow River from Xinquan Army to the great desert, south to Helan Camel Ridge—the land between would be idle fields.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yellow River from Xinquan garrison to the great desert, and south to Helan Camel Ridge, the intervening land would remain unoccupied.

sentences.zh: 二國所棄戍地毋增兵，毋創城堡，毋耕邊田。」

translations.literal: On abandoned garrison lands of the two states there would be no adding troops, no building new castles, and no plowing border fields."
translations.idiomatic: Neither side would reinforce abandoned posts, build new forts, or farm the border marches."

sentences.zh: 既盟，請鎰詣壇西南隅浮屠幄為誓。

translations.literal: After the alliance they asked Yian to go to the pagoda tent at the altar's southwest corner to swear.
translations.idiomatic: After the pact they asked Zhang Yian to swear in the Buddhist tent at the altar's southwest corner.

sentences.zh: 於是升壇大享，獻酬乃還。

translations.literal: Thereupon they ascended the altar for a great feast; after presenting and returning gifts they departed.
translations.idiomatic: They then mounted the altar for a great feast, exchanged gifts, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝命宰相、尚書與虜使者盟長安，而清水之約，疆埸不定，復令漢衡決於贊普，乃克盟。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered chief ministers and ministers to ally with the barbarian envoys at Chang'an. But the Qingshui covenant left the borders unfixed, so Hanheng was again sent to decide with the Zanpu before the alliance could be concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his chief ministers and senior officials to conclude an alliance with the Tibetan envoys at Chang'an. Because the Qingshui treaty had left the frontier lines unsettled, Hanheng was sent back to settle the matter with the Zanpu before the pact could stand.

sentences.zh: 於是宰相李忠臣盧杞關播崔寧、工部尚書喬琳、御史大夫於頎、太府卿張獻恭、司農卿段秀實、少府監李昌夔、京兆尹王翃、金吾衛大將軍渾瑊與區頰贊等同盟京城之右郊，禮如清水。

translations.literal: Thereupon chief ministers Li Zhongchen, Lu Qi, Guan Bo, and Cui Ning; Minister of Works Qiao Lin; Censor-in-Chief Yu Yi; Grand Steward Zhang Xiangong; Minister of Agriculture Duan Xiushi; Director of the Palace Workshops Li Changkui; Metropolitan Governor Wang Hong; and Golden Guard general Hun Zhen allied with Qu Zan and others in the capital's right suburb, the rites as at Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Li Zhongchen, Lu Qi, Guan Bo, and Cui Ning, together with Minister of Works Qiao Lin, Censor-in-Chief Yu Yi, Grand Steward Zhang Xiangong, Minister of Agriculture Duan Xiushi, Director of the Palace Workshops Li Changkui, Metropolitan Governor Wang Hong, Golden Guard general Hun Zhen, and Qu Zan then concluded the alliance in the capital's eastern suburb with the same rites as at Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 前二月告廟，齊，三日，關播跪讀載書，已盟，乃大享。

translations.literal: Two months before they notified the ancestral temple and fasted. On the third day Guan Bo knelt and read the covenant text; after the alliance they held a great feast.
translations.idiomatic: Two months earlier the court had notified the ancestral temple and observed a fast. On the third day Guan Bo knelt and read the treaty text; once the alliance was sealed, a great feast followed.

sentences.zh: 詔左僕射李揆為入蕃會盟使，還區頰贊等。

translations.literal: An edict made Left Vice Director Li Kui envoy for entering Tibet to conclude the alliance and return Qu Zan and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Left Vice Director Li Kui envoy to Tibet to ratify the alliance and sent Qu Zan and his party home.

sentences.zh: 朱泚之亂，吐蕃請助討賊，詔右散騎常侍於頎持節慰撫，太常少卿沈房為安西、北庭宣慰使以報之。

translations.literal: During Zhu Ci's rebellion Tibet requested to help suppress the rebels. An edict made Right Attendant Cavalier Yu Yi bearer of credentials to console and soothe them; Taichang Vice Minister Shen Fang was made Anxi and Beiting comfort envoy in return.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion the Tibetans offered to help suppress the rebels. The emperor sent Right Attendant Cavalier Yu Yi with credentials to receive them graciously, and appointed Taichang Vice Minister Shen Fang comfort envoy to Anxi and Beiting in reply.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊用論莽羅兵破泚將韓旻於武亭川。

translations.literal: Hun Zhen used Lun Mangluo's troops to defeat Zhu Ci's general Han Min at Wutingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Zhen used Lun Mangluo's Tibetan troops to defeat Zhu Ci's general Han Min at Wuting River.

sentences.zh: 初，與虜約，得長安，以涇、靈四州畀之。

translations.literal: Initially they had agreed with the barbarians that if Chang'an were taken, the four prefectures Jing, Ling, and others would be given to them.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset they had promised the Tibetans that if Chang'an fell, the four prefectures of Jing, Ling, and the rest would be ceded to them.

sentences.zh: 會大疫，虜輒引去。

translations.literal: When a great epidemic occurred, the barbarians then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: A great epidemic broke out, and the Tibetans withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及泚平，責先約求地。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci was pacified, they pressed the prior covenant and demanded the land.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's defeat they invoked the earlier bargain and demanded the promised territory.

sentences.zh: 天子薄其勞，第賜詔書，償結贊、莽羅等帛萬匹，於是虜以為怨，

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven slighted their labor and only bestowed an edict, compensating Jiezan, Mangluo, and others with ten thousand rolls of silk—thereupon the barbarians took this as a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought little of their service and sent only an edict with ten thousand bolts of silk for Jiezan, Mangluo, and the rest. The Tibetans took this as an insult.

sentences.zh: 詔倉部郎中趙建往使，而虜已犯涇、隴、邠、寧，掠人畜，敗田稼，內州皆閉壁。

translations.literal: After this grievance an edict sent Treasury Bureau Director Zhao Jian on mission, but the barbarians had already violated Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning, plundering people and livestock, ruining field crops, and inner prefectures all closed their walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of that resentment the emperor sent Treasury Bureau Director Zhao Jian as envoy, but the Tibetans had already struck Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning, looting people and herds, destroying the harvest, and every interior prefecture had shut its gates.

sentences.zh: 遊騎至好畤，左金吾將軍張獻甫、神策將李升曇等屯咸陽，河中渾瑊、華州駱元光援之。

translations.literal: Scouting cavalry reached Haochi. Left Golden Guard general Zhang Xianfu, Divine Strategy general Li Shengyan, and others encamped at Xianyang; Hezhong Hun Zhen and Huazhou Luo Yuanguang came to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan scouts reached Haochi. Left Golden Guard general Zhang Xianfu and Divine Strategy general Li Shengyan held Xianyang, while Hun Zhen from Hezhong and Luo Yuanguang from Huazhou hurried to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 以左監門將軍康成使焉。

translations.literal: Left Gate general Kang Cheng was sent there on mission.
translations.idiomatic: Left Gate general Kang Cheng was dispatched on the mission.

sentences.zh: 尚結贊屯上砦原，亦令使論乞陀來請盟。

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan encamped at Shangzhaiyuan and also sent envoy Lun Qituo to request an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan camped at Shangzhaiyuan and also sent Lun Qituo to ask for peace talks.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔李晟遣部將王佖以銳兵三千夜入汧陽，明日，薄其中軍，虜驚潰走，結贊僅自脫。

translations.literal: Fengxiang Li Sheng sent deputy general Wang Fu with sharp troops three thousand by night entering Qianyang; next day pressed close to their center army; barbarians startled collapsed fled; Jiezan only himself escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng of Fengxiang sent his deputy Wang Fu with three thousand elite troops into Qianyang by night; the next day they pressed the enemy center; the barbarians panicked, broke, and fled, and Jiezan barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 虜眾二萬侵鳳翔，李晟擊卻之，因襲破摧沙堡，燒儲廥，斬守者。

translations.literal: Barbarian host twenty thousand invaded Fengxiang; Li Sheng struck repelled them; thereupon raided broke Cuisha fort; burned store granaries; beheaded defenders.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand barbarians invaded Fengxiang; Li Sheng struck and drove them back, then raided and broke Cuisha Fort, burned the storehouses, and beheaded the garrison.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃攻鹽、夏，刺史杜彥光、拓拔乾暉不能守，悉其眾南奔，虜遂有其地。

translations.literal: Tubo attacked Yan, Xia; prefects Du Yanguang, Tuo Ba Qianhui could not defend; all their hosts south fled; barbarians then had those lands.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet attacked Yan and Xia; prefects Du Yanguang and Tuo Ba Qianhui could not hold; they led all their forces south in flight, and the barbarians then possessed those lands.

sentences.zh: 天子以邊人殘沒，下詔避正殿，痛自咎。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven because frontier people slaughtered annihilated; issued edict avoiding main hall; bitterly self-blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Because frontier people had been slaughtered and wiped out, the Son of Heaven issued an edict to avoid the main audience hall and bitterly blamed himself.

sentences.zh: 詔駱元光經略鹽、夏。

translations.literal: Edict made Luo Yuanguang commissioner over Yan, Xia.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Luo Yuanguang to oversee Yan and Xia.

sentences.zh: 三年，命左庶子崔瀚、李铦踵使。

translations.literal: Third year; ordered Left Palace Companion Cui Han, Li Qian to follow as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he appointed Left Palace Companion Cui Han and Li Qian to follow as envoys.

sentences.zh: 結贊得鹽、夏，皆戍以兵，乃自屯鳴沙，然饋餉數困。

translations.literal: Jiezan obtained Yan, Xia; all garrisoned with troops; then himself encamped Mingsha; yet provisions repeatedly strained.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan took Yan and Xia, garrisoned them with troops, and himself encamped at Mingsha, yet supplies were repeatedly strained.

sentences.zh: 於是駱元光、韓遊瑰濱塞而屯，而燧次石州，跨河相掎角。

translations.literal: Thereupon Luo Yuanguang, Han Yougui along passes encamped; Ma Sui halted Shizhou; across river mutually braced like pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Luo Yuanguang and Han Yougui encamped along the border passes, while Ma Sui held at Shizhou; across the river they braced each other like pincers.

sentences.zh: 結贊大懼，屢請盟，天子不許。

translations.literal: Jiezan greatly feared; repeatedly requested alliance; Son of Heaven did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan was greatly afraid and repeatedly asked for an alliance; the Son of Heaven would not agree.

sentences.zh: 即以貴將論頰熱厚賂乞和於燧，燧以為情，身入見天子，諸將以燧入，皆守壁不戰。

translations.literal: Then used noble general Lun Xia're thick bribes begging peace from Sui; Sui took it as sincere feeling; personally entered audience Son of Heaven; generals because Sui entered all held walls did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent the noble general Lun Xia're with lavish bribes to beg peace from Ma Sui; Sui took it as sincere and went in person to audience with the emperor; the generals, because Sui had gone in, all held their walls and did not fight.

sentences.zh: 結贊遽還走，馬多死，士不能步，有饑色。

translations.literal: Jiezan hastily returned fled; horses mostly died; soldiers could not walk; had hunger look.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan hurriedly turned back and fled; most of the horses died; the soldiers could not walk and showed signs of hunger.

sentences.zh: 瀚始至鳴沙，傳詔讓結贊破約陷鹽、夏，對曰：「本以武亭功未償乃來，又候碑仆，疆埸不明，故行境上。

translations.literal: Han first reached Mingsha; transmitted edict reproaching Jiezan breaking covenant seizing Yan, Xia; replied: Originally because Wuting merit not repaid thus came; also awaited stele fallen; border unclear; therefore marched frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Han first reached Mingsha he transmitted an edict reproaching Jiezan for breaking the covenant and seizing Yan and Xia. Jiezan replied: "I came because Wuting merit had not been repaid; I also awaited the stele's fall—the border was unclear—so I marched on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 涇州乘城自保，鳳翔李令不納吾使，雖康成等來，皆不能致委曲。

translations.literal: Jingzhou manned walls self-defended; Fengxiang Li Ling did not admit my envoys; although Kang Cheng and others came, all could not convey full particulars.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou manned its walls for self-defense; Li Ling of Fengxiang would not admit my envoys; though Kang Cheng and others came, none could convey the full particulars.

sentences.zh: 我日望大臣而卒無至者，我故引還。

translations.literal: I daily looked for great ministers yet in end none came; I therefore drew back.
translations.idiomatic: I daily looked for great ministers, yet in the end none came, so I withdrew.

sentences.zh: 鹽、夏守將懼吾眾，以城丐我，非我敢攻也。

translations.literal: Yan, Xia defending generals feared my host; offered cities begging me; not I dared attack of myself.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan and Xia defending generals feared my forces and offered the cities to beg me—it was not that I dared attack on my own.

sentences.zh: 若天子復許盟，虜之願也，唯所命，當以鹽、夏還唐。」

translations.literal: If Son of Heaven again grants alliance, barbarians' wish; only as commanded; shall return Yan, Xia to Tang."
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor again grants alliance, that is the barbarians' wish; whatever is commanded, we shall return Yan and Xia to Tang."

sentences.zh: 又言清水盟，大臣少，故約易壞，請悉遣宰相元帥二十一人會盟。

translations.literal: He also said Qingshui alliance great ministers few; therefore pact easily broken; requested all send chancellors marshals twenty-one to meet in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that at the Qingshui alliance the great ministers were few, so the pact was easily broken, and asked that all twenty-one chancellors and marshals be sent to meet in alliance.

sentences.zh: 並言靈鹽節度使杜希全、涇原節度使李觀，外蕃所信，請主盟。

translations.literal: Also said Lingyan military governor Du Xiquan, Jingyuan military governor Li Guan, outer barbarians trusted; requested preside over alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Lingyan governor Du Xiquan and Jingyuan governor Li Guan were trusted by the outer barbarians and asked that they preside over the alliance.

sentences.zh: 帝復使瀚報結贊曰：「希全守靈州，有分地，不可以越境；

translations.literal: Emperor again sent Han to reply Jiezan: Xiquan guards Lingzhou, has allotted territory; cannot cross border;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Han to reply to Jiezan: "Xiquan guards Lingzhou and has allotted territory; he cannot cross the border;

sentences.zh: 觀既徙官，以渾瑊為盟會使。」

translations.literal: Guan already transferred office; made Hun Zhen alliance convenor."
translations.idiomatic: Guan has already been transferred; Hun Zhen is made alliance convenor."

sentences.zh: 約五月盟清水，使先效二州，以驗虜信。

translations.literal: Agreed fifth month ally Qingshui; envoys first surrender two prefectures to verify barbarian sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed to ally at Qingshui in the fifth month, with envoys first to surrender the two prefectures to verify barbarian sincerity.

sentences.zh: 結贊辭清水非吉地，請會原州之土梨樹，乃歸二州。

translations.literal: Jiezan declined Qingshui not auspicious place; requested meet Yuanzhou Tuli tree; then return two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan declined Qingshui as an inauspicious site and requested meeting at the Tuli tree of Yuanzhou; then he would return the two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 天子從之。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven agreed.

sentences.zh: 瑊來受命，拜漢衡兵部尚書以副瑊。

translations.literal: Zhen came received commission; appointed Han Heng Minister of War as deputy to Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen came to receive the commission; Han Heng was appointed Minister of War as Zhen's deputy.

sentences.zh: 瑊率師二萬待期，詔駱元光助之。

translations.literal: Zhen led army twenty thousand awaiting appointed day; edict ordered Luo Yuanguang assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen led twenty thousand troops awaiting the appointed day; an edict ordered Luo Yuanguang to assist him.

sentences.zh: 宰相議所盟地，左神策將馬有鄰建言：「土梨樹林薈巖阻，兵易詭伏，不如平涼夷漫坦直，且近涇，緩急可保也。」

translations.literal: Chancellors debated alliance site; Left Divine Strategy general Ma Youlin submitted: Tuli tree grove dense cliffs barriers; troops easy trick ambush; better Pingliang level open straight; also near Jing; urgency ease can secure."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors debated the alliance site; Left Divine Strategy general Ma Youlin said: "The Tuli tree grove is dense with cliffs and barriers, and troops are easy to ambush by trickery—better Pingliang, level and open, and near Jing; in urgency or ease it can be secured."

sentences.zh: 乃定盟平涼。

translations.literal: Thus fixed alliance Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they fixed the alliance at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 瑊約結贊，主客均以兵三千至壇外，誕從四百叩壇，以遊軍交邏相入。

translations.literal: Zhen arranged with Jiezan host guest each with troops three thousand to outside altar; four hundred attendants approached altar; patrol forces mutually entered and out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen arranged with Jiezan that host and guest each bring three thousand troops to outside the altar, four hundred attendants to approach the altar, and patrol forces to enter and out in rotation.

sentences.zh: 將盟，結贊伏精騎三萬於西，縱邏騎出入瑊軍，瑊將梁奉貞亦駷馬入虜軍營，陰執之，而瑊不知也。

translations.literal: About to ally; Jiezan hid elite cavalry thirty thousand west; let patrol cavalry pass in out Zhen army; Zhen general Liang Fengzhen also spurred horse into barbarian camp; secretly seized him; yet Zhen did not know.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to ally, Jiezan hid thirty thousand elite cavalry to the west and let patrol horsemen pass through Zhen's army; Zhen's general Liang Fengzhen also spurred into the barbarian camp and was secretly seized, yet Zhen did not know.

sentences.zh: 客請瑊等具冠劍，皆就幄更衣，從容胖肆。

translations.literal: Guests requested Zhen and others fully cap sword; all went to tent change clothes; at ease expansive.
translations.idiomatic: The guests asked Zhen and the others to don caps and swords; all went to the tent to change clothes, at ease and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 虜忽三伐鼓，眾噪而興，瑊不知所出，走幄後，得馬不銜而馳，十里始得銜。

translations.literal: Barbarians suddenly thrice beat drums; crowd clamored rose; Zhen did not know which way out; ran behind tent; got horse without bit galloped; ten li before obtained bit.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians suddenly thrice beat drums; the crowd clamored and rose; Zhen did not know which way to flee; he ran behind the tent, mounted a horse without a bit and galloped, and went ten li before obtaining a bit.

sentences.zh: 虜追，矢若雨不傷也，至元光營乃脫。

translations.literal: Barbarians pursued; arrows like rain did not harm; reached Yuanguang camp then escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians pursued; arrows fell like rain yet did not harm him; reaching Yuanguang's camp he escaped.

sentences.zh: 裨將辛榮兵數百據北阜與虜戰，矢盡乃降。

translations.literal: Vice general Xin Rong troops several hundred held north hill fought barbarians; arrows exhausted then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Vice general Xin Rong with several hundred men held the north hill and fought the barbarians; when arrows were exhausted he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 判官韓弇、監軍宋鳳朝死之。

translations.literal: Judge Han Mian, supervising commissioner Song Fengchao died.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Han Mian and supervising commissioner Song Fengchao were killed.

sentences.zh: 漢衡與判官鄭叔矩路泌、掌書記袁同直、列將扶余準馬寧孟日華李至言樂演明範澄馬弇、中人劉延邕俱文珍李朝清等六十人皆被執，士死者五百，生獲者千餘人。

translations.literal: Han Heng with judges Zheng Shuju, Lu Bi, secretary Yuan Tongzhi, column generals Fuyu Zhun, Ma Ning, Meng Rihua, Li Zhiyan, Yue Yanming, Fan Cheng, Ma Yan, eunuchs Liu Yanyong, Ju Wenzhen, Li Chaoqing and sixty others all seized; soldiers dead five hundred; living captured over one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Han Heng, judges Zheng Shuju and Lu Bi, secretary Yuan Tongzhi, generals Fuyu Zhun, Ma Ning, Meng Rihua, Li Zhiyan, Yue Yanming, Fan Cheng, and Ma Yan, eunuchs Liu Yanyong, Ju Wenzhen, Li Chaoqing, and sixty others were all seized; five hundred soldiers died and more than a thousand were captured alive.

sentences.zh: 漢衡語虜曰：「我，崔尚書也，結贊與我善。

translations.literal: Han Heng said to barbarians: I am Vice Director Cui; Jiezan and I on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Han Heng said to the barbarians: "I am Vice Director Cui; Jiezan and I are on good terms.

sentences.zh: 若殺我，結贊亦殺若。」

translations.literal: If kill me, Jiezan also will kill you."
translations.idiomatic: If you kill me, Jiezan will also kill you."

sentences.zh: 乃不死。

translations.literal: Thus did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he did not die.

sentences.zh: 人負一木，以繩三約之，系其發驅之；

translations.literal: Each man bore one log; with rope thrice bound; tied their hair drove them;
translations.idiomatic: Each man bore a log, bound thrice with rope, tied by the hair and driven along;

sentences.zh: 夜則杙地系而仆，蒙以罽，守者寢其上。

translations.literal: at night then pegged ground tied and made lie; covered with felt; guards slept atop them.
translations.idiomatic: at night they were pegged to the ground, tied, and made to lie down, covered with felt, while guards slept on top of them.

sentences.zh: 始結贊將劫希全、觀，急以銳兵直趣京師，既不克，又欲禽瑊等，搗虛入寇，其謀本然。

translations.literal: Initially Jiezan intended seize Xiquan, Guan; hastened elite troops straight toward capital; when not succeeded also wished capture Zhen and others; raid emptiness invade; plan was originally so.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Jiezan had intended to seize Xiquan and Guan and hurry elite troops straight toward the capital; when that failed he also wished to capture Zhen and others and raid in weakness to invade—the plan had been so from the start.

sentences.zh: 既引去，至故原州，坐帳中見漢衡等，慢言：「渾瑊戰武功，我力也。

translations.literal: After drew away; reached old Yuanzhou; seated in tent received Han Heng and others; said dismissively: Hun Zhen fought Wugong—that was my strength.
translations.idiomatic: After he withdrew, reaching old Yuanzhou, he sat in his tent and received Han Heng and the others, saying dismissively: "Hun Zhen fought at Wugong—that was my doing.

sentences.zh: 許裂地償我，而自食其言。

translations.literal: Promised cede land compensate me; yet himself ate his words.
translations.idiomatic: He promised to cede land to compensate me, yet himself broke his word.

sentences.zh: 吾既作金枷，將必得瑊以見贊普，乃今失之，徒致公等，無益也。

translations.literal: I already made golden cage; intended surely get Zhen to present tsanpo; now lost him; only brought you gentlemen; of no use.
translations.idiomatic: I had already made a golden cage intending surely to get Zhen to present to the tsanpo; now I have lost him—only bringing you gentlemen, of no use.

sentences.zh: 當使人歸報。」

translations.literal: Shall send someone return report."
translations.idiomatic: I shall send someone back to report."

sentences.zh: 初，漢衡遇亂，從史呂溫身蔽兵，溫傷而漢衡脫，虜人嘉其義，厚給養之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Han Heng met turmoil attendant Lu Wen body screened weapons; Wen wounded yet Han Heng escaped; barbarians admired his righteousness; generously supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Heng met the turmoil, attendant Lu Wen shielded him with his body; Wen was wounded yet Han Heng escaped; the barbarians admired his loyalty and gave him generous support.

sentences.zh: 結贊屯石門，以俱文珍、馬寧、馬弇歸唐，而囚漢衡、叔矩河州，辛榮廓州，扶余準鄯州。

translations.literal: Jiezan encamped Shimen; sent Ju Wenzhen, Ma Ning, Ma Yan back Tang; imprisoned Han Heng, Shuju at Hezhou; Xin Rong Kuozhou; Fuyu Zhun Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan encamped at Shimen, sent Ju Wenzhen, Ma Ning, and Ma Yan back to Tang, and imprisoned Han Heng and Shuju at Hezhou, Xin Rong at Kuozhou, and Fuyu Zhun at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝猶使中人賫詔書賜結贊，拒不受。

translations.literal: Emperor still sent eunuch bearing edict bestow Jiezan; refused did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still sent a eunuch bearing an edict to bestow on Jiezan; he refused and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 虜戍鹽、夏，涉春疫大興，皆思歸。

translations.literal: Barbarians garrisoned Yan, Xia; passing spring epidemic greatly arose; all wished return.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians garrisoned Yan and Xia; when spring came epidemic broke out greatly and all wished to return.

sentences.zh: 結贊以騎三千迎之，火二州廬舍，頹郛堞而去，杜希全分兵保之。

translations.literal: Jiezan with cavalry three thousand went to meet them; burned two prefectures dwellings; toppled ramparts and left; Du Xiquan divided troops secured them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan went with three thousand cavalry to meet them, burned the dwellings of the two prefectures, toppled the ramparts, and withdrew; Du Xiquan divided troops to secure them.

sentences.zh: 帝哀漢衡等陷辱，下詔賜其子七品官，叔矩、泌、弇、日華、榮、至言、澄、良賁、演明一子八品官，袁同直而下一子九品官。

translations.literal: Emperor pitied Han Heng and others fallen disgrace; issued edict bestowed their sons seventh-rank office; Shuju, Bi, Yan, Rihua, Rong, Zhiyan, Cheng, Liangben, Yanming one son each eighth-rank; Yuan Tongzhi and below one son ninth-rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied Han Heng and others in captivity and disgrace; he issued an edict granting their sons seventh-rank offices, one son of Shuju, Bi, Yan, Rihua, Rong, Zhiyan, Cheng, Liangben, and Yanming each eighth-rank, and one son of Yuan Tongzhi and those below ninth-rank.

sentences.zh: 以決勝軍使唐良臣屯潘原，神策將蘇太平屯隴州。

translations.literal: Made victory-deciding army commissioner Tang Liangchen encamp Panyuan; Divine Strategy general Su Taiping encamp Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Victory-deciding army commissioner Tang Liangchen was posted at Panyuan, and Divine Strategy general Su Taiping at Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 結贊召漢衡、日華、延邕至石門，以五騎送境上，遣使者奉表來。

translations.literal: Jiezan summoned Han Heng, Rihua, Yanyong to Shimen; with five riders sent them to border; dispatched envoys bearing memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan summoned Han Heng, Rihua, and Yanyong to Shimen, sent them to the border with five riders, and dispatched envoys bearing a memorial.

sentences.zh: 李觀曰：「有詔不內吐蕃使者。」

translations.literal: Li Guan said: There is edict not to admit Tubo envoys."
translations.idiomatic: Li Guan said: "There is an edict not to admit Tibetan envoys."

sentences.zh: 受漢衡等，放其使。

translations.literal: Received Han Heng and others; released their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He received Han Heng and the others and released their envoys.

sentences.zh: 結贊以羌、渾眾屯潘口，傍青石嶺，三分其兵趨隴、汧陽間，連營數十里，中軍距鳳翔一舍，詭漢服，號邢君牙兵，入吳山、寶雞，焚聚落，略畜牧、丁壯，殺老孺，斷手剔目，乃去。

translations.literal: Jiezan with Qiang, Hun hosts encamped Pankou; along Qingshi ridge; divided his troops three parts toward Long, Qianyang; linked camps several tens of li; center army one stage from Fengxiang; feigned Han dress; called themselves Xing Junya's troops; entered Wushan, Baoji; burned settlements; plundered livestock, strong youths; killed old and infants; severed hands gouged eyes; then left.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan with Qiang and Hun forces encamped at Pankou along Qingshi Ridge, divided his troops in three toward Long and Qianyang, and linked camps for several tens of li; the center army was one stage from Fengxiang; feigning Han dress they called themselves Xing Junya's troops, entered Wushan and Baoji, burned settlements, plundered livestock and strong youths, killed the old and infants, severed hands and gouged out eyes, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李晟嘗蹙大木塞安化隘處，虜過，悉焚之。

translations.literal: Li Sheng once piled large timbers blocking Anhua pass; barbarians passed; all burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng had once piled large timbers to block Anhua Pass; when the barbarians passed they burned them all.

sentences.zh: 詔神策將石季章壁武功，良臣移師百里城。

translations.literal: Edict ordered Divine Strategy general Shi Jizhang fortify Wugong; Liangchen moved army Bailicheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Divine Strategy general Shi Jizhang to fortify Wugong, and Liangchen moved his army to Bailicheng.

sentences.zh: 虜又剽汧陽、華亭男女萬人以畀羌、渾，將出塞，令東向辭國，眾慟哭，投塹谷死者千數。

translations.literal: Barbarians again plundered Qianyang, Huating men and women ten thousand to give Qiang, Hun; about to leave passes; ordered face east bid farewell homeland; crowd wailed; threw into ditches valleys dead several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians again plundered ten thousand men and women of Qianyang and Huating to give to the Qiang and Hun; as they were about to leave the passes they were ordered to face east and bid farewell to their country; the crowd wailed, and thousands died throwing themselves into ditches and ravines.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃又入豐義，圍華亭，絕汲道。

translations.literal: Tubo again entered Fengyi; besieged Huating; cut off water-drawing route.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet again entered Fengyi, besieged Huating, and cut off the water route.

sentences.zh: 守將王仙鶴請救於隴州，刺史蘇清沔合太平兵赴之，虜逆戰，太平不勝，引還。

translations.literal: Defending general Wang Xianhe requested rescue from Longzhou; prefect Su Qingmian combined Taiping troops went; barbarians met battle; Taiping did not prevail; withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Defender Wang Xianhe requested rescue from Longzhou; prefect Su Qingmian combined Taiping's troops to go; the barbarians met them in battle; Taiping did not prevail and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 虜日千騎四掠，隴兵不敢出。

translations.literal: Barbarians daily thousand cavalry raided on four sides; Long troops dared not sortie.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians daily sent a thousand cavalry to raid on four sides, and Long troops dared not sortie.

sentences.zh: 虜積薪將焚華亭，仙鶴以眾降。

translations.literal: Barbarians piled firewood intending burn Huating; Xianhe with his host surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians piled firewood intending to burn Huating; Xianhe surrendered with his force.

sentences.zh: 清沔潛兵大象龕，夜半，約城中舉火燭天，虜眾驚，因襲其營，乃去。

translations.literal: Qingmian secretly sent troops Daxiang grotto; midnight coordinated with city raise fires lighting sky; barbarian host startled; then raided their camp; then left.
translations.idiomatic: Qingmian secretly sent troops to Daxiang grotto; at midnight he coordinated with the city to raise fires lighting the sky; the barbarian host panicked; they raided the camp and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 更攻連雲堡，飛石投中，井皆滿。

translations.literal: Again attacked Lianyun fort; flying stones struck home; all wells filled.
translations.idiomatic: They again attacked Lianyun Fort; flying stones struck home and all the wells were filled.

sentences.zh: 為虛梁絕塹而升，守將張明遠降於虜。

translations.literal: Made false bridges cut moats and ascended; defending general Zhang Mingyuan surrendered to barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: They made false bridges and cut the moats to ascend; defending general Zhang Mingyuan surrendered to the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 虜分捕山間亡人及牛羊率萬計，涇、隴、邠之民蕩然盡矣。

translations.literal: Barbarians separately captured mountain fugitives and cattle sheep numbering tens of thousands; people of Jing, Long, Bin utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians separately captured mountain fugitives and cattle and sheep numbering tens of thousands in all; the people of Jing, Long, and Bin were utterly swept away.

sentences.zh: 諸將曾不能得一俘，但賀賊出塞而已。

translations.literal: Generals could not obtain even one captive; only congratulated bandits left passes.
translations.idiomatic: The generals could not obtain even one captive; they only congratulated themselves that the bandits had left the passes.

sentences.zh: 連雲堡，涇要地也，三垂峭絕，北據高，虜所進退，候火易通。

translations.literal: Lianyun fort was Jing strategic place; three faces precipitous sheer; north held heights; barbarian advance retreat; signal fires easily communicated.
translations.idiomatic: Lianyun Fort was a Jing strategic point, precipitous on three sides, holding the heights to the north—barbarian advance and retreat; signal fires easily communicated.

sentences.zh: 既失之，城下即虜境，每藝稼，必陳兵於野，故多失時。

translations.literal: Once lost; below walls was barbarian territory; whenever planting crops must array troops in open; therefore often missed season.
translations.idiomatic: Once it was lost, below the walls was barbarian territory; whenever they planted crops they had to array troops in the open, so they often missed the season.

sentences.zh: 是歲，三州不宿麥。

translations.literal: That year three prefectures did not winter wheat.
translations.idiomatic: That year the three prefectures did not plant winter wheat.

sentences.zh: 虜數千騎犯長武城，城使韓全義拒之。

translations.literal: Barbarians several thousand cavalry violated Changwu fort; fort commissioner Han Quanyi resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand barbarian cavalry attacked Changwu Fort; fort commissioner Han Quanyi resisted them.

sentences.zh: 韓遊瑰兵不出，於是虜安行邠、涇間，諸屯西門皆閉，虜治故原州保之。

translations.literal: Han Yougui's troops did not sortie; thereupon barbarians passed at ease between Bin, Jing; all garrisons' west gates closed; barbarians repaired old Yuanzhou and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui's troops did not sortie; thereupon the barbarians passed at ease between Bin and Jing; all garrison west gates were closed; the barbarians repaired old Yuanzhou and held it.

sentences.zh: 帝取所獲吐蕃生口不二百，徇諸市以安京師。

translations.literal: Emperor took captured Tubo living captives fewer than two hundred; displayed through markets to reassure capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took fewer than two hundred captured Tibetan captives alive and paraded them through the markets to reassure the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，虜三萬騎略涇、邠、寧、慶、鄜五州之鄙，焚吏舍民閻，系執數萬。

translations.literal: Fourth year fifth month; barbarians thirty thousand cavalry raided outskirts of Jing, Bin, Ning, Qing, Fu; burned officials' quarters commoners' lanes; bound seized tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year thirty thousand barbarian cavalry raided the outskirts of Jing, Bin, Ning, Qing, and Fu, burned officials' quarters and commoners' lanes, and bound and seized tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 韓全義以陳許兵戰長武，無功。

translations.literal: Han Quanyi with Chenxu troops fought Changwu; no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanyi fought at Changwu with Chenxu troops without success.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃盜塞，畏春夏疾疫，常以盛秋。

translations.literal: Initially Tubo raided passes; feared spring-summer epidemics; usually came in full autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Tibet raided the passes, fearing spring and summer epidemics, and usually came in full autumn.

sentences.zh: 及是得唐俘，多厚給產，質其孥，故盛夏入邊。

translations.literal: By this time having obtained Tang captives; many generously gave property; held their families as pledges; therefore high summer entered frontier.
translations.idiomatic: By this time, having obtained Tang captives, they gave many generous grants of property and held their families as pledges, so they entered the frontier in high summer.

sentences.zh: 尚悉董星、論莽羅等又寇寧州，張獻甫拒斬裁百級，轉剽鄜、坊乃去。

translations.literal: Shang Xidongxing, Lun Mangluo and others again raided Ningzhou; Zhang Xianfu resisted beheaded barely hundred heads; turned plunder Fu, Fang then left.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Xidongxing, Lun Mangluo, and others again raided Ningzhou; Zhang Xianfu resisted and beheaded barely a hundred, then turned to plunder Fu and Fang before leaving.

sentences.zh: 五年，韋臯以劍南兵戰臺登，殺虜將乞臧遮遮、悉多楊朱，西南少安。

translations.literal: Fifth year Wei Gao with Jiannan troops fought Taideng; killed barbarian generals Qizang Zhezhe, Siduo Yangzhu; southwest somewhat quiet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Wei Gao with Jiannan troops fought at Taideng, killed the barbarian generals Qizang Zhezhe and Siduo Yangzhu, and the southwest was somewhat quiet.

sentences.zh: 不三年，盡得巂州地。

translations.literal: Within less than three years entirely obtained Xi prefecture territory.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than three years he entirely recovered Xi prefecture's territory.

sentences.zh: 久之，北庭沙陀別部叛，吐蕃因是陷北庭都護府，安西道絕。

translations.literal: After long while Beiting Shatuo separate division rebelled; Tubo thereby took Beiting Protectorate; Anxi route cut off.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the Beiting Shatuo separate division rebelled; Tibet thereby took the Beiting Protectorate and the Anxi route was cut off.

sentences.zh: 獨西州人尚為唐守。

translations.literal: Only Xizhou people still held for Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Only the people of Xizhou still held for Tang.

sentences.zh: 八年，寇靈州，陷水口，塞營田渠。

translations.literal: Eighth year raided Lingzhou; took Shuikou; blocked garrison-farm canals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year they raided Lingzhou, took Shuikou, and blocked the garrison-farm canals.

sentences.zh: 發河東、振武兵，合神策軍擊之，虜引還。

translations.literal: Deployed Hedong, Zhenwu troops; combined Divine Strategy army struck them; barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong and Zhenwu troops were deployed, combined with the Divine Strategy army to strike them, and the barbarians withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又寇涇州，掠田軍千人，守捉使唐朝臣戰不利。

translations.literal: Again raided Jingzhou; plundered Tiantian army thousand men; frontier guard commissioner Tang Chaochen fought unsuccessfully.
translations.idiomatic: They again raided Jingzhou, plundered a thousand men of the Tiantian army, and frontier guard commissioner Tang Chaochen fought unsuccessfully.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使嚴震破虜於芳州，取黑水壁，焚積聚。

translations.literal: South of Mountains West Circuit military governor Yan Zhen defeated barbarians at Fangzhou; took Heishui rampart; burned stores.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Mountains West Circuit governor Yan Zhen defeated the barbarians at Fangzhou, took Heishui rampart, and burned their stores.

sentences.zh: 自虜得鹽州，塞防無以障遏，而靈武單露，鄜、坊侵迫，寇日以驕，數入為邊患。

translations.literal: Since barbarians obtained Yanzhou; pass defenses had nothing to block; Lingwu stood exposed alone; Fu, Fang pressed; raids daily grew arrogant; repeatedly entered as frontier troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Since the barbarians obtained Yanzhou, the pass defenses had nothing to block them, Lingwu stood exposed alone, Fu and Fang were pressed, raids grew daily more arrogant, and they repeatedly entered as frontier troubles.

sentences.zh: 帝復詔城之，使涇原、劍南、山南深入窮討，分其兵，毋令專向東方。

translations.literal: Emperor again ordered city built; sent Jingyuan, Jiannan, south of mountains to penetrate deep exhaustive pursuit; divide their troops; not let focus only east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered the city built and sent Jingyuan, Jiannan, and the south of the mountains to pursue deep in exhaustive raids, divide their forces, and not let them focus only on the east.

sentences.zh: 詔朔方河中晉絳邠寧兵馬副元帥渾瑊、朔方靈鹽豐夏綏銀節度都統杜希全、邠寧節度使張獻甫、右神策軍行營節度使邢君牙、夏綏銀節度使韓潭、鄜坊丹延節度使王棲曜、振武麟勝節度使範希朝合兵三萬，以左神策將軍胡堅、右神策將軍張昌為鹽州行營節度使，板築之，役者六千人，餘皆陣城下。

translations.literal: Edict: Shuofang Hezhong Jin Jiang Bin Ning deputy marshal Hun Zhen; Shuofang Lingyan Feng Xia Sui Yin overall commander Du Xiquan; Binning governor Zhang Xianfu; Right Divine Strategy field army governor Xing Junya; Xia Sui Yin governor Han Tan; Fu Fang Dan Yan governor Wang Qiyao; Zhenwu Linsheng governor Fan Xichao combined army thirty thousand; Left Divine Strategy generals Hu Jian, Right Zhang Chang made Yanzhou field army governors; timbered walls; laborers six thousand; rest all arrayed below city.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered deputy marshals Hun Zhen of Shuofang, Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Bin, and Ning; overall commander Du Xiquan of Shuofang, Lingyan, Feng, Xia, Sui, and Yin; Binning governor Zhang Xianfu; Right Divine Strategy field army governor Xing Junya; Xia-Sui-Yin governor Han Tan; Fu-Fang-Dan-Yan governor Wang Qiyao; and Zhenwu-Linsheng governor Fan Xichao to combine thirty thousand troops; Left Divine Strategy generals Hu Jian and Right Zhang Chang were made Yanzhou field army governors to build the walls—six thousand laborers, the rest arrayed below the city.

sentences.zh: 九年始栽，閱二旬訖功，而虜兵不出，遂以兼御史大夫紇幹遂與兼中丞杜彥光戍之。

translations.literal: Ninth year planting began; within twenty days work finished; yet barbarian troops did not sortie; thereupon concurrent Grand Censorate Commissioner Qagan Sui and concurrent Vice Censorate Commissioner Du Yanguang garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year planting began; within twenty days the work was finished, yet barbarian troops did not sortie; thereupon concurrent Grand Censorate commissioner Qagan Sui and concurrent vice commissioner Du Yanguang garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 當是時，韋臯功最多，破堡壁五十餘所，敗其南道元帥論莽熱沒籠乞悉蓖；

translations.literal: At that time Wei Gao's achievements were greatest; broke forts ramparts over fifty; defeated their southern-route marshal Lun Mangre Molong Qixipi;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Gao's achievements were greatest—he broke more than fifty forts and ramparts and defeated their southern-route marshal Lun Mangre Molong Qixipi;

sentences.zh: 又與南詔破之於神川、於鐵橋，臯俘馘三萬，降首領論乞髯湯沒藏悉諾硉。

translations.literal: again with Nanzhao defeated them at Shenchuan, at Iron Bridge; Gao captured thirty thousand heads; accepted surrender of chieftains Lun Qiran, Tangmeizang, Sinuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: again with Nanzhao he defeated them at Shenchuan and at Iron Bridge—Gao took thirty thousand heads and accepted the surrender of chieftains Lun Qiran, Tangmeizang, and Sinuoluo.

sentences.zh: 十二年，寇慶州及華池，殺略吏人。

translations.literal: Twelfth year raided Qingzhou and Huachi; killed plundered officials people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year they raided Qingzhou and Huachi, killing and plundering officials and people.

sentences.zh: 是歲，尚結贊死。

translations.literal: That year Shang Jiezan died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shang Jiezan died.

sentences.zh: 明年，贊普死，其子足之煎立。

translations.literal: Next year tsanpo died; his son Trizig was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the tsanpo died; his son Trizig was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 邢君牙築永信城於隴州以備虜，虜使者農桑昔來請脩好，朝廷以其無信，不受。

translations.literal: Xing Junya built Yongxin fort at Longzhou to guard against barbarians; barbarian envoy Nongsangxi came requesting restored good relations; court because they untrustworthy did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Junya built Yongxin Fort at Longzhou to guard against the barbarians; barbarian envoy Nongsangxi came to request restored good relations; the court, finding them untrustworthy, did not accept.

sentences.zh: 韋臯取新城，虜治劍山、馬嶺，進寇臺登，巂州刺史曹高仕擊卻之，禽籠官，斬級三百，獲馬、糧、械數千。

translations.literal: Wei Gao took Xincheng; barbarians repaired Jianshan, Maling; advanced raided Taideng; Xi prefect Cao Gaoshi struck repelled them; captured Longguan; beheaded three hundred heads; obtained horses, grain, weapons several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao took Xincheng; the barbarians repaired Jianshan and Maling and advanced to raid Taideng; Xi prefect Cao Gaoshi struck and drove them back, captured Longguan, beheaded three hundred, and obtained thousands of horses, grain, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 十四年，韓全義破虜於鹽州。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year Han Quanyi defeated barbarians at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Han Quanyi defeated the barbarians at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，靈州破虜於烏蘭橋，韋臯拔末恭、颙二城。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year Lingzhou defeated barbarians at Wulan Bridge; Wei Gao took Mogong, Yong two cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Lingzhou defeated the barbarians at Wulan Bridge; Wei Gao took the two cities of Mogong and Yong.

sentences.zh: 十七年，寇鹽州，陷麟州，殺刺史郭鋒，湮隍墮陴，系居人，掠党項諸部，屯橫槽烽。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year; raided Yanzhou; took Linzhou; killed prefect Guo Feng; filled moats toppled walls; bound residents; plundered Tangut tribes; encamped Hengcao beacon.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year they raided Yanzhou, took Linzhou, and killed Prefect Guo Feng; they filled the moats and toppled the walls, bound the inhabitants, plundered the Tangut tribes, and encamped at Hengcao Beacon.

sentences.zh: 虜將徐舍人者，語俘道人延素曰：「我乃司空英公裔孫也。

translations.literal: Barbarian general called Xu Sheren; spoke to captive monk Yansu: I am descendant of Duke Ying the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A barbarian general called Xu Sheren spoke to the captive monk Yansu and said: "I am a descendant of Duke Ying, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 武后時，家祖以兵尊王室不克，子孫奔播絕域，今三世矣。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time; our forebear with troops upheld royal house but failed; descendants fled to far borderlands; now three generations.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's time my forebear raised troops to uphold the royal house but failed; his descendants fled to the far borderlands—it has been three generations now.

sentences.zh: 我雖握兵，心未嘗忘歸也，顧不能自拔耳。」

translations.literal: Though I hold troops; heart never forgot returning; only cannot extricate myself."
translations.idiomatic: Though I hold troops, my heart has never forgotten returning—only that I cannot extricate myself."

sentences.zh: 陰使延素夜逸。

translations.literal: He secretly had Yansu escape by night.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly had Yansu escape by night.

sentences.zh: 又言：「吾按邊求資糧，至麟而守者無備，遂入之。

translations.literal: He also said: I pressed border seeking provisions; reaching Lin defenders unprepared; thus entered.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I was pressing the border to obtain provisions; when I reached Lin the defenders were unprepared, so we entered.

sentences.zh: 知郭使君勛臣家，欲全安之，不幸死亂兵。」

translations.literal: Knowing Commissioner Guo was meritorious minister's house; wished to preserve him in safety; unluckily died in chaotic troops."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Commissioner Guo came from a house of meritorious ministers, I wished to keep him safe; he unluckily died in the chaos of troops."

sentences.zh: 語方已，會飛鳥使至，召其軍還，遂引去。

translations.literal: Words just ended; met Feiniao envoy arrived; summoned his army back; then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: As he had just finished speaking, a flying-bird envoy arrived, summoned his army back, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 飛鳥，猶傳騎也。

translations.literal: Feiniao—like relay riders.
translations.idiomatic: "Flying bird" meant relay riders.

sentences.zh: 韋臯出西山與虜戰，破之雅州。

translations.literal: Wei Gao went out Xishan fought barbarians; defeated them at Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao went out from Xishan and fought the barbarians, defeating them at Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 籠官馬定德本虜之知兵有策慮者，周知山川險易，每用兵，常馳驛計議，授諸將以行。

translations.literal: Longguan Ma Dingde was originally among barbarians skilled in warfare with strategy; thoroughly knew mountains rivers difficult easy; whenever employing troops often sent relay post-stages to deliberate; instructed generals to execute.
translations.idiomatic: Longguan Ma Dingde had originally been among the barbarians skilled in warfare and strategy; he knew thoroughly the difficult and easy points of mountains and rivers; whenever troops were employed he often sent relays along the post-roads to deliberate plans and instruct the generals how to proceed.

sentences.zh: 比年寇黎、巂，臯常折其兵，定德畏得罪，遂來降，因定昆明諸蠻。

translations.literal: In recent years raided Li Juan; Gao often broke their forces; Dingde feared punishment; thus came to surrender; thereby pacified Kunming tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years they had raided Li and Juan; Gao often broke their forces; Dingde feared punishment and came to surrender, thereby pacifying the Kunming tribes.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以下屢叛，大侵靈州。

translations.literal: Peoples under Tibet repeatedly rebelled; greatly invaded Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The peoples subject to Tibet repeatedly rebelled and greatly invaded Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時臯圍維州，贊普使論莽熱沒籠乞悉蓖兼松州五道節度兵馬都統、群牧大使，引兵十萬援維州。

translations.literal: At the time Gao besieged Weizhou; tsenpo sent Lun Mangre Molong Qixibi as combined Songzhou five-circuit military herds commissioner; led troops hundred thousand to relieve Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gao was besieging Weizhou; the tsenpo sent Lun Mangre Molong Qixibi as combined commander of the Songzhou five-circuit forces and herds commissioner, leading a hundred thousand troops to relieve Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 臯率南詔兵薄險設伏以待，才使千人嘗敵，乞悉蓖見兵寡，悉眾追，墮伏中，兵四合急擊，遂禽之，獻京師。

translations.literal: Gao led Nanzhao troops through narrow terrain set ambush to wait; sent only thousand men to test enemy; Qixibi saw troops few; pursued with whole force; fell into ambush; troops closed four sides urgent strike; thus captured him; presented to capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gao led Nanzhao troops through narrow terrain to set an ambush and wait; he sent only a thousand men to test the enemy; Qixibi saw few troops and pursued with his whole force; he fell into the ambush; troops closed on four sides and struck urgently; they captured him and presented him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，吐蕃使者論頰熱復來，右龍武大將軍薛伾往報。

translations.literal: Next year Tibetan envoy Lun Renault came again; Right Dragon Martial grand general Xue Yi went to respond.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Tibetan envoy Lun Renault came again, and Right Dragon Martial grand general Xue Yi went to respond.

sentences.zh: 二十年，贊普死，遣工部侍郎張薦吊祠，其弟嗣立，再使使者入朝。

translations.literal: Twentieth year tsenpo died; sent Ministry of Works vice minister Zhang Jian to offer condolence sacrifices; younger brother succeeded; again sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the tsenpo died; the court sent Ministry of Works vice minister Zhang Jian to offer condolence sacrifices; his younger brother succeeded, and envoys were again sent to court.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，以左金吾衛將軍田景度、庫部員外郎熊執易持節往使，

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended; appointed Left Golden Guard general Tian Jingdu Treasury department vice director Xiong Zhiyi bearing credentials to go as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended, Left Golden Guard general Tian Jingdu and Treasury department vice director Xiong Zhiyi were appointed bearing credentials to go as envoys.

sentences.zh: 論乞縷勃藏歸金幣、馬牛助崇陵，有詔陳太極廷中。

translations.literal: Lun Qilü Bocang returned gold coins horses cattle to assist Chong Mausoleum; edict ordered display in Taiji courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Lun Qilü Bocang returned gold, coins, horses, and cattle to assist the Chong Mausoleum; an edict ordered them displayed in the Taiji courtyard.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初，遣使者脩好，且還其俘。

translations.literal: At beginning of Xianzong's reign; sent envoys to restore good relations; also returned their captives.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianzong's reign envoys were sent to restore good relations and also to return their captives.

sentences.zh: 又以使告順宗喪，吐蕃亦以論勃藏來。

translations.literal: Also sent envoys to announce Shunzong's death; Tibet also sent Lun Bocang.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were also sent to announce Shunzong's death, and Tibet likewise sent Lun Bocang.

sentences.zh: 後比年來朝，然以五萬騎入振武拂鵜泉，萬騎至豐州大石谷，鈔回鶻還國者。

translations.literal: Afterwards came to court year after year; yet with fifty thousand riders entered Zhenwu brushing Piquan; ten thousand riders reached Fengzhou Dashigu Valley; plundered Uyghurs returning to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards they came to court year after year, yet with fifty thousand riders they entered Zhenwu brushing Piquan, and ten thousand riders reached Fengzhou's Dashigu Valley to plunder Uyghurs returning to their country.

sentences.zh: 五年，以祠部郎中徐復往使，並賜缽闡布書。

translations.literal: Fifth year; sent Ministry of Rites director Xu Fu as envoy; also bestowed letter to Bonchanbu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Ministry of Rites director Xu Fu was sent as envoy, and a letter was also bestowed on Bonchanbu.

sentences.zh: 缽闡布者，虜浮屠豫國事者也，亦曰「缽掣逋」。

translations.literal: Bonchanbu was barbarian monk who deliberated state affairs; also called Bochebo.
translations.idiomatic: Bonchanbu was the barbarian monk who deliberated on state affairs; he was also called "Bochebo."

sentences.zh: 復至鄯州擅還，其副李逢致命贊普，復坐貶。

translations.literal: Fu reached Shazhou returned on own authority; his vice Li Fengming reported to tsenpo; Fu was demoted on account.
translations.idiomatic: Fu reached Shazhou and returned on his own authority; his vice Li Fengming reported to the tsenpo, and Fu was demoted on that account.

sentences.zh: 虜以論思邪熱入謝，且歸鄭叔矩、路泌之柩，因言原歸秦、原、安樂州。

translations.literal: Barbarians sent Lun Sixie to enter thanks; also returned coffins of Zheng Shuju Lu Bi; thereby requested return of Qin Yuan Anle prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians sent Lun Sixie to offer thanks, also returned the coffins of Zheng Shuju and Lu Bi, and requested the return of Qin, Yuan, and Anle prefectures.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相杜佑等與議中書，論思邪熱拜於廷，佑答拜堂上，復以鴻臚少卿李铦、丹王府長史吳暈報之。

translations.literal: Edict ordered grand counselors Du You and others to discuss at Zhongshu; Lun Sixie bowed in court; You returned bow on hall; again sent Honglu vice director Li Xian Prince of Dan chief administrator Wu Yun to respond.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered grand counselors Du You and others to discuss the matter at Zhongshu; Lun Sixie bowed in court and You returned the bow on the hall; Honglu vice director Li Xian and Prince of Dan chief administrator Wu Yun were again sent to respond.

sentences.zh: 自是朝貢歲入。

translations.literal: From this tribute came in yearly.
translations.idiomatic: From this tribute came in every year.

sentences.zh: 又款隴州塞，丐互市，詔可。

translations.literal: Again appealed at Longzhou pass; begged mutual market; edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: They again appealed at the Longzhou pass and begged for a mutual market; an edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 十二年，贊普死，使者論乞髯來，以右衛將軍烏重玘、殿中侍御史段鈞吊祭之。

translations.literal: Twelfth year tsenpo died; envoy Lun Qiran came; sent Right Guard general Wu Chongqi palace censor Duan Jun to offer condolence sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the tsenpo died; envoy Lun Qiran came; Right Guard general Wu Chongqi and palace censor Duan Jun were sent to offer condolence sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 可黎可足立為贊普，重玘以扶余準、李驂偕歸。

translations.literal: Kelikexun established as tsenpo; Chongqi returned with Fuyu Zhun Li Can.
translations.idiomatic: Kelikexun was established as tsenpo; Chongqi returned with Fuyu Zhun and Li Can.

sentences.zh: 準，東明人，本朔方騎將；

translations.literal: Zhun; native of Dongming; originally Shuofang cavalry officer;
translations.idiomatic: Zhun, a native of Dongming, had originally been a Shuofang cavalry officer;

sentences.zh: 驂，隴西人，貞元初戰沒於虜者。

translations.literal: Can; native of Longxi; who in early Zhenyuan era fell in battle to barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Can, a native of Longxi, who in the early Zhenyuan era had fallen in battle to the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 使者知不死，求之，乃得還。

translations.literal: Envoys knew they were not dead; sought them; thus obtained their return.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys knew they were not dead, sought them, and obtained their return.

sentences.zh: 詔以準為澧王府司馬，驂嘉王友。

translations.literal: Edict appointed Zhun Prince of Li household marshal; Can Prince of Jia friend.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Zhun marshal of the Prince of Li's household and Can friend to the Prince of Jia.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃使論矩立藏來朝，未出境，吐蕃寇宥州，與靈州兵戰定遠城，虜不勝，斬首二千級。

translations.literal: Tibetan envoy Lun Julizang came to court; before leaving border; Tibet raided Youzhou; fought Lingzhou troops at Dingyuan city; barbarians did not prevail; two thousand heads cut.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan envoy Lun Julizang came to court; before he had left the border Tibet raided Youzhou and fought Lingzhou troops at Dingyuan City; the barbarians did not prevail and two thousand heads were cut.

sentences.zh: 平涼鎮遏使郝玼又破虜兵二萬，夏州節度使田縉破其眾三千，詔留矩立藏等不遣。

translations.literal: Pingliang suppression commissioner Hao Qian again broke twenty thousand barbarian troops; Xiazhou circuit commissioner Tian Jin broke their force three thousand; edict detained Julizang and others without sending back.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang suppression commissioner Hao Qian again broke twenty thousand barbarian troops; Xiazhou circuit commissioner Tian Jin broke a force of three thousand; an edict detained Julizang and the others without sending them back.

sentences.zh: 劍南兵拔峨和、棲雞城。

translations.literal: Jiannan troops took Ehe Qiji cities.
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan troops took the cities of Ehe and Qiji.

sentences.zh: 十四年，乃歸矩立藏等。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year; then returned Julizang and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Julizang and the others were at last returned.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃節度論二摩、宰相尚塔藏、中書令尚綺心兒總兵十五萬圍鹽州，為飛梯、鵝車攻城，刺史李文悅拒之，城壞輒補，夜襲其營，晝出戰，破虜萬人，積三旬不能拔。

translations.literal: Tibetan commissioner Lun Erma grand counselor Shang Tacang chancellor Shang Qixiner commanded troops hundred fifty thousand besieged Yanzhou; made flying ladders goose carts to attack city; prefect Li Wenyue resisted; whenever walls broke immediately repaired; night raided their camp; day sortied to fight; broke barbarians ten thousand; accumulated thirty days could not take.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan commissioner Lun Erma, grand counselor Shang Tacang, and chancellor Shang Qixiner commanded a hundred fifty thousand troops to besiege Yanzhou; they built flying ladders and goose carts to attack the city; Prefect Li Wenyue resisted, repairing the walls whenever they broke, raiding their camp by night and fighting by day; they broke ten thousand barbarians, yet after thirty days could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 朔方將史敬奉以奇兵繞出虜背，大破之，解圍去。

translations.literal: Shuofang general Shi Jingfeng with surprise troops circled out behind barbarians; greatly broke them; lifted siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang general Shi Jingfeng with surprise troops circled behind the barbarians and broke them greatly; they lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 始，沙州刺史周鼎為唐固守，贊普徙帳南山，使尚綺心兒攻之。

translations.literal: Initially Shazhou prefect Zhou Ding held firm for Tang; tsenpo moved camp to southern mountains; sent Shang Qixiner to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Shazhou Prefect Zhou Ding held firm for Tang; the tsenpo moved his camp to the southern mountains and sent Shang Qixiner to attack.

sentences.zh: 鼎請救回鶻，逾年不至，議焚城郭，引眾東奔，皆以為不可。

translations.literal: Ding requested rescue from Uyghurs; over a year did not arrive; discussed burning city walls; leading host east to flee; all considered impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Ding requested rescue from the Uyghurs; after more than a year they had not come; he discussed burning the city walls and leading the host east to flee, but all considered it impossible.

sentences.zh: 鼎遣都知兵馬使閻朝領壯士行視水草，晨入謁辭行，與鼎親吏周沙奴共射，彀弓揖讓，射沙奴即死，執鼎而縊殺之，自領州事。

translations.literal: Ding sent military affairs commissioner Yan Chao leading stalwarts to reconnoiter water grass; morning entered audience to bid farewell; with Ding's intimate clerk Zhou Shanü shot together; drew bow bowed yielding; shot Shanü immediately dead; seized Ding and strangled him; himself took prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ding sent military affairs commissioner Yan Chao with stalwarts to reconnoiter water and pasture; in the morning Chao entered audience to bid farewell; he and Ding's intimate clerk Zhou Shanü shot together; drawing the bow with courteous yielding he shot Shanü dead at once, seized Ding and strangled him, and himself took charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城守者八年，出綾一端募麥一斗，應者甚眾。

translations.literal: City defenders eight years; offered one bolt silk to recruit one dou wheat; responders very many.
translations.idiomatic: The city had been defended for eight years; they offered one bolt of silk to recruit one dou of wheat, and very many responded.

sentences.zh: 朝喜曰：「民且有食，可以死守也。」

translations.literal: Chao rejoiced: The people will have food; can die defending firmly."
translations.idiomatic: Chao rejoiced and said: "The people will have food; we can die defending the city."

sentences.zh: 又二歲，糧械皆竭，登城而謼曰：「茍毋徙佗境，請以城降。」

translations.literal: After two more years grain weapons all exhausted; ascended walls and cried: If only not relocate to other territory; request surrender city."
translations.idiomatic: After two more years grain and weapons were all exhausted; he ascended the walls and cried: "If only we are not relocated to other territory, I ask to surrender the city."

sentences.zh: 綺心兒許諾，於是出降。

translations.literal: Qixiner promised; thereupon came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qixiner promised, and thereupon they came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 自攻城至是凡十一年。

translations.literal: From beginning siege to this altogether eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of the siege to this point it had been eleven years in all.

sentences.zh: 贊普以綺心兒代守。

translations.literal: Tsenpo had Qixiner replace to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The tsenpo had Qixiner replace him to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 後疑朝謀變，置毒靴中而死。

translations.literal: Later suspected Chao plotted mutiny; placed poison in boots and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, suspecting Chao of plotting mutiny, they placed poison in his boots and he died.

sentences.zh: 州人皆胡服臣虜，每歲時祀父祖，衣中國之服，號慟而藏之。

translations.literal: Prefecture people all wore barbarian dress submitted to barbarians; each year season sacrificed to fathers ancestors; wore China's dress; wailed mournfully and hid them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture all wore barbarian dress and submitted to the barbarians; each year when they sacrificed to their fathers and ancestors they wore Chinese dress, wailed in mourning, and hid the garments away.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，遣秘書少監田洎往告，使者亦來。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended; sent Secretariat vice director Tian Ji to announce; envoys also came.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended, Secretariat vice director Tian Ji was sent to announce it, and envoys also came.

sentences.zh: 虜引兵入屯靈武，靈州兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Barbarians led troops entered encamped Lingwu; Lingzhou troops struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians led troops in and encamped at Lingwu; Lingzhou troops struck and repelled them.

sentences.zh: 又犯青塞烽，進寇涇州，瀕水而營，綿五十里。

translations.literal: Again violated Qingsai beacon; advanced raided Jingzhou; camped along water; stretched fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: They again attacked Qingsai Beacon, advanced to raid Jingzhou, camped along the water, and stretched their lines for fifty li.

sentences.zh: 始洎至牙，虜欲會盟長武，洎含糊應之。

translations.literal: When Ji first reached court; barbarians wished to meet alliance at Changwu; Ji vaguely assented.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji first reached the Tibetan court the barbarians wished to meet for an alliance at Changwu, and Ji vaguely assented.

sentences.zh: 至是顯言：「洎許我盟，我是以來。」

translations.literal: At this openly said: Ji promised us alliance; I therefore came."
translations.idiomatic: At this they openly said: "Ji promised us an alliance—that is why I have come."

sentences.zh: 逼涇一舍止。

translations.literal: Pressed Jing one stage and halted.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed to within one stage of Jing and halted.

sentences.zh: 詔右軍中尉梁守謙為左右神策軍、京西北行營都監，發卒合八鎮兵援涇州，泛洎郴州司戶參軍，以太府少卿邵同持節為和好使。

translations.literal: Edict appointed Right Army commandant Liang Shouqian as combined Left Right Divine Strategy Armies Northwest Capital expeditionary overseer; raised troops combining eight garrisons to aid Jingzhou; demoted Ji to Chenzhou revenue clerk; appointed Grand Storehouse vice director Shao Tong bearing credentials as peace envoy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Right Army commandant Liang Shouqian overseer of the combined Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the Northwest Capital expeditionary force, raised troops from the eight garrisons to aid Jingzhou, demoted Ji to Chenzhou revenue clerk, and appointed Grand Storehouse vice director Shao Tong bearing credentials as peace envoy.

sentences.zh: 初，夏州田縉裒沓，党項怨之，導虜入鈔，郝玼與戰，多殺其眾。

translations.literal: Initially Xiazhou Tian Jin was grasping; Tangut resented him; guided barbarians in to plunder; Hao Qian fought them; killed many of their host.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Xiazhou's Tian Jin was grasping; the Tangut resented him and guided the barbarians in to plunder; Hao Qian fought them and killed many of their force.

sentences.zh: 李光顏又以邠兵至，乃引去。

translations.literal: Li Guangyan also with Bin troops arrived; then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan also arrived with Bin troops, and they then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復遣使者來。

translations.literal: Again sent envoys to come.
translations.idiomatic: They again sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 南略雅州，詔方鎮與虜接者謹備邊，

translations.literal: South raided Yazhou; edict ordered regional commands bordering barbarians carefully guard frontier.
translations.idiomatic: They raided south toward Yazhou; an edict ordered the regional commands bordering the barbarians to guard the frontier carefully.

sentences.zh: 聞回鶻和親，犯清塞堡，為李文悅所逐。

translations.literal: Hearing Uyghur peace marriage; attacked Qingsai fort; was driven off by Li Wenyue.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the Uyghur peace marriage, they attacked Qingsai Fort and were driven off by Li Wenyue.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使者尚綺力陀思來朝，且乞盟，詔許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon sent envoy Shang Qilituosi to court; also begged alliance; edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon sent envoy Shang Qilituosi to court and also begged for an alliance; an edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 崔植、杜元穎、王播輔政，議欲告廟。

translations.literal: Cui Zhi Du Yuanying Wang Bo assisted government; discussed wishing to announce at ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhi, Du Yuanying, and Wang Bo assisted the government and discussed announcing the alliance at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 禮官謂：「肅宗、代宗皆嘗與吐蕃盟，不告廟。

translations.literal: Rites officials said: Suzong Daizong both once allied with Tibet; did not announce at temple.
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials said: "Suzong and Daizong both once allied with Tibet without announcing at the temple.

sentences.zh: 德宗建中之盟，將重其約，始詔告廟。

translations.literal: Dezong's Jianzhong alliance; about to weight its covenant; first edict announced at temple.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong's Jianzhong alliance, intending to give weight to the covenant, was the first for which an edict announced it at the temple.

sentences.zh: 至會平涼，不復告，殺之也。」

translations.literal: When it came to Pingliang meeting; no longer announced; slaughter followed."
translations.idiomatic: When it came to the Pingliang meeting it was no longer announced—slaughter followed."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 以大理卿劉元鼎為盟會使，右司郎中劉師老副之，詔宰相與尚書右僕射韓臯、御史中丞牛僧孺、吏部尚書李絳、兵部尚書蕭俯、戶部尚書楊於陵、禮部尚書韋綬、太常卿趙宗儒、司農卿裴武、京兆尹柳公綽、右金吾將軍郭鏦及吐蕃使者論訥羅盟京師西郊。

translations.literal: Appointed Court of Review director Liu Yuanding as alliance commissioner; Right Department director Liu Shilao as vice; edict ordered grand counselors with Right Vice Director Han Gao Censor-in-chief Niu Sengru Personnel Director Li Jiang War Director Xiao Fu Revenue Director Yang Yuling Rites Director Wei Shou Grand Steward Zhao Zongru Agriculture Director Pei Wu Jingzhao Intendant Liu Gongchuo Right Golden Guard general Guo Chong and Tibetan envoy Lun Naluo to ally at capital western suburb.
