translations.idiomatic: Court of Review director Liu Yuanding was appointed alliance commissioner with Right Department director Liu Shilao as his deputy; an edict ordered the grand counselors together with Right Vice Director Han Gao, censor-in-chief Niu Sengru, personnel director Li Jiang, war director Xiao Fu, revenue director Yang Yuling, rites director Wei Shou, grand steward Zhao Zongru, agriculture director Pei Wu, Jingzhao intendant Liu Gongchuo, Right Golden Guard general Guo Chong, and the Tibetan envoy Lun Naluo to conclude the alliance at the western suburb of the capital.

sentences.zh: 贊普以盟言約：「二國無相寇讎，有禽生問事，給服糧歸之。」

translations.literal: Tsenpo with alliance words covenanted: Two states shall not mutually raid as foes; if living captives inquire on affairs; provide clothes grain and return them."
translations.idiomatic: The tsenpo covenanted in the alliance words: "The two states shall not raid each other as foes; if living captives inquire on affairs, provide clothes and grain and return them."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: Edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 大臣豫盟者悉載名於策。

translations.literal: Grand ministers participating in alliance all had names recorded on covenant document.
translations.idiomatic: All grand ministers participating in the alliance had their names recorded on the covenant document.

sentences.zh: 方盟時，吐蕃以壯騎屯魯州，靈州節度使李進誠與戰大石山，破之。

translations.literal: Just as alliance was made; Tibet with strong cavalry encamped Luzhou; Lingzhou circuit commissioner Li Jincheng fought at Dashishan; broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the alliance was being made Tibet stationed strong cavalry at Luzhou; Lingzhou circuit commissioner Li Jincheng fought them at Dashishan and broke them.

sentences.zh: 虜遣使者趙國章來，且致宰相信幣。

translations.literal: Barbarians sent envoy Zhao Guozhang to come; also presented grand counselor's trust gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians sent envoy Zhao Guozhang and also presented the grand counselor's trust gifts.

sentences.zh: 明年，請定疆候，元鼎與論訥羅就盟其國，敕虜大臣亦列名於策。

translations.literal: Next year; requested fixing border markers; Yuanding with Lun Naluo concluded alliance in their state; edict ordered barbarian grand ministers also list names on covenant.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they requested fixing the border markers; Yuanding and Lun Naluo concluded the alliance in their state; an edict ordered barbarian grand ministers also to list their names on the covenant.

sentences.zh: 元鼎逾成紀、武川，抵河廣武梁，故時城郭未隳，蘭州地皆杭稻，桃、李、榆柳岑蔚，戶皆唐人，見使者麾蓋，夾道觀。

translations.literal: Yuanding crossed Chengj Wu Chuan; reached river Guangwu ford; former times city walls not yet ruined; Lanzhou lands all paddy rice; peach plum elm willow lush; households all Tang people; seeing envoy's banners canopies; lined roads to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanding crossed Chengj and Wuchuan and reached the Guangwu ford on the river; the city walls of former times were not yet ruined; the lands of Lanzhou were all paddy fields; peach, plum, elm, and willow grew lush; the households were all Tang people; seeing the envoy's banners and canopies they lined the roads to watch.

sentences.zh: 至龍支城，耋老千人拜且泣，問天子安否，言：「頃從軍沒於此，今子孫未忍忘唐服，朝廷尚念之乎？

translations.literal: Reached Longzhi city; thousand aged bowed and wept; asked whether Son of Heaven was well; said: Not long ago followed army perished here; now descendants cannot bear forget Tang dress; does court still remember them?
translations.idiomatic: At Longzhi City a thousand aged men bowed and wept, asking whether the Son of Heaven was well, and said: "Not long ago we followed the army and perished here; now our descendants cannot bear to forget Tang dress—does the court still remember us?

sentences.zh: 兵何日來？」

translations.literal: When will troops come?"
translations.idiomatic: When will the troops come?"

sentences.zh: 言己皆嗚咽。

translations.literal: Having spoken all sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: Having spoken, all sobbed.

sentences.zh: 密問之，豐州人也。

translations.literal: Secretly asked them; were people of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked them privately—they were people of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 過石堡城，崖壁峭豎，道回屈，虜曰鐵刀城。

translations.literal: Passed Shibao fort; cliff walls steep vertical; road winding bent; barbarians called Iron Knife Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Shibao Fort, where cliff walls rose steep and vertical and the road wound and bent, the barbarians called it Iron Knife Fort.

sentences.zh: 右行數十里，土石皆赤，虜曰赤嶺。

translations.literal: Turned right traveled several tens of li; earth stones all red; barbarians called Red Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Turning right and traveling several tens of li, the earth and stones were all red—the barbarians called it Red Ridge.

sentences.zh: 而信安王祎、張守珪所定封石皆仆，獨虜所立石猶存。

translations.literal: Yet Prince Xin'an Yi Zhang Shougui's boundary stones all fallen; only stones barbarians erected still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the boundary stones set by Prince Xin'an Yi and Zhang Shougui had all fallen; only the stones the barbarians erected still remained.

sentences.zh: 赤嶺距長安三千里而贏，蓋隴右故地也。

translations.literal: Red Ridge three thousand li from Chang'an with surplus; was former Longyou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Red Ridge was more than three thousand li from Chang'an—it was the former Longyou territory.

sentences.zh: 曰悶怛盧川，直邏娑川之南百里，臧河所流也。

translations.literal: Called Mondalu River; straight south of Luosuo River hundred li; where Zang River flows.
translations.idiomatic: It was called the Mondalu River, a hundred li due south of the Luosuo River, where the Zang River flows.

sentences.zh: 河之西南，地如砥，原野秀沃，夾河多檉柳。

translations.literal: Southwest of river; land like whetstone; open fields lush fertile; along river many tamarisk willows.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the river the land was level as a whetstone, the open fields lush and fertile, and tamarisk willows grew thick along the river.

sentences.zh: 山多柏，坡皆丘墓，旁作屋，赪塗之，繪白虎，皆虜貴人有戰功者，生衣其皮，死以旌勇，徇死者瘞其旁。

translations.literal: Mountains many cypress; slopes all mounds tombs; beside built houses; red painted them; painted white tigers; all barbarian nobles with battle merit; living wore their skins; dead to display courage; followers who died buried beside.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains had many cypresses; the slopes were all mounds and tombs; houses were built beside them, painted red and decorated with white tigers—all barbarian nobles with battle merit, who in life wore the skins and in death displayed courage; followers who died were buried beside them.

sentences.zh: 度悉結羅嶺，鑿石通車，逆金城公主道也。

translations.literal: Crossed Xijieluo Ridge; chiseled stone to open for carts; against Jincheng Princess's road.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed Xijieluo Ridge, chiseled through the stone to open a road for carts—the road against which Princess Jincheng had traveled.

sentences.zh: 至麋谷，就館。

translations.literal: Reached Migu; took lodging.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Migu and took lodging.

sentences.zh: 臧河之北川，贊普之夏牙也。

translations.literal: North bank of Zang River; tsenpo's summer court.
translations.idiomatic: The north bank of the Zang River was the tsenpo's summer court.

sentences.zh: 周以槍累，率十步植百長槊，中剚大幟為三門，相距皆百步。

translations.literal: Perimeter with spears piled; every ten paces planted hundred long spears; center planted great banners as three gates; each separated hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: The perimeter was piled with spears; every ten paces a hundred long spears were planted; in the center great banners were set as three gates, each a hundred paces apart.

sentences.zh: 甲士持門，巫祝鳥冠虎帶擊豉，凡入者搜索乃進。

translations.literal: Armored soldiers held gates; shamans bird crowns tiger belts struck drums; all who entered searched then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Armored soldiers held the gates; shamans in bird crowns and tiger belts struck drums; all who entered were searched before they advanced.

sentences.zh: 中有高臺，環以寶楯，贊普坐帳中，以黃金飾蛟螭虎豹，身被素褐，結朝霞冒首，佩金鏤劍。

translations.literal: Within was high terrace; ringed with precious shields; tsenpo sat in tent; with gold adorned dragons tigers leopards; body wore plain brown; tied dawn-clouds cap on head; wore gold-inlaid sword.
translations.idiomatic: Within was a high terrace ringed with precious shields; the tsenpo sat in his tent adorned with gold dragons, horned dragons, tigers, and leopards; he wore plain brown, a dawn-clouds cap bound on his head, and a gold-inlaid sword.

sentences.zh: 缽掣逋立於右，宰相列臺下。

translations.literal: Bochebo stood at right; grand counselors arrayed below terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Bochebo stood at his right; the grand counselors were arrayed below the terrace.

sentences.zh: 唐使者始至，給事中論悉答熱來議盟，大享於牙右，飯舉酒行，與華制略等，樂奏《秦王破陣曲》，又奏《涼州》、《胡渭》、《錄要》、雜曲，百伎皆中國人。

translations.literal: When Tang envoys first arrived; attendant Lun Xidare came to discuss alliance; great feast at court right; meal raised wine circulated; roughly equal to Chinese rites; music played Prince of Qin Breaks the Array; also played Liangzhou Huwei Luyao miscellaneous tunes; hundred performers all Chinese people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang envoys first arrived, attendant Lun Xidare came to discuss the alliance; a great feast was held to the right of the court; the meal was served and wine circulated in rites roughly equal to Chinese practice; music played "Prince of Qin Breaks the Array," then "Liangzhou," "Huwei," "Luyao," and miscellaneous tunes—all hundred performers were Chinese.

sentences.zh: 盟壇廣十步，高二尺。

translations.literal: Alliance altar ten paces wide; two chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The alliance altar was ten paces wide and two chi high.

sentences.zh: 使者與虜大臣十餘對位，酋長百餘坐壇下，上設巨榻，缽掣逋升，告盟，一人自旁譯授於下。

translations.literal: Envoys with barbarian grand ministers more than ten faced each other; chieftains hundred plus sat below altar; above set great couch; Bochebo ascended; announced alliance; one person from side translated and transmitted below.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys and more than ten barbarian grand ministers faced each other; a hundred-plus chieftains sat below the altar; a great couch was set above; Bochebo ascended and announced the alliance, while one man at the side translated and transmitted it below.

sentences.zh: 已歃血，缽掣逋不歃。

translations.literal: After blood was tasted; Bochebo did not taste.
translations.idiomatic: After the blood oath had been tasted, Bochebo did not taste it.

sentences.zh: 盟畢，以浮屠重為誓，引郁金水以飲，與使者交慶，乃降。

translations.literal: Alliance complete; took Buddhist monk Zhong as oath witness; drew Yushui to drink; with envoys exchanged congratulations; then descended.
translations.idiomatic: When the alliance was complete, they took the Buddhist monk Zhong as witness to the oath, drew water from the Yushui to drink, exchanged congratulations with the envoys, and then descended.

sentences.zh: 元鼎還，虜元帥尚塔藏館客大夏川，集東方節度諸將百餘，置盟策臺上，遍曉之，且戒各保境，毋相暴犯。

translations.literal: Yuan Ding returned; barbarian commander Shang Tacang lodged guests at Daxia River; gathered eastern circuit generals more than hundred; placed alliance document on platform; informed all; also warned each guard territory, not mutually violently violate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding returned. The barbarian commander Shang Tacang received guests at Daxia River and gathered more than a hundred generals of the eastern circuits. He placed the alliance document on a platform, informed them all, and warned each to guard his own territory and not raid one another.

sentences.zh: 策署。

translations.literal: Document signed.
translations.idiomatic: The document was signed.

sentences.zh: 尚塔藏語元鼎曰：「回鶻小國，我嘗討之，距城三日危破，會國有喪乃還，非我敵也。

translations.literal: Shang Tacang said to Yuan Ding: "Uyghurs small state; I once attacked them; three days from city nearly broken; met state mourning then returned; not my match.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Tacang said to Yuan Ding, "The Uyghurs are a small state. I once campaigned against them and within three days of their city had them on the brink of collapse, but returned when their state fell into mourning. They are no match for us.

sentences.zh: 唐何所畏，乃厚之？」

translations.literal: What does Tang fear, thus treat them generously?"
translations.idiomatic: What does Tang have to fear that it treats them so generously?

sentences.zh: 元鼎曰：「回鶻有功，且如約，未始妄以兵取尺寸地，是以厚之。」

translations.literal: Yuan Ding said: "Uyghurs have merit, and as promised; never rashly took land by arms even a foot's breadth; thus treat generously."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding said, "The Uyghurs have rendered service and kept their agreements. They have never rashly seized so much as a foot of ground by force. That is why Tang treats them generously."

sentences.zh: 塔藏默然。

translations.literal: Tacang fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Tacang said nothing.

sentences.zh: 元鼎逾湟水，至龍泉谷，西北望殺胡川，哥舒翰故壁多在。

translations.literal: Yuan Ding crossed Huangshui; reached Longquan Valley; northwest gazed at Slaughter-Hu River valley; Geshu Han's old ramparts many there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding crossed the Huangshui, reached Longquan Valley, and looking northwest toward Slaughter-Hu River valley saw many of Geshu Han's old fortifications still standing.

sentences.zh: 湟水出蒙谷，抵龍泉與河合。

translations.literal: Huangshui emerges Meng Valley; reaches Longquan and joins river.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangshui rises in Meng Valley, reaches Longquan, and joins the river.

sentences.zh: 河之上流，繇洪濟梁西南行二千里，水益狹，春可涉，秋夏乃勝舟。

translations.literal: River's upper reaches; from Hongji Ford southwest two thousand li; water increasingly narrow; spring can ford; autumn summer only bear boats.
translations.idiomatic: The river's upper course, from Hongji Ford southwest for two thousand li, grows ever narrower: in spring one can wade across, but only in autumn and summer can boats navigate it.

sentences.zh: 其南三百里三山，中高而四下，曰紫山，直大羊同國，古所謂昆侖者也，虜曰悶摩黎山，東距長安五千里，河源其間，流澄緩下，稍合眾流，色赤，行益遠，它水並註則濁，故世舉謂西戎地曰河湟。

translations.literal: South three hundred li three mountains; center high four sides low; called Purple Mountain; faces Great Yangtong state; ancient called Kunlun; barbarians call Munmoli Mountain; east five thousand li from Chang'an; river source between; flows clear slow down; gradually joins many streams; color red; travels farther; other waters together pour then turbid; thus world calls Western Rong lands He-Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li to the south stand three mountains, high in the center and sloping on four sides, called Purple Mountain, facing the Great Yangtong state—the Kunlun of antiquity, which the barbarians call Munmoli Mountain, five thousand li east of Chang'an. The river's source lies among them; its current runs clear and slow, gradually gathering tributaries and turning red. Farther downstream, when other streams pour in together, it grows turbid; hence the world calls the Western Rong lands He-Huang.

sentences.zh: 河源東北直莫賀延磧尾殆五百里，磧廣五十里，北自沙州，西南入吐谷渾浸狹，故號磧尾。

translations.literal: River source northeast straight to Moheyan desert tail nearly five hundred li; desert wide fifty li; north from Shazhou; southwest enters Tuyuhun gradually narrow; thus called desert tail.
translations.idiomatic: From the river's source northeast to the tail of the Moheyan Desert is nearly five hundred li; the desert is fifty li wide, running north from Shazhou and narrowing as it enters Tuyuhun to the southwest—hence the name Desert Tail.

sentences.zh: 隱測其地，蓋劍南之西。

translations.literal: Covertly gauged that land; roughly west of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: By covert reckoning, that country lay roughly west of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 元鼎所經見，大略如此。

translations.literal: What Yuan Ding passed and saw; broadly thus.
translations.idiomatic: What Yuan Ding passed through and observed was broadly as described.

sentences.zh: 虜遣論悉諾息等入謝，天子命左衛大將軍令狐通、太僕少卿杜載答之。

translations.literal: Barbarians sent Lun Xinuoqi and others enter to thank; Son of Heaven ordered Left Guard General Linghu Tong, Grand Stable Vice Minister Du Zai reply.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians sent Lun Xinuoqi and others to present thanks. The Son of Heaven ordered Left Guard General Linghu Tong and Grand Stable Vice Minister Du Zai to respond.

sentences.zh: 是歲，尚綺心兒以兵擊回鶻、党項，小相尚設塔率眾三萬牧馬木蘭梁。

translations.literal: This year Shang Qixin'er with troops attacked Uyghurs, Tangut; junior minister Shang Sheta led host thirty thousand pasturing horses at Mulan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shang Qixin'er attacked the Uyghurs and Tangut with troops, while junior minister Shang Sheta led thirty thousand men to pasture horses at Mulan Ford.

sentences.zh: 比歲，使者獻金盎、銀冶犀、鹿，貢牦牛。

translations.literal: In recent years envoys presented gold bowls, silver-worked rhinoceros, deer; tribute yak.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years envoys presented gold bowls, silver-worked rhinoceros horn, and deer, and offered yaks as tribute.

sentences.zh: 寶歷至大和，再遣使者朝。

translations.literal: From Baoli to Dahe; again sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: From the Baoli through the Dahe reigns, they again sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 五年，維州守將悉怛謀挈城以降，劍南西川節度使李德裕受之，收符章仗鎧，更遣將虞藏儉據之。

translations.literal: Fifth year; Weizhou garrison commander Sidamo led city to surrender; Jiannan West Circuit military commissioner Li Deyu received; collected tallies seals arms armor; again sent general Yu Zangjian hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Weizhou garrison commander Sidamo brought the city over in surrender. Li Deyu, military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit, accepted it, collected the tallies, seals, arms, and armor, and sent General Yu Zangjian to hold the place.

sentences.zh: 州南抵江陽岷山，西北望隴山，一面崖，三涯江，虜號無憂城，為西南要捍。

translations.literal: Prefecture south reaches Jiangyang Min Mountains; northwest gazes Long Mountains; one face cliff; three banks river; barbarians call Carefree City; is southwest key defense.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture abuts the Jiangyang Min Mountains to the south and looks toward the Long Mountains to the northwest; cliffs on one side and rivers on three, the barbarians called it Carefree City—a key bulwark of the southwest.

sentences.zh: 會牛僧孺當國，議還悉怛謀，歸其城。

translations.literal: Met Niu Sengru holding state; discussed return Sidamo; restore its city.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru was then directing the state; the court debated returning Sidamo and restoring the city to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃夷誅無遺種，以怖諸戎。

translations.literal: Tibetans exterminated without remnant seed; to terrify various Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans exterminated them to the last man, to terrify the other frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 自是比五年虜使來，必報。

translations.literal: From this for five years barbarian envoys came; always repaid.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever barbarian envoys came within five years, Tang always repaid them in kind.

sentences.zh: 所貢有玉帶、金皿、獺褐、牦牛尾、霞氈、馬、羊、橐它。

translations.literal: Tribute had jade belt, gold vessels, otter fur, yak tail, cloud felt, horses, sheep, camels.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute included jade belts, gold vessels, otter pelts, yak tails, cloud-pattern felt, horses, sheep, and camels.

sentences.zh: 贊普立幾三十年，病不事，委任大臣，故不能抗中國，邊候晏然。

translations.literal: Tsenpo reigned nearly thirty years; ill did not attend affairs; entrusted grand ministers; thus could not resist China; border posts tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The tsenpo had reigned nearly thirty years. Illness kept him from affairs of state, and he entrusted everything to his grand ministers, so Tibet could not stand against China and the border posts were tranquil.

sentences.zh: 死，以弟達磨嗣。

translations.literal: Died; younger brother Damo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and his younger brother Damo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 達磨嗜酒，好畋獵，喜內，且凶愎少恩，政益亂，

translations.literal: Damo loved wine; loved hunting; loved inner quarters; moreover fierce obstinate little grace; government increasingly chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Damo was addicted to wine, loved hunting and the inner quarters, and was fierce, obstinate, and sparing of mercy; government grew ever more chaotic.

sentences.zh: 遣太子詹事李景儒往使，吐蕃以論集熱來朝，獻玉器羊馬。

translations.literal: Dispatched Crown Prince Household Minister Li Jingru as envoy; Tibet sent Lun Jire to court; presented jade vessels sheep horses.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Crown Prince Household Minister Li Jingru as envoy; Tibet sent Lun Jire to court with jade vessels, sheep, and horses.

sentences.zh: 自是國中地震裂，水泉湧，岷山崩；

translations.literal: From this within state earth quaked split; springs gushed; Min Mountains collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: From then on the land quaked and split within the realm, springs burst forth, and the Min Mountains collapsed;

sentences.zh: 洮水逆流三日，鼠食稼，人饑疫，死者相枕藉。

translations.literal: Tao River flowed backward three days; rats ate crops; people hunger plague; dead piled pillow on pillow.
translations.idiomatic: the Tao River flowed backward for three days, rats devoured the crops, famine and plague struck the people, and the dead lay heaped upon one another.

sentences.zh: 鄯、廓間夜聞鼙鼓聲，人相驚，

translations.literal: Between Shan and Kuo at night heard war drums; people mutually alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Between Shan and Kuo prefectures people heard war drums at night and alarmed one another.

sentences.zh: 贊普死，論贊熱等來告，天子命將作監李璟吊祠。

translations.literal: Tsenpo died; Lun Zanre and others came announce; Son of Heaven ordered Directorate of Works Li Jing mourn and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The tsenpo died. Lun Zanre and others came to announce it, and the Son of Heaven ordered Directorate of Works Commissioner Li Jing to offer mourning and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 無子，以妃綝兄尚延力子乞離胡為贊普，始三歲，妃共治其國。

translations.literal: No son; took consort's clansman brother Shang Yanli's son Qilihu as tsenpo; just three years; consort together governed state.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, so they made Qilihu, son of the consort's clansman Shang Yanli, tsenpo at the age of three, and the consort ruled the state with him.

sentences.zh: 大相結都那見乞離胡不肯拜，曰：「贊普支屬尚多，何至立綝氏子邪？」

translations.literal: Grand minister Jeduna saw Qilihu would not bow; said: "Tsenpo collateral kin still many; how reach install Chen clan child?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand minister Jeduna, seeing that Qilihu would not bow, said, "Collateral lines of the tsenpo are still numerous—why install a child of the Chen clan?

sentences.zh: 哭而出，用事者共殺之。

translations.literal: Wept and went out; those in power together killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and left; those in power together killed him.

sentences.zh: 別將尚恐熱為落門川討擊使，姓末，名農力，「熱」猶中國號「郎」也，譎詭善幻，約三部得萬騎，擊鄯州節度使尚婢婢，略地至渭州，與宰相尚與思羅戰薄寒山。

translations.literal: Vice general Shang Kongje was Luomen River punitive commissioner; surname Mo; name Nongli; "je" like China title "lang"; cunning deceitful good illusion; about three divisions got ten thousand riders; attacked Shanzhou military commissioner Shang Bibi; seized land to Weizhou; with grand counselor Shang Yusiluo fought at Bohen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Vice general Shang Kongje served as punitive commissioner of Luomen River; his surname was Mo and his name Nongli—"je" being the Tibetan equivalent of the Chinese "lang." Cunning and skilled in illusion, he mustered ten thousand horsemen from three divisions, attacked Shanzhou military commissioner Shang Bibi, raided as far as Weizhou, and fought grand counselor Shang Yusiluo at Bohen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 思羅敗走松州，合蘇毗、吐渾、羊同兵八萬保洮河自守，恐熱謂蘇毗等曰：「宰相兄弟殺贊普，天神使我舉義兵誅不道，爾屬乃助逆背國耶？」

translations.literal: Yusiluo defeated fled Songzhou; united Supi, Tuhun, Yangtong troops eighty thousand guard Tao River self-defend; Kongje said to Supi etc.: "Grand counselors brothers killed tsenpo; heaven spirits made me raise righteous army punish unrighteous; your kind yet aid rebellion betray state?"
translations.idiomatic: Yusiluo was defeated and fled to Songzhou. He united eighty thousand troops of the Supi, Tuhun, and Yangtong to hold the Tao River. Kongje said to the Supi and others, "The grand counselor brothers murdered the tsenpo. The spirits of heaven sent me to raise a righteous army and punish the wicked—will you aid rebellion and betray the state?

sentences.zh: 蘇毗等疑而不戰，恐熱麾輕騎涉河，諸部先降，並其眾至十餘萬，禽思羅縊殺之。

translations.literal: Supi etc. doubted and did not fight; Kongje commanded light cavalry cross river; various divisions first surrendered; combined their hosts to more than hundred thousand; captured Yusiluo strangled killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Supi hesitated and would not fight. Kongje led light cavalry across the river; the various divisions surrendered first. Combining their forces he reached more than a hundred thousand men, captured Yusiluo, and strangled him.

sentences.zh: 婢婢，姓沒盧，名贊心牙，羊同國人，世為吐蕃貴相，寬厚，略通書記，不喜仕，贊普強官之。

translations.literal: Bibi; surname Molu; name Zanxinya; Yangtong state person; generations Tibet grand counselor; generous; slightly knew writing records; disliked office; tsenpo forced office on him.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi, surname Molu, name Zanxinya, was a man of the Yangtong state whose family for generations had been grand counselors of Tibet. Generous and with some knowledge of writing, he disliked office, but the tsenpo forced rank upon him.

sentences.zh: 三年，國人以贊普立非是，皆叛去。

translations.literal: Third year; state people because tsenpo installation not right; all rebelled left.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, because the tsenpo's installation was deemed illegitimate, the people of the realm all rebelled and departed.

sentences.zh: 恐熱自號宰相，以兵二十萬擊婢婢，鼓鼙、牛馬、橐它聯千餘里，至鎮西軍，大風雷電，部將震死者十餘人，羊、馬、橐它亦數百。

translations.literal: Kongje self-titled grand counselor; with troops two hundred thousand attacked Bibi; drums cattle horses camels linked thousand-plus li; reached Zhenxi Army; great wind thunder lightning; subordinate generals thunder-killed more than ten; sheep horses camels also several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Kongje styled himself grand counselor and attacked Bibi with two hundred thousand men. Drums, cattle, horses, and camels stretched in a line more than a thousand li to Zhenxi Army. A great storm of wind, thunder, and lightning struck; more than ten subordinate generals were killed by lightning, along with several hundred sheep, horses, and camels.

sentences.zh: 恐熱惡之，按軍不進。

translations.literal: Kongje hated it; held army did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Kongje took it as an ill omen and halted the army without advancing.

sentences.zh: 婢婢聞之，厚幣詒書約，恐熱大喜曰：「婢婢，書生，焉知軍事。

translations.literal: Bibi heard; thick gifts deceptive letter alliance; Kongje greatly pleased said: "Bibi, book man; how know military affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Bibi heard of it and sent rich gifts with a deceptive letter proposing alliance. Kongje was greatly pleased and said, "Bibi is a bookish man—what does he know of war?

sentences.zh: 我為贊普，當以家居宰相處之。」

translations.literal: I become tsenpo; ought treat him as household grand counselor."
translations.idiomatic: When I become tsenpo, I shall keep him at home as my grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 於是退營大夏川。

translations.literal: Then withdrew camp to Daxia River.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew his camp to Daxia River.

sentences.zh: 婢婢遣將厖結心、莽羅薛呂擊恐熱於河州之南，伏兵四萬，結心據山射書極罵，恐熱怒甚，盛兵出鬥。

translations.literal: Bibi sent generals Mangjiexin, Mangluoxuelu attack Kongje south of Hezhou; ambush troops forty thousand; Jiexin held mountain shot letters extreme curses; Kongje anger extreme; massed troops out fought.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi sent generals Mangjiexin and Mangluoxuelu to strike Kongje south of Hezhou with forty thousand men in ambush. Jiexin held the mountain, shot letters of the vilest abuse, and Kongje, enraged, massed his troops and gave battle.

sentences.zh: 結心偽北，恐熱追至數十里，莽羅薛呂以伏兵衷擊，大風雨，河溢，溺死甚眾，恐熱單騎而逃。

translations.literal: Jiexin feigned north; Kongje pursued several tens li; Mangluoxuelu with ambush troops center struck; great wind rain; river overflowed; drowned dead very many; Kongje single horse fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiexin feigned retreat north; Kongje pursued for several tens of li; Mangluoxuelu struck from ambush in the center. A great storm blew, the river overflowed, and very many drowned; Kongje fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 既不得志，尤猜忍殺戮，部將岌藏、豐贊皆降，婢婢厚遇之。

translations.literal: Already not attained ambition; especially suspicious cruel slaughter; subordinate generals Jizang, Fengzan all surrendered; Bibi thickly treated them.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his ambitions, he grew all the more suspicious and cruel in slaughter. Subordinate generals Jizang and Fengzan both surrendered, and Bibi treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 明年，恐熱復攻鄯州，婢婢分兵五道拒守，恐熱保東谷山，堅壁不出。

translations.literal: Next year Kongje again attacked Shanzhou; Bibi divided troops five routes resist guard; Kongje held East Valley Mountain; firm walls did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Kongje again attacked Shanzhou. Bibi divided his forces along five routes to resist him; Kongje held East Valley Mountain and would not come out behind his walls.

sentences.zh: 岌藏繚以重柵，斷汲道，旬日，恐熱走薄寒山，募散卒稍至，得數千人，復戰鹖雞山，再戰南谷，皆大敗。

translations.literal: Jizang entwined with heavy palisades; cut water-draw routes; ten days; Kongje fled Bohen Mountain; recruited scattered soldiers gradually arrived; got several thousand; again fought at Pheasant Mountain; again fought South Valley; all great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Jizang built heavy palisades and cut off the water routes. After ten days Kongje fled to Bohen Mountain, gathered scattered soldiers until he had several thousand, and fought again at Pheasant Mountain and again at South Valley—but was utterly defeated both times.

sentences.zh: 兵拿仍歲不解，

translations.literal: Arms seized; years still not released.
translations.idiomatic: Arms were locked in struggle year after year without respite.

sentences.zh: 婢婢屯兵河源，聞恐熱謀度河，急擊之，為恐熱所敗。

translations.literal: Bibi stationed troops River Source; heard Kongje planned cross river; urgently struck; by Kongje was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi stationed troops at River Source. Hearing that Kongje planned to cross the river, he struck urgently but was defeated by Kongje.

sentences.zh: 婢婢統銳兵扼橋，亦不勝，焚橋而還。

translations.literal: Bibi commanded sharp troops choke bridge; also not victorious; burned bridge and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi led elite troops to hold the bridge but still could not win; he burned the bridge and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 恐熱間出雞頂嶺關，馮硤為梁攻婢婢，至白土嶺，敗其將尚鐸羅榻藏，進戰牦牛硤。

translations.literal: Kongje by path emerged Jiding Ridge pass; bridged gorge attacked Bibi; reached White Earth Ridge; defeated his general Shang Duoluotazang; advanced fought Yak Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Kongje slipped out through Jiding Ridge pass, bridged the gorge, and attacked Bibi. Reaching White Earth Ridge, he defeated Bibi's general Shang Duoluotazang and pressed on to fight at Yak Gorge.

sentences.zh: 婢婢將燭盧鞏力欲負硤自固以困恐熱，大將磨離羆子不從，乃辭疾先歸。

translations.literal: Bibi's general Zhulu Gongli wished bear gorge self-fortify to weary Kongje; great general Moli Bizi did not follow; then pleaded illness first returned.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi's general Zhulu Gongli wished to hold the gorge and wear Kongje down, but great general Moli Bizi would not agree and pleaded illness to return first.

sentences.zh: 羆子急擊恐熱，一戰而死。

translations.literal: Bizi urgently attacked Kongje; one battle died.
translations.idiomatic: Bizi pressed the attack on Kongje and died in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 婢婢糧盡，引眾趨甘州西境，以拓拔懷光居守，恐熱麾下多歸之。

translations.literal: Bibi grain exhausted; led host toward Ganzhou western border; left Tuoba Huaiguang garrison guard; Kongje subordinates many returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi's provisions were exhausted. He led his host toward the western border of Ganzhou, left Tuoba Huaiguang to hold the place, and many of Kongje's followers came over to him.

sentences.zh: 恐熱大略鄯、廓、瓜、肅、伊、西等州，所過捕戮，積屍狼藉，麾下內怨，皆欲圖之。

translations.literal: Kongje broadly raided Shan, Kuo, Gua, Su, Yi, Xi and other prefectures; where passed captured slaughtered; piled corpses scattered; subordinates inward resentment; all wished plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Kongje raided broadly through Shan, Kuo, Gua, Su, Yi, Xi, and other prefectures. Wherever he passed he seized and slaughtered until corpses lay heaped in disorder. Resentment grew within his ranks, and all wished to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 乃揚聲將請唐兵五十萬共定其亂，保渭州，求冊為贊普，奉表歸唐。

translations.literal: Then proclaimed would request Tang troops five hundred thousand together pacify his chaos; held Weizhou; sought investiture as tsenpo; presented memorial return Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed that he would ask Tang for five hundred thousand troops to pacify the turmoil together, held Weizhou, sought investiture as tsenpo, and presented a memorial submitting to Tang.

sentences.zh: 宣宗詔太僕卿陸耽持節慰勞，命涇原、靈武、鳳翔、邠寧、振武等兵迎援。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Grand Stable Minister Lu Dan hold tally comfort; ordered Jingyuan, Lingwu, Fengxiang, Binning, Zhenwu and other troops welcome aid.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Grand Stable Minister Lu Dan to go with credentials to comfort him and commanded troops of Jingyuan, Lingwu, Fengxiang, Binning, Zhenwu, and other circuits to go forth in support.

sentences.zh: 恐熱既至，詔尚書左丞李景讓就問所欲。

translations.literal: Kongje already arrived; edict Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Li Jingrang go inquire desires.
translations.idiomatic: When Kongje had arrived, an edict sent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Li Jingrang to ask what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 恐熱倨誇自大，且求河渭節度使，帝不許。

translations.literal: Kongje haughty boastful self-great; also sought He-Wei military commissioner; emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Kongje was arrogant and boastful and also demanded to be military commissioner of He-Wei; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 還過咸陽橋，咄嘆曰：「我舉大事，覬得濟此河與唐分境。」

translations.literal: Returning passed Xianyang Bridge; clucked sighed: "I raised great affair; hoped could cross this river with Tang divide border."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he passed Xianyang Bridge and sighed, "I raised a great enterprise, hoping to cross this river and divide the border with Tang.

sentences.zh: 於是復趨落門川收散卒，將寇邊，會久雨糧絕，恐熱還奔廓州。

translations.literal: Then again rushed Luomen River gathered scattered soldiers; about to raid border; met long rain grain exhausted; Kongje again fled Kuo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then rushed again to Luomen River to gather scattered soldiers and was about to raid the border, but prolonged rain cut off his provisions, and Kongje fled back to Kuo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是鳳翔節度使李比復清水；

translations.literal: Then Fengxiang military commissioner Li Bi recovered Qingshui;
translations.idiomatic: Then Fengxiang military commissioner Li Bi recovered Qingshui;

sentences.zh: 涇原節度使康季榮復原州，取石門等六關，得人畜幾萬；

translations.literal: Jingyuan military commissioner Kang Jirong recovered Yuanzhou; took Shimen and six other passes; got people livestock nearly ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan military commissioner Kang Jirong recovered Yuanzhou, took Shimen and six other passes, and gained nearly ten thousand people and livestock;

sentences.zh: 靈武節度使李欽取安樂州，詔為威州；

translations.literal: Lingwu military commissioner Li Qin took Anle prefecture; edict made Weizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu military commissioner Li Qin took Anle prefecture, which was issued an edict as Weizhou;

sentences.zh: 邠寧節度使張欽緒復蕭關；

translations.literal: Binning military commissioner Zhang Qinxu recovered Xiaoguan;
translations.idiomatic: Binning military commissioner Zhang Qinxu recovered Xiaoguan;

sentences.zh: 鳳翔收秦州；

translations.literal: Fengxiang recovered Qinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang recovered Qinzhou;

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使鄭涯得扶州。

translations.literal: Shannan West Circuit military commissioner Zheng Ya got Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan West Circuit military commissioner Zheng Ya took Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔兵與吐蕃戰隴州，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: Fengxiang troops with Tibet fought at Longzhou; beheaded heads five hundred ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang troops fought Tibet at Longzhou and took five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河、隴高年千餘見闕下，天子為禦延喜樓，賜冠帶，皆爭解辮易服。

translations.literal: This year He-Long elders more than thousand saw below palace; Son of Heaven for them mounted Yanxi Tower; bestowed caps belts; all vied unbind braids change dress.
translations.idiomatic: That year more than a thousand elders of He-Long came to court. The Son of Heaven mounted Yanxi Tower for them, bestowed caps and belts, and all vied to unbind their braids and change into Chinese dress.

sentences.zh: 因詔差賜四道兵，錄有勞者；

translations.literal: Thereupon edict differentially bestowed four-circuit troops; recorded those with merit;
translations.idiomatic: An edict then differentially rewarded the troops of the four circuits and recorded those who had merit;

sentences.zh: 三州七關地腴衍者，聽民墾藝，貸五歲賦；

translations.literal: Three prefectures seven passes land fertile rich; permitted people reclaim plant; loaned five years tax;
translations.idiomatic: on fertile land in the three prefectures and seven passes the people were permitted to reclaim and plant, with taxes remitted for five years;

sentences.zh: 溫池委度支榷其鹽，以贍邊；

translations.literal: Warm Pool entrusted Revenue Commission monopolize its salt; to support border;
translations.idiomatic: Warm Pool was entrusted to the Revenue Commission to monopolize its salt for border support;

sentences.zh: 四道兵能營田者為給牛種，戍者倍其資餉，再歲一代；

translations.literal: Four-circuit troops able garrison fields given ox seed; garrison soldiers doubled their provisions pay; every two years one rotation;
translations.idiomatic: troops of the four circuits able to open garrison farms were given oxen and seed; garrison soldiers received double provisions, with rotation every two years;

sentences.zh: 商賈往來於邊者，關鎮毋何留；

translations.literal: Merchants traveling at border; pass forts not detain;
translations.idiomatic: merchants traveling to the border were not to be detained at passes;

sentences.zh: 兵欲墾田，與民同。

translations.literal: Soldiers wishing reclaim fields; same as civilians.
translations.idiomatic: and soldiers who wished to reclaim land were treated the same as civilians.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗平薛仁杲，得隴上地；

translations.literal: Initially Taizong pacified Xue Rengao; got Longshang lands;
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, when Taizong pacified Xue Rengao, he gained the lands of Longshang;

sentences.zh: 虜李軌，得涼州；

translations.literal: captured Li Gui; got Liangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: captured Li Gui and gained Liangzhou;

sentences.zh: 破吐谷渾、高昌，開四鎮。

translations.literal: broke Tuyuhun, Gaochang; opened Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: broke Tuyuhun and Gaochang and opened the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 玄宗繼收黃河積石、宛秀等軍，中國無斥候警者幾四十年。

translations.literal: Xuanzong continued recovered Yellow River Jishi, Wanshow and other armies; China no scouts alarm nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong in turn recovered the armies of the Yellow River, Jishi, Wanshow, and others, and China went nearly forty years without scout alarms.

sentences.zh: 輪臺、伊吾屯田，禾菽彌望。

translations.literal: Luntai, Yiwu garrison fields; grain beans filled view.
translations.idiomatic: At Luntai and Yiwu garrison farms, grain and beans stretched as far as the eye could see.

sentences.zh: 開遠門揭候署曰「西極道九千九百里」，示戍人無萬里行也。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan Gate posted scout office: "Western extremity road nine thousand nine hundred li"; showed garrison men no ten-thousand-li march.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaiyuan Gate the scout office posted "Western extremity road: nine thousand nine hundred li," to show garrison men they need not march ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 乾元後，隴右、劍南西山三州七關軍鎮監牧三百所皆失之。

translations.literal: After Qianyuan; Longyou, Jiannan western mountains three prefectures seven passes army forts supervisory pastures three hundred places all lost.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianyuan era, Longyou, the western mountains of Jiannan, the three prefectures, seven passes, and three hundred army forts and supervisory pastures were all lost.

sentences.zh: 憲宗常覽天下圖，見河湟舊封，赫然思經略之，未暇也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong often viewed empire maps; saw He-Huang old domains; vividly thought plan them; no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong often studied the maps of the realm, and seeing the old domains of He-Huang vividly wished to recover them, but had no leisure.

sentences.zh: 至是群臣奏言：「王者建功立業，必有以光表於世者。

translations.literal: At this ministers memorialized: "King who establishes merit and enterprise; must have what brightly displays to world.
translations.idiomatic: At this the ministers memorialized, "A king who establishes merit and enterprise must have something to display his glory to the world.

sentences.zh: 今不勤一卒，血一刃，而河湟自歸，請上天子尊號。」

translations.literal: Now not mobilizing one soldier; blood one blade; yet He-Huang of themselves returned; request elevate Son of Heaven honorific."
translations.idiomatic: Now without mobilizing a single soldier or drawing a single blade, He-Huang has returned of itself—we beg to elevate the Son of Heaven's honorific title.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「憲宗嘗念河、湟，業未就而殂落。

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Xianzong once thought of He, Huang; enterprise not completed then died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Xianzong once yearned for He and Huang, but died before the work was done.

sentences.zh: 今當述祖宗之烈，其議上順、憲二廟謚號，誇顯後世。」

translations.literal: Now ought narrate ancestors' brilliance; discuss elevating Shun, Xian two temples posthumous titles; boast display later generations."
translations.idiomatic: Now we should recount the brilliance of our ancestors. Let the court discuss elevating the posthumous titles of the Shun and Xian temple shrines, to display our glory to later generations."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「朕姑息民，其山外諸州，須後經營之。」

translations.literal: Again edict: "I spare people; those beyond-mountain prefectures; must afterward manage."
translations.idiomatic: He also issued an edict: "I wish to ease the burden on the people; the prefectures beyond the mountains must be brought under control in due course."

translations.literal: (close of edict)
translations.idiomatic: (close of edict)

sentences.zh: 明年，沙州首領張義潮奉瓜、沙、伊、肅、甘等十一州地圖以獻。

translations.literal: Next year Shazhou leader Zhang Yichao presented Gua, Sha, Yi, Su, Gan and eleven prefectures territory maps as offering.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shazhou leader Zhang Yichao presented maps of eleven prefectures including Gua, Sha, Yi, Su, and Gan.

sentences.zh: 始，義潮陰結豪英歸唐，一日，眾擐甲噪州門，漢人皆助之，虜守者驚走，遂攝州事。

translations.literal: Initially Yichao secretly joined heroes return Tang; one day; host donned armor clamored prefecture gate; Han people all aided; barbarian garrison startled fled; then assumed prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yichao secretly rallied bold men to return to Tang. One day the crowd donned armor and clamored at the prefectural gate; Han people all aided them; the barbarian garrison fled in alarm, and he then took charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 繕甲兵，耕且戰，悉復余州。

translations.literal: Repaired armor weapons; farmed and fought; all recovered remaining prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired arms and armor, farmed while fighting, and recovered all the remaining prefectures.

sentences.zh: 以部校十輩皆操挺，內表其中，東北走天德城，防禦使李丕以聞。

translations.literal: Sent ten company officers all grasping clubs; memorial inside; northeast ran to Tiande city; defense commissioner Li Pi reported.
translations.idiomatic: He sent ten company officers, each bearing a club with the memorial hidden within, who ran northeast to Tiande city; defense commissioner Li Pi reported it to court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其忠，命使者賫詔收慰，擢義潮沙州防禦使，俄號歸義軍，遂為節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor praised his loyalty; ordered envoy carry edict accept comfort; promoted Yichao Shazhou defense commissioner; soon titled Guiyi Army; then became military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty, sent an envoy with an edict to accept and comfort him, promoted Yichao to defense commissioner of Shazhou, soon styled his force the Guiyi Army, and made him military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其後河、渭州虜將尚延心以國破亡，亦獻款。

translations.literal: Afterward He, Wei prefecture barbarian general Shang Yanxin because state broken perished; also submitted allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the barbarian general Shang Yanxin of He and Wei prefectures, seeing the state broken and ruined, also submitted his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史高駢誘降延心及渾末部萬帳，遂收二州，拜延心武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Qinzhou prefect Gao Pian induced surrender Yanxin and Hunmo division ten thousand tents; then recovered two prefectures; enfeoffed Yanxin Martial Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou prefect Gao Pian induced Yanxin and ten thousand tents of the Hunmo division to surrender, recovered the two prefectures, and enfeoffed Yanxin as Martial Guard general.

sentences.zh: 駢收鳳林關，以延心為河、渭等州都遊弈使，

translations.literal: Pian recovered Fenglin Pass; made Yanxin He, Wei and other prefectures overall patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pian recovered Fenglin Pass and appointed Yanxin overall patrol commissioner of He, Wei, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 義潮奉涼州來歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Yichao presented Liangzhou and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhang Yichao offered Liangzhou and came over to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 七年，北庭回鶻仆固俊擊取西州，收諸部。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Beiting Uyghur Pugu Jun attacked and took Xizhou, gathering the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Pugu Jun of the Beiting Uyghurs seized Xizhou and brought the tribes under his sway.

sentences.zh: 鄯州城使張季颙與尚恐熱戰，破之，收器鎧以獻。

translations.literal: Shanzhou garrison commander Zhang Jiying fought Shang Kongre, defeated him, and collected weapons and armor to present.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiying, garrison commander of Shanzhou, defeated Shang Kongre and sent captured arms and armor to court.

sentences.zh: 吐番餘眾犯邠、寧，節度使薛弘宗卻之。

translations.literal: Tibetan remnant forces raided Bin and Ning; military governor Xue Hongzong drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan remnants attacked Bin and Ning prefectures; Xue Hongzong repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 會仆固俊與吐蕃大戰，斬恐熱首，傳京師。

translations.literal: Just then Pugu Jun fought a great battle with Tibet, beheaded Kongre, and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Jun then fought a major engagement with the Tibetans, killed Kongre, and forwarded his head to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 八年，義潮入朝，為右神武統軍，賜第及田，命族子淮深守歸義。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Yichao came to court, was made commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, granted a mansion and fields, and his clansman Huai Shen was ordered to guard Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Zhang Yichao attended court, was appointed commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, given a residence and farmland, and his kinsman Huai Shen was left to hold Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 沙州以長史曹義金領州務，遂授歸義節度使。

translations.literal: Shazhou had Chief Administrator Cao Yijin direct prefectural affairs; he was then appointed military governor of Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yijin as chief administrator ran Shazhou and was made military governor of Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 後中原多故，王命不及，甘州為回鶻所並，歸義諸城多沒。

translations.literal: Later the central plain was troubled by many events and imperial orders could not reach them; Ganzhou was annexed by the Uyghurs and most cities of Guiyi were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later turmoil in the heartland cut off imperial authority; Ganzhou fell to the Uyghurs and most of the Guiyi circuit was lost.

sentences.zh: 渾末，亦曰嗢末，吐蕃奴部也。

translations.literal: Hunmo, also called Wamo, was a slave tribe of Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunmo, also known as the Wamo, were a servile people under Tibet.

sentences.zh: 虜法，出師必發豪室，皆以奴從，平居散處耕牧。

translations.literal: By barbarian custom, when troops marched out great houses were mustered and all went with slaves; in peace they were scattered farming and herding.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan law required great households to march with their slaves whenever armies took the field; in peacetime they farmed and grazed livestock in scattered settlements.

sentences.zh: 及恐熱亂，無所歸，共相嘯合數千人，以嗢末自號，居甘、肅、瓜、沙、河、渭、岷、廓、疊、宕間，其近蕃牙者最勇，而馬尤良云。

translations.literal: When Kongre's rebellion broke out they had nowhere to go; several thousand banded together in a rally, styled themselves Wamo, and dwelt between Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, He, Wei, Min, Kuo, Die, and Dang; those nearest the Tibetan court were fiercest, and their horses were especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: When Kongre's revolt left them homeless, several thousand united under the name Wamo and ranged across the northwestern marches from Ganzhou to Dangzhou; those closest to the Tibetan seat were the boldest fighters and their horses were renowned.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唐興，四夷有弗率者，皆利兵移之，蹙其牙，犁其廷而後已。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When Tang rose, any of the four barbarians who would not submit was met with sharp weapons and moved upon, their lairs pressed and their courts plowed up before it ended.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: At the founding of Tang, any refractory tribe among the four quarters was met with armed force—its strongholds cornered and its court uprooted before peace returned.

sentences.zh: 惟吐蕃、回鶻號強雄，為中國患最久。

translations.literal: Only Tibet and the Uyghurs were called mighty and heroic, plaguing China longest.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tibet and the Uyghurs ranked as the great powers, and they troubled China the longest.

sentences.zh: 贊普遂盡盜河湟，薄王畿為東境，犯京師，掠近輔，殘馘華人。

translations.literal: The Zanpu then stole all of the Huang and Huangshui valleys, pressed the royal domain as his eastern border, violated the capital, plundered the near suburbs, and slaughtered Chinese people.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan kings seized the whole Hehuang region, made the Tang heartland their eastern frontier, struck at Chang'an, ravaged the capital's outskirts, and massacred Chinese subjects.

sentences.zh: 謀夫虓帥，圜視共計，卒不得要領。

translations.literal: Strategists and fierce commanders looked about and plotted together, yet in the end could not grasp the essential point.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors and generals debated in circles yet never found a decisive answer.

sentences.zh: 晚節二姓自亡，而唐亦衰焉。

translations.literal: In the late period both houses perished of themselves, and Tang also declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the end both dynasties destroyed themselves—and Tang declined with them.

sentences.zh: 夫外撫內寧，惟聖人不讓。

translations.literal: To pacify the outer and secure the inner—only the sage does not yield this.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying outsiders while securing the realm within is a task only the sage fully masters.

sentences.zh: 玄宗有逸德，而拓地太大，務遠功，忽近虞，逆賊一奮，中原封裂，訖二百年不得復完，而至陵夷。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had dissolute virtue, yet expanded territory too greatly, sought distant achievements and neglected nearby warnings; when the rebel flared once, the central plain was riven, and for two hundred years could not be made whole again, until decline set in.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong indulged his pleasures yet pushed the frontier too far, chasing distant glory while ignoring threats at hand; one rebel uprising split the empire, and for two centuries the heartland never fully healed—until Tang slid into decay.

sentences.zh: 然則內先自治，釋四夷為外懼，守成之良資也。

translations.literal: Thus to govern the interior first and treat the four barbarians as external anxieties is the fine capital of preserving what has been won.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson is plain: put internal order first, keep the four quarters at arm's length, and you have the true foundation of a lasting realm.
